requirements:
一、数据类型定义需求
1. 系统需要定义两种专用结构化数据，分别是传感器采集数据 SensorData、制动控制信号 BrakeSignal。
2. 系统需要独立封装全局数据字典包 DataDictionary，对外公开全部数据类型定义，支持系统内所有组件引用调用。
二、数据存储传输容量需求
3. 单帧传感器数据 SensorData，固定占用存储空间与传输带宽大小为 8 字节。
4. 单帧制动信号 BrakeSignal，固定占用存储空间与传输带宽大小为 8 字节。

一、模块划分与依赖需求

1. 系统需单独设计制动硬件组件包 Brake，包内定义制动相关硬件设备，对外公开可引用。
2. Brake 模块必须引入外部依赖包，分别为全局数据字典 DataDictionary、底层基础设施 Infrastructure、设备属性规范 SEI，依赖包内定义的数据、总线、属性参数可在本模块直接调用。

二、制动硬件设备基础定义需求

1. 系统存在基础制动硬件设备 SimpleBrake，该设备属于硬件 device 类型组件。
2. SimpleBrake 设备需具备三类外部交互接口：
第一类为数据输入端口 dataIn，端口输入数据类型固定为 DataDictionary 包内定义的制动信号 BrakeSignal，用于接收外部下发的制动指令数据。
第二类为总线接入接口 busIn，设备需要占用基础设施包中 canBus 总线的 i 实例通道，实现总线通信交互。
第三类为供电接入接口 powerIn，设备需要占用基础设施包通用供电总线 power.generic，获取设备工作电源。
3. 设备内部定义数据流向 brakeFlow，该数据流终点绑定 dataIn 输入端口，代表制动信号从外部端口流入制动设备的完整数据通路。

三、制动设备实现层性能与硬件约束需求

1. SimpleBrake 设备存在专用实现版本 SimpleBrake.i，所有设备硬件约束、性能指标统一在实现层配置。
2. 数据流时延约束：brakeFlow 这条制动信号输入数据流，信号传输处理总时延必须控制在 3 毫秒至 5 毫秒区间内。
3. 设备物理重量约束：遵循 SEI 规范定义的重量限值属性，整套 SimpleBrake 制动硬件总重量不得超过 1.0 千克。
4. 供电功耗约束：针对 powerIn 供电接口，设备运行功耗预算上限为 4.0 瓦，设备工作全程功耗不能超出该限值。

一、模块依赖与架构划分需求

1. 系统需单独搭建底层基础设施包 Infrastructure，统一管理通信总线、供电总线、电源源组件，包内内容对外公开供其他业务模块引用。
2. Infrastructure 包需要引入 SEI 标准化属性规范集，所有总线、电源相关硬件性能、功耗指标均采用 SEI 定义的属性进行配置管控。

二、车载通信总线定义需求

1. 系统需要实现两类专用通信总线组件，分别为 CanBus 总线、Bus1553 总线，两类总线基础参数配置保持一致。
2. 总线单包传输数据长度约束：CanBus、Bus1553 总线单次传输数据包固定大小为 8 字节。
3. 总线带宽分配需求：遵循 SEI 带宽预算属性，两条总线分配可用带宽预算上限为 512.0 千字节每秒；总线硬件物理最大承载带宽容量为 768.0 千字节每秒。
4. 两类总线均需提供独立实现实例 CanBus.i、Bus1553.i，预留后续总线底层参数拓展配置空间。

三、供电总线分层定义需求

1. 系统单独定义通用供电总线 power，用于全系统所有用电硬件设备的供电资源接入。
2. 供电总线提供通用实例 power.generic，所有设备统一引用该实例获取供电通道，统一供电资源接口标准。

四、电源供电源组件功能需求

1. 系统需要设计供电源系统组件 PowerSource，作为整车统一供电输出单元。
2. PowerSource 组件对外提供供电总线输出接口 powerOut，接口绑定通用供电总线实例 power.generic，向外输出电能。
3. 电源输出功率约束：依据 SEI 供电功率属性，powerOut 供电接口最大输出供电功率为 10.0 瓦。
4. PowerSource 组件配套独立实现实例 PowerSource.i，支持后续补充电源相关硬件、电气性能参数。

一、模块依赖与架构划分需求

1. 系统需独立设计控制器业务包 Controller，包内定义整车控制核心组件，内容对外公开供其他模块调用。
2. Controller 包必须引入三类外部依赖包，分别为全局数据字典 DataDictionary、底层基础设施 Infrastructure、标准化硬件属性规范 SEI，以此引用统一数据结构、底层总线资源、硬件约束参数。

二、控制器核心组件外部接口需求

1. 系统需要实现核心控制组件 SimpleController，组件类型为 system，承担信号采集、逻辑运算、制动指令下发的控制功能。
2. 组件输入总线接口 busIn：需要占用基础设施包 Bus1553 总线实例 bus1553.i，通过该总线接收外部传输的传感器原始数据。
3. 组件数据输入端口 dataIn：输入数据类型为 DataDictionary 包内 SensorData 传感器数据，用于接收外部上传的传感采集信息。
4. 组件输出总线接口 busOut：需要占用基础设施包 CanBus 总线实例 canBus.i，通过该总线向外发送制动控制指令。
5. 组件数据输出端口 dataOut：输出数据类型为 DataDictionary 包内 BrakeSignal 制动信号，用于下发经过控制器运算后的制动指令。
6. 组件供电接入接口 powerIn：需要接入基础设施通用供电总线 power.generic，为控制器硬件提供工作电源。

三、控制器内部数据流需求

1. 组件内部定义完整业务数据流 controllerFlow，数据通路逻辑为外部传感器输入 dataIn 经过控制器内部运算处理后，从 dataOut 端口输出制动指令。

四、故障安全与错误管理需求（EMV2 错误模型）

1. 控制器组件必须搭载 EMV2 错误建模规范，引用通用故障库 ErrorLibrary，采用 FailStop 停机失效故障行为模型。
2. 故障传播通道定义需求
输入故障通道 datain：允许接收两类外部输入故障，分别为服务缺失故障 ServiceOmission、数值异常故障 ValueError；数据流 f1 作为输入故障接收端，捕获输入端口产生的两类故障。
输出故障通道 dataout：可向外传播两类自身故障，分别为服务缺失故障 ServiceOmission、数值异常故障 ValueError；数据流 f2 作为输出故障源头，向外发送控制器自身产生的两类故障。
3. 组件故障状态切换需求
控制器正常工作状态为 Operational 运行态；一旦触发服务缺失故障事件 serviceommission、数值异常故障事件 valueerror，组件立即切换至 FailStop 停机失效状态，停止全部控制输出。

五、控制器硬件性能与物理约束需求

1. SimpleController 配套独立实现实例 SimpleController.i，所有时延、重量、功耗量化约束统一配置在实现层。
2. 数据流时延约束：controllerFlow 完整信号处理通路，从接收传感器数据到输出制动指令总时延范围为 3 毫秒至 5 毫秒。
3. 硬件重量约束：遵循 SEI 重量规范，整套 SimpleController 控制器硬件总重量上限为 1.2 千克。
4. 供电功耗约束：针对 powerIn 供电接口，控制器运行功耗预算最大值为 4.0 瓦，工作功耗不可超出该限值。

一、顶层系统模块依赖与架构划分需求

1. 系统顶层业务包命名为 SCS，对外公开顶层整车控制系统定义，作为全系统集成根节点。
2. SCS 包需引入外部依赖组件包，包含 SimpleSensor 传感器包、Controller 控制器包、Infrastructure 底层基础设施包、Brake 制动执行机构包，用于集成所有底层硬件、控制单元、执行单元。
3. 顶层系统分为基础声明与实现两层，HighLevelSCS 为顶层系统基础定义，所有子组件实例、连接关系、端到端数据流、绑定规则、时延约束全部配置在 HighLevelSCS.i 实现实例中。

二、系统子组件集成部署需求

1. 顶层系统内部需要实例化全部功能硬件与底层资源，共六类子组件：
第一，传感硬件实例 sensor1，设备类型引用 SimpleSensor 包 SimpleSensor.i 传感器实现；
第二，核心控制单元实例 controller1，系统类型引用 Controller 包 SimpleController.i 控制器实现；
第三，制动执行机构实例 brake1，设备类型引用 Brake 包 SimpleBrake.i 制动设备实现；
第四，CAN 通信总线实例 canBus，总线类型引用 Infrastructure 包 CanBus.i，额外约束该总线传输时延区间 13 毫秒至 15 毫秒；
第五，1553 通信总线实例 bus1553，总线类型引用 Infrastructure 包 Bus1553.i，固定总线时延为 7 毫秒；
第六，集中供电源实例 powerSource，系统类型引用 Infrastructure 包 PowerSource.i 电源实现；
第七，通用供电总线实例 power，总线类型引用 Infrastructure 包 power.generic 通用供电通道。

三、组件端口数据连接需求

1. 端口连接 c1：传感器 sensor1 的数据输出端口 dataOut，直连控制器 controller1 的数据输入端口 dataIn，实现传感数据向控制器单向传输。
2. 端口连接 c2：控制器 controller1 的数据输出端口 dataOut，直连制动设备 brake1 的数据输入端口 dataIn，实现控制器制动指令向制动执行机构单向下发。
3. 端口连接统一时延约束：c1、c2 两条数据端口链路，数据传输时延范围 15 毫秒至 25 毫秒。
4. 端口链路总线绑定规则：c1 传感数据链路物理绑定至 bus1553 总线；c2 制动指令链路物理绑定至 canBus 总线，明确两条数据流对应的底层物理传输总线。

四、硬件总线资源接入连接需求

1. 总线连接 bus1：传感器 sensor1 的总线输出接口 busOut 双向接入 bus1553 总线，传感器通过 1553 总线对外发送传感数据。
2. 总线连接 bus2：控制器 controller1 的总线输入接口 busIn 双向接入 bus1553 总线，控制器通过 1553 总线接收传感器上传数据。
3. 总线连接 bus3：控制器 controller1 的总线输出接口 busOut 双向接入 canBus 总线，控制器通过 CAN 总线下发制动控制指令。
4. 总线连接 bus4：制动设备 brake1 的总线输入接口 busIn 双向接入 canBus 总线，制动设备通过 CAN 总线接收控制器下发的制动信号。
5. 供电总线连接 bus5、bus6、bus7：通用供电总线 power 分别双向接入传感器 sensor1、制动设备 brake1、控制器 controller1 的供电输入接口 powerIn，所有用电硬件统一由集中供电总线供电。

五、全链路端到端数据流需求

1. 系统定义完整端到端业务数据流 ete1，完整数据流转路径为：传感器内部传感数据流 sensorFlow，经过端口连接 c1 传输至控制器，经控制器内部控制数据流 controllerFlow 处理后，通过端口连接 c2 传输至制动设备，最终流入制动设备内部制动数据流 brakeFlow。
2. 端到端全链路时延约束：从传感器采集数据到制动机构接收指令的完整流程总时延区间为 30 毫秒至 40 毫秒。

一、模块依赖与架构划分需求

1. 系统单独创建传感器业务包 SimpleSensor，包内定义传感采集硬件设备，包内内容对外公开供顶层系统集成调用。
2. SimpleSensor 包需要引入三类外部依赖包，分别为全局数据字典 DataDictionary、底层基础设施 Infrastructure、标准化硬件属性规范 SEI，以此引用统一数据结构、底层总线供电资源、硬件量化约束参数。

二、传感硬件设备外部接口需求

1. 系统需要实现传感采集硬件设备 SimpleSensor，组件类型为 device，负责采集外部传感数据并向外发送。
2. 设备数据输出端口 dataOut：输出数据类型固定为 DataDictionary 包内定义的 SensorData 传感器数据，用于向外传输采集完成的传感信息。
3. 设备总线输出接口 busOut：需要占用基础设施包 Bus1553 总线实例 bus1553.i，依靠该总线完成传感数据对外传输。
4. 设备供电接入接口 powerIn：接入基础设施通用供电总线 power.generic，为传感器硬件提供工作电力。

三、传感器内部数据流需求

1. 设备内部定义传感输出数据流 sensorFlow，该数据流作为数据源头绑定 dataOut 输出端口，代表传感器采集生成数据并向外输出的数据通路。

四、传感器运行调度与性能时延需求

1. SimpleSensor 配套独立实现实例 SimpleSensor.i，设备调度周期、时延、重量、功耗全部量化约束配置在实现层。
2. 调度运行模式约束：传感器采用周期式调度协议 dispatch\_protocol，周期性采集、输出传感数据。
3. 采集输出周期约束：传感器数据采集发送固定周期为 50 毫秒，每 50ms 完成一次传感数据生成与发送。
4. 内部数据流时延约束：sensorFlow 传感输出数据流从数据生成到端口输出处理时延区间为 3 毫秒至 5 毫秒。

五、传感器硬件物理与电气约束需求

1. 硬件重量约束：遵循 SEI 标准化属性规范，整套 SimpleSensor 传感硬件总重量上限为 0.2 千克。
2. 供电功耗约束：针对 powerIn 供电接口，传感器正常运行功耗预算最大值为 4.0 瓦，设备工作功耗不得超出该限值。

系统需构建独立的公共数据模型基础模块，该模块为全系统公共依赖组件，自身不依赖任何业务功能模块，面向系统内所有具备跨组件数据交互需求的功能单元提供统一的数据类型定义服务，从底层规范全系统交互数据格式标准，消除跨组件数据解析不兼容风险。

公共数据模型模块内需定义两类标准化交互数据类型，第一类为传感器数据类型SensorData，该类型单实例数据大小固定为2千字节，所有涉及传感器采集数据收发的组件交互接口，必须采用该数据类型作为交互载荷的统一格式，严禁各组件私自定义异构的传感器数据交互格式；第二类为执行控制指令数据类型actuatecmd，该类型单实例数据大小固定为100字节，所有涉及执行机构控制指令收发的组件交互接口，必须采用该数据类型作为交互载荷的统一格式，严禁各组件私自定义异构的控制指令交互格式。

系统核心业务数据流围绕两类标准化数据构建，其中SensorData类型数据流转覆盖传感器数据采集、数据传输、数据处理、决策计算类功能组件，actuatecmd类型数据流转覆盖决策计算、指令传输、执行驱动类功能组件；两类数据在全链路跨组件传递过程中，需严格遵循定义的数据大小与格式要求，不得出现非授权的格式转换、长度裁剪或扩充操作，保障全链路数据解析一致性。

传感器控制系统集成包IntegratedSCS的构建需依赖外部通用软件构件包SoftwareParts与通用物理构件包PhysicalParts，集成过程中需直接复用两个依赖包内的成熟通用构件，不得在集成包内重复定义已在依赖包中声明的软件、硬件通用构件。
顶层传感器控制系统SCS为传感器控制类系统的通用模板，其单层架构实现singletier0需集成四类一级子构件，分别为核心控制子系统ControlSystem、第一路传感器设备sensor1、第二路传感器设备sensor2、执行器设备actuator，不得在顶层系统与上述子构件之间增设额外的中间封装层级。
核心控制子系统ControlSystem为顶层传感器控制系统的核心运算控制单元，其单层架构实现singletier0需划分为软件、硬件两个独立子构件域，软件域需实例化SoftwareParts包内定义的DigitalControl数字控制软件构件，承担信号处理、控制运算、指令生成的核心软件功能；硬件域需实例化PhysicalParts包内定义的main_board主板硬件构件，承担运算资源供给、软件运行承载、外设信号转接的核心硬件功能；数字控制软件构件需与主板硬件构件完成部署绑定，确保软件可在对应硬件平台上正常加载运行。
当前单层架构定义阶段未明确各子构件的对外接口形式、交互协议，未定义子构件间的数据流连接路径与数据交互规则，未明确各功能任务的调度策略、周期、优先级以及数据传输、功能执行的时延约束。上述内容需在后续构件细化设计阶段补充明确，具体需覆盖两路传感器到核心控制子系统的采样数据传输接口规范、核心控制子系统到执行器的控制指令传输接口规范，对应的数据格式、传输带宽、传输时延要求，以及传感器采样、控制运算、执行器驱动全链路的任务调度规则、最坏执行时间、端到端控制时延约束，保障系统功能与性能满足设计目标。

系统需构建公共物理部件定义包PhysicalParts，包内所有构件定义对外公共可见，可被上层系统设计复用，作为系统物理架构、硬件资源建模的基础元素集合。

包内需定义五类基础构件模型，分别为powerpc类型处理器构件，用于表征PowerPC架构的核心运算处理硬件单元；CANbus类型总线构件，用于表征CAN类总线通信传输硬件单元；main_memory类型主存构件，用于表征板载主存储硬件单元；main_board类型主板系统构件，用于表征承载板载硬件集成的系统级板卡单元；Power抽象构件，用于表征供电类资源的抽象实体，支撑后续供电链路、供电属性的扩展建模。

main_board主板构件需提供single构型的实现版本，该实现为单处理器单板架构，模块依赖关系明确，实现内必须集成三个硬件子构件，分别为1个powerpc类型的处理器实例，实例标识为cpu；1个main_memory类型的主存实例，实例标识为ram；1个CANbus类型的总线实例，实例标识为canbus。三个子构件为该构型主板的必备组成部分，主板正常运行依赖三个子构件的无故障工作。

接口适配需求方面，该单板构型下的各硬件子构件需具备匹配的互联接口支撑板内集成，处理器需提供适配主存的存储访问接口、适配CAN总线的总线接入接口；主存需提供适配处理器访问时序的存储服务接口；CAN总线需提供适配板内器件接入、板外设备互联的总线接入接口，为硬件间的物理连接、数据交互提供接口支撑。

数据流约束方面，该单板架构下的板内数据交互需依托硬件互联链路完成，处理器从主存读取运算指令、待处理数据，以及处理器向主存写入运算结果、暂存数据的双向数据流，需通过板内存储互联通路传输；处理器与板外节点之间的交互数据流，需通过CAN总线构建的通信链路传输，所有硬件链路需保障端到端通路的连通性。

调度与资源支撑约束方面，该单板硬件架构需为上层功能软件运行提供底层硬件资源底座，powerpc处理器需为上层软件任务的调度、执行提供运算算力载体；主存需为处理器运行过程中的指令加载、数据缓存提供存储空间支撑，访问时序需适配处理器的运算节奏，避免产生不必要的运算等待；CAN总线需为板间数据交互提供通信链路支撑，保障上层跨节点通信数据的可传输性。

本系统为数字控制系统，采用tier1层级架构落地实现，系统顶层按功能边界划分为两个一级进程组件，分别为IO进程、指令进程，两个进程协同支撑全系统数字控制功能运行。全系统软件构件依赖独立的DataModel数据包提供统一的数据类型规范，所有跨组件交互传输的数据结构必须引用该数据包内的定义，严禁各组件自行定义跨链路传输的数据格式。

IO进程采用impl版本实现，进程内部划分为三个二级线程组件，分别为传感器采样线程、模式切换线程、执行器输出线程。指令进程采用impl版本实现，进程内部划分为三个二级线程组件，分别为滤波应用线程、导控线程、控制应用线程。其中模式切换线程与导控线程为进程内部功能线程，暂未定义对外交互接口，仅支撑进程内部逻辑运行，不直接参与核心控制闭环的跨线程数据交互。

参与核心控制闭环的各线程需按规范配置标准化数据交互端口。传感器采样线程需配置一个输入数据端口、一个输出数据端口，输入端口用于接收符合DataModel中SensorData类型定义的原始传感数据，输出端口用于对外输出符合SensorData类型定义的传感数据，作为滤波环节的输入。执行器输出线程需配置一个输入数据端口、一个输出数据端口，输入端口用于接收符合DataModel中actuatecmd类型定义的控制指令数据，输出端口用于对外输出符合actuatecmd类型定义的执行器驱动指令，对接底层执行器设备。滤波应用线程需配置一个输入数据端口、一个输出数据端口，输入端口用于接收符合SensorData类型定义的传感采样数据，输出端口用于对外输出符合SensorData类型定义的滤波后传感数据，作为控制计算环节的输入。控制应用线程需配置一个输入数据端口、一个输出数据端口，输入端口用于接收符合SensorData类型定义的滤波后传感数据，输出端口用于对外输出符合actuatecmd类型定义的控制指令，传输至执行输出环节。

系统核心控制业务需形成闭环数据流转链路，数据传输路径需遵循以下逻辑，传感器采样线程从外部获取原始SensorData类型传感数据，经采样处理后将传感数据传输至滤波应用线程；滤波应用线程对接收到的传感数据完成滤波处理后，将滤波后的SensorData类型传感数据传输至控制应用线程；控制应用线程基于输入的滤波传感数据完成控制计算，生成actuatecmd类型的控制指令，将控制指令传输至执行器输出线程；执行器输出线程对接收到的控制指令完成输出处理后，将最终actuatecmd类型驱动指令传输至底层执行器，完成单轮控制闭环的数据流转。

核心控制闭环内的所有功能线程均采用固定周期调度机制，统一调度周期为20ms，各线程需满足对应的资源配置与执行时间约束。传感器采样线程的栈内存配置不得小于10KB，每次周期激活后的计算执行时间需严格控制在10ms至12ms范围内，不得超出该时间边界。执行器输出线程的栈内存配置不得小于10KB，每次周期激活后的计算执行时间需严格控制在8ms至10ms范围内，不得超出该时间边界。滤波应用线程的栈内存配置不得小于25KB，需预留不小于250KB的专用数据存储空间用于日志记录，每次周期激活后的计算执行时间需严格控制在5ms至7ms范围内，不得超出该时间边界。控制应用线程的栈内存配置不得小于25KB，需预留不小于50KB的专用数据存储空间用于保存控制状态数据，每次周期激活后的计算执行时间需严格控制在2ms至6ms范围内，不得超出该时间边界。IO进程内的模式切换线程、指令进程内的导控线程暂未明确资源配置、调度参数与执行时间约束，需待具体功能定义明确后补充对应要求。

热源功能模块封装于heat_source公共包内，包级依赖关系明确为引入isoletteDataModel恒温箱通用数据模型包，复用该包内定义的标准化业务数据类型，确保跨组件数据交互过程中的类型一致性。模块内定义抽象设备类型heat_source_dev描述热源硬件的对外交互与流属性，配套定义可实例化的设备实现heat_source_dev.impl作为系统热输出执行端的实体单元，纳入整体系统的硬件组件架构。

热源设备对外仅配置唯一的数据输入端口，端口标识为heat_control，端口传输的数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel包中定义的heat_control数据类型，端口方向为输入，专门用于接收系统其他组件下发的热源控制数据。设备不额外配置其他数据、事件或控制类对外交互端口，所有针对热源设备的控制操作均需通过该输入端口完成，不支持其他路径的控制接入。

热源设备内部定义唯一的流汇路径heat_control_flow，该流路径的起点为设备对外的heat_control输入端口，终点为设备内部的热输出执行单元，所有流入heat_control端口的控制数据需沿该固定路径完整、无篡改传输至执行端。设备内部不设置数据流分支路径，也不配置对外的数据流出端口，不存在数据转发、数据上报类的对外数据流，热源设备仅作为热源控制数据流的终端接收节点，不承担数据中转或数据上传功能。

热源设备实现heat_source_dev.impl未定义内部子组件结构，设备的指令接收、解析与热输出执行全流程依托设备自身硬件运行时序完成调度，不依赖其他内部子单元的协同调度。流路径上的控制数据传输需保证顺序一致性，不得出现指令乱序、数据丢失的情况，由于当前模型未定义量化时延指标，设备实现阶段需明确控制指令沿heat_control_flow路径传输的时延上界，保障控制动作的时间确定性。

恒温箱控制系统采用顶层模块化集成架构，共包含四类核心功能构件，分别为恒温器子系统、温度传感器设备、热源设备、操作员接口子系统。系统统一交互数据模型独立封装，依赖通用数据建模基础包提供的数据表示、值域约束、度量单位定义等基础属性支撑；四类功能构件分别归属独立的功能定义包，由顶层系统完成装配集成，构件间不存在循环依赖关系。

系统所有跨构件交互的数据需遵循统一定义的类型、值域与精度规则，所有温度类物理量统一采用华氏度为度量单位，以十分之一华氏度为定点表示精度。系统定义三类基础枚举数据类型，第一类为数据有效标志枚举，取值包含无效、有效两类，用于标识温度采样值、设置值的合法性；第二类为开关状态枚举，取值包含开、关两类，用于支撑加热控制、告警触发的二值状态表达；第三类为模块运行状态枚举，取值包含正常、故障两类，用于标识功能模块的运行健康状态。温度类数据统一采用结构体形式封装，包含温度数值、数据有效标志两个组成元素，针对不同业务场景定义独立的值域约束：传感器实测温度的值域范围为68.0华氏度至105.0华氏度；操作员可配置的下限期望温度值域为97.0华氏度至99.0华氏度，上限期望温度值域为98.0华氏度至100.0华氏度；系统告警判定对应的下限告警温度值域为93.0华氏度至98.0华氏度，上限告警温度值域为99.0华氏度至103.0华氏度。加热控制指令数据基于开关状态枚举实现，仅允许输出开或关两类控制值。操作员反馈数据为复合结构体，包含调节器运行状态、监控器运行状态、待显示温度值、告警状态四个组成字段，支撑操作员对系统运行状态的全面感知。

顶层系统内各构件的交互端口需按确定路径建立单向连接，形成四条固定数据流链路。第一条为温度采样数据流，传输方向为温度传感器到恒温器，由温度传感器采集并输出带有效标志的当前实测温度数据，经类型匹配的端口传输至恒温器的温度输入端口，作为恒温控制逻辑的核心输入依据。第二条为加热控制数据流，传输方向为恒温器到热源，由恒温器根据内置控制逻辑输出开关型加热控制指令，经类型匹配的端口传输至热源设备的控制输入端口，驱动热源启动或停止加热动作。第三条为操作员设置数据流，传输方向为操作员接口到恒温器，由操作员接口采集用户输入的各类温度设置参数，经类型匹配的端口传输至恒温器的设置输入端口，作为恒温控制的目标参数依据。第四条为运行反馈数据流，传输方向为恒温器到操作员接口，由恒温器整合内部调节器运行状态、监控器运行状态、当前温度值、告警触发状态形成综合反馈数据，经类型匹配的端口传输至操作员接口的反馈输入端口，支撑界面信息展示与告警提示输出。

当前顶层系统集成模型与统一数据模型未明确跨构件数据传输的时延指标、各功能构件的调度策略、执行周期、时间确定性等时序类约束，相关约束需在各子系统、设备的细化实现模型中结合功能安全要求补充定义；所有跨端口数据交互过程需保证数据类型严格匹配，传输数据的取值不得超出对应类型定义的值域范围，禁止传输未按规范封装的非法数据。

恒温箱顶层系统的实现需依赖四个独立组件包提供的功能模块，无其他额外第三方组件依赖。四个子组件分别为恒温器子系统、温度传感器设备、热源设备、操作员接口子系统，其中恒温器子系统、操作员接口子系统为系统类软件组件，分别来源于thermostat包的恒温器子系统实现、operator_interface包的操作员接口子系统实现；温度传感器、热源为硬件设备类组件，分别来源于temperature_sensor包的温度传感器设备实现、heat_source包的热源设备实现。所有子组件的交互路径必须在顶层系统实现中统一定义，禁止子组件之间建立未经过顶层声明的直接交互链路。

各子组件必须按互联要求匹配对应数据端口，保证跨组件交互的类型与语义一致性。温度传感器设备需对外提供当前温度输出端口，用于传输实时采集的环境温度数据。恒温器子系统需提供四类交互端口，分别为接收实时温度数据的当前温度输入端口、接收操作员配置参数的设置信息输入端口、向热源发送控制指令的热控制输出端口、向操作员接口发送运行状态的反馈信息输出端口。热源设备需提供热控制输入端口，用于接收恒温器下发的加热调节指令。操作员接口子系统需提供两类交互端口，分别为向恒温器发送操作员配置参数的设置信息输出端口、接收恒温器反馈运行状态的反馈信息输入端口。所有互联端口的数据语义、取值范围需保持匹配，不允许出现类型不兼容、语义不一致的端口连接。

系统共包含两类核心数据流，覆盖闭环控温与操作员交互两个业务域。第一类为温度闭环控制数据流，完整路径为温度传感器采集实时环境温度，经传输链路送至恒温器，恒温器结合采集温度与设定阈值生成加热控制决策，再经传输链路将控制指令送至热源设备，驱动热源执行对应加热功率调整或启停动作，该链路为系统核心控温功能的承载路径，需满足端到端流的完整性要求。第二类为操作员交互双向数据流，上行方向为操作员通过接口输入的温度阈值、工作模式等配置参数，经传输链路送至恒温器作为控温基准；下行方向为恒温器生成的当前实际温度、热源工作状态、异常告警等运行信息，经传输链路送至操作员接口，完成运行状态的人机展示。所有数据流需按既定路径传输，不得出现非预期的数据分流、丢包或篡改。

系统所有跨组件传输链路与端到端流需满足明确的时延范围要求，保障控温功能的实时性。单段跨组件端口连接的时延要求如下，温度传感器至恒温器的温度数据传输链路，端口间传输时延需处于2毫秒至4毫秒区间内；恒温器至热源的控制指令传输链路，端口间传输时延需处于5毫秒至6毫秒区间内；操作员接口至恒温器的配置参数传输链路，端口间传输时延需处于1毫秒至2毫秒区间内；恒温器至操作员接口的状态反馈传输链路，端口间传输时延需处于2毫秒至4毫秒区间内。端到端控温流时延要求如下，从温度传感器内部温度采集流起点发起温度数据传输开始，经传感器输出端口、跨链传输、恒温器内部控温决策流、跨链传输，到热源内部控制指令接收流终点的全链路时延，需处于5毫秒至9毫秒区间内。系统任务调度需优先保障核心控温数据流的传输与计算资源，不得因非核心任务的资源抢占导致各链路时延超出约束范围。

系统需构建独立的operator_interface功能包，包的公共访问域对外开放所有子系统类型与实现定义，包级依赖需显式引入isoletteDataModel公共数据模型包，包内所有跨组件交互的数据类型需复用isoletteDataModel中定义的标准化数据结构，不得在包内定义结构与isoletteDataModel中同名类型不一致的私有数据结构。功能包内需完成操作员接口子系统类型operator_interface_ss的规范定义，同时提供与该子系统类型完全匹配的实现版本operator_interface_ss.impl，实现版本需完整继承子系统类型声明的所有对外交互特征，不得擅自增减对外端口、变更端口方向或端口绑定的数据类型。

操作员接口子系统需配置两类合规的数据交互端口，第一类为输出方向的数据端口operator_settings，端口承载的数据必须严格遵循isoletteDataModel中operator_settings数据类型的结构、取值范围约束，用于向系统内其他关联组件输出操作员提交的设置参数；第二类为输入方向的数据端口operator_feedback，端口承载的数据必须严格遵循isoletteDataModel中operator_feedback数据类型的结构、取值范围约束，用于接收系统内其他关联组件发送的需向操作员展示的反馈信息。所有跨组件的端口连接必须满足方向匹配、数据类型完全兼容的要求，禁止出现端口方向错接、数据类型不匹配的非法连接。

操作员接口子系统的业务数据流需遵循固定流向规则，操作员通过人机交互环节输入的设置类信息，经子系统内部处理封装为标准格式的operator_settings数据后，仅可通过operator_settings输出端口单向流出至下游关联组件，不得通过该端口接收任何外部输入数据；系统内其他关联组件生成的面向操作员的反馈类信息，仅可通过operator_feedback输入端口单向流入操作员接口子系统，经子系统内部解析处理后完成面向操作员的信息呈现，不得通过该端口向外输出任何数据。数据传输全流程需保障数据完整性，不得出现字段缺失、数值异常篡改的问题。

当前操作员接口子系统的规范定义未设置专属的执行周期、调度优先级、最坏执行时间、数据传输时延等非功能约束，子系统在集成部署阶段需遵循所属上层系统的全局调度与时延管控规则，需保障operator_settings端口的输出时序与下游接收组件的采样时序匹配，避免设置指令丢失；需保障operator_feedback端口流入的反馈信息处理、呈现时延满足上层系统对人机交互响应的全局阈值要求，避免反馈信息滞后超标。

温度传感器相关功能元素需封装在具备公共访问权限的temperature_sensor独立包内，该包需显式依赖isoletteDataModel数据模型包，所有温度传输相关的数据类型复用该数据模型包内的标准化定义，包内无其他功能包或第三方组件依赖。

温度传感器作为硬件设备节点，仅配置一类对外交互接口，即标识为current_temperature的输出数据端口，该端口传输的数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel包中定义的current_temperature数据结构，设备不配置输入数据端口、事件端口、总线访问接口、服务调用接口等其他交互通道，所有对外数据交互仅通过该输出端口完成。

温度传感器设备需定义标识为current_temperature_flow的源端数据流，该数据流的唯一源点为设备自身的current_temperature输出端口，传感器采集生成的当前温度数据为该数据流的唯一输入来源，设备内部不设置数据加工、缓存、路由等处理环节，采集得到的温度数据直接经该数据流向外输出，设备内部不存在数据流分支、汇聚、回流或中转路径。

温度传感器设备需提供对应的实体实现，实现标识为temperature_sensor_dev.impl，该实现为温度传感器硬件的直接逻辑映射，实现内部不嵌套任何软件、硬件子组件，不定义内部端口连接逻辑，仅作为系统的温度采集源端节点接入。

当前温度传感器模型未设置显式的采样调度策略、采样周期、端口数据传输时延、采集响应时延等时序约束，传感器的运行时序需匹配所接入系统的整体时序协同要求，保障温度数据输出的时序一致性。

恒温器系统封装于thermostat包内，系统构建需依赖isoletteDataModel公共数据模型包，该包提供系统所有对外交互所需的标准化数据类型定义，恒温器系统全部交互端口的数据类型均引用该数据模型中的对应定义；thermostat_ss.impl为顶层系统thermostat_ss的实现实体，当前实现未声明内部子组件、内部连接及额外外部依赖，系统的对外交互边界由顶层系统的端口定义明确。

恒温器顶层系统需配置四个对外数据交互端口，所有端口采用数据端口模式完成跨边界数据交互。输入类端口共两个，其一为current_temperature输入端口，数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel中定义的current_temperature类型，用于接收外部温度感知单元上报的当前环境温度采样数据；其二为operator_settings输入端口，数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel中定义的operator_settings类型，用于接收操作员交互终端下发的温控工作参数配置信息。输出类端口共两个，其一为heat_control输出端口，数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel中定义的heat_control类型，用于向外部加热执行单元下发加热控制指令；其二为operator_feedback输出端口，数据类型严格匹配isoletteDataModel中定义的operator_feedback类型，用于向操作员交互终端上报系统运行状态类反馈信息。

系统需显式定义端到端流路径current_temperature_flow，该流路径的源端为current_temperature输入端口，宿端为heat_control输出端口，覆盖当前温度数据进入系统边界、经内部逻辑处理生成对应加热控制指令、送出系统边界至加热控制端口的完整数据传输链路；系统需支撑两类基础数据流转，一是操作员配置参数从operator_settings输入端口进入系统后，参与内部温控逻辑运算的内部数据流转，二是系统内部处理生成的反馈信息传输至operator_feedback输出端口并送出系统边界的数据流转，所有跨边界数据传输需保证数据类型与端口定义匹配，禁止传输类型不兼容的非法数据。

针对已定义的current_temperature_flow端到端流路径，系统需为该路径上的数据接收、逻辑处理、指令发送环节分配匹配的计算与通信资源，保障该路径的端到端处理与传输时延满足恒温控制场景的实时响应要求，避免因响应滞后导致温度控制偏差超出允许范围；系统所有端口的数据交互调度需匹配外部单元的数据收发速率，输入端口需配置满足峰值数据到达速率要求的缓存空间，输出端口需按照约定时序发送输出数据，杜绝数据丢失、错序、重复发送的交互异常。

The system shall establish a standalone publicly accessible AADL package named DataModel, which functions as the centralized reusable data type definition repository for the overall system model. This package maintains no import dependencies on any other external AADL packages, and all model elements declared within the public section of the package are available for reference and use by other packages in the system model that declare appropriate public access to the DataModel package. The DataModel package is scoped exclusively to hold data type definitions, and does not encapsulate system, hardware, software, or execution platform component declarations within its boundary.

No component type or component implementation declarations are included in the DataModel package, so there are no requirements for definition of external functional interfaces, internal interaction points, port declarations, subprogram access points, or component-level access contracts within the scope of this package. No component hierarchy, subcomponent composition, or component connection structure is defined as part of this package’s content.

As the DataModel package contains only static data type specifications without executable component instances, communication links, or port connection declarations, there are no defined end-to-end data transmission paths, segment-level data flow routes, or data routing rules specified within this package. All data flow definitions that use the data types declared in this package shall be specified in separate system or component implementation packages that import the DataModel repository.

The DataModel package does not contain declarations for threads, processes, processors, virtual processors, schedulers, or other execution-related model elements, so no periodic dispatch rules, execution deadline constraints, end-to-end latency budgets, transmission delay limits, or jitter tolerance requirements are defined within the scope of this package. All timing and scheduling constraints associated with data instances of the types defined in this package shall be specified in the relevant execution and component architecture packages that reference these data types.

Two core reusable data types shall be defined within the public section of the DataModel package, with no associated data implementation declarations provided for either type, as they serve as standardized payload type specifications rather than composite data structures requiring internal subcomponent composition. The first data type is named SensorData, which represents structured sampled sensor measurement data exchanged between system sensing and processing elements; this data type shall have a fixed Data_Size property value of 2 KByte to standardize static memory allocation, transmission payload calculation, and buffer sizing for all usages of SensorData across the system model. The second data type is named actuatecmd, which represents structured actuation command data transmitted between system control processing elements and actuation output elements; this data type shall have a fixed Data_Size property value of 100 Bytes to standardize static memory allocation, transmission payload calculation, and buffer sizing for all usages of actuatecmd across the system model. No communication bus, virtual bus, bus access protocol, or bus-related property definitions are included in the DataModel package, as bus specification falls outside the scope of this dedicated data type repository.

A dedicated AADL package named IntegratedSCS shall be defined as the top-level naming container for all sensor control system related model elements, and this package shall explicitly declare import dependencies on two external packages, namely SoftwareParts and PhysicalParts, to enable valid reference to model elements defined in those external namespaces. An abstract system type named SCS, representing the generic sensor control system template, shall be defined within the IntegratedSCS package, with no preconfigured internal structure to support extension across multiple deployment configurations. A system implementation named SCS.singletier0 shall be created for the SCS system type to represent a single-tier deployment configuration; this implementation shall contain four top-level subcomponents, including one instance of the ControlSystem system type named ControlSystem, two independent device instances named sensor1 and sensor2 respectively to represent field sensing units, and one device instance named actuator to represent the field actuation unit, with all subcomponents arranged in a flat deployment hierarchy under this configuration. A standalone abstract system type named ControlSystem shall be defined within the IntegratedSCS package to serve as the aggregation abstraction for control logic and its supporting hardware infrastructure, with no preconfigured internal structure to support variant implementation options. A system implementation named ControlSystem.singletier0 shall be created for the ControlSystem system type to match the single-tier deployment configuration of the top-level SCS; this implementation shall contain two nested subcomponents, including one instance of the DigitalControl system type referenced from the SoftwareParts package named Software to carry core digital control algorithm functions, and one instance of the main_board system type referenced from the PhysicalParts package named Hardware to provide physical computing, storage, and interconnection support for the hosted control software.

All system types defined directly within the IntegratedSCS package, including the top-level SCS type and the nested ControlSystem type, shall not declare externally exposed features such as input ports, output ports, service access points, configuration parameter interfaces, or physical connection points in the current baseline version, with reserved extension space for subsequent interface refinement as functional requirements evolve. All subcomponents contained in the SCS.singletier0 implementation, including sensor1, sensor2, actuator, and the ControlSystem instance, shall not declare component-level external interaction interfaces in the current baseline, and no explicit interface binding between these peer subcomponents shall be configured at this stage. All subcomponents contained in the ControlSystem.singletier0 implementation, including the Software instance referencing the external DigitalControl system and the Hardware instance referencing the external main_board system, shall not declare cross-layer interaction interfaces in the current baseline, and no explicit interface mapping between the software and hardware subcomponents shall be configured at this stage. All subsequent interface additions shall comply with the namespace governance rules of the parent component, and shall maintain full consistency with interface definitions of referenced elements from external dependent packages.

No explicit end-to-end data flow paths shall be defined in the current baseline of the singletier0 configuration under the IntegratedSCS package. No data link mappings shall be configured between the sensor device instances and the control system instance, between the control system instance and the actuator device instance, or between the internal software and hardware subcomponents of the ControlSystem instance at this stage. Reserved configuration space shall be retained for all data flow links, and subsequent data flow definitions shall follow the inherent hierarchical flow direction from field sensing endpoints to control processing nodes then to field actuation endpoints, with link connections strictly matching the interface definitions of connected subcomponents after interface refinement is completed.

No explicit timing-related properties shall be configured for any system, device component or their instances in the current baseline version, including but not limited to periodic scheduling rules, execution priority attributes, end-to-end transmission latency constraints, component worst-case execution time budgets, or hard/soft response time requirements. Reserved configuration entry points shall be retained for all timing-related attributes. Subsequent timing constraint binding shall be applied to specific subcomponent instances and interaction links, and shall not violate the flat scheduling domain partition of the single-tier deployment configuration. Timing configurations for software and hardware components within the ControlSystem domain shall align with the inherent property requirements of the referenced external components from the SoftwareParts and PhysicalParts packages to avoid integration mismatch.

No custom data type definitions shall be created within the IntegratedSCS package in the current baseline version. All data types used for subsequent interface interaction and data transmission shall reuse compliant data types already defined in the dependent SoftwareParts and PhysicalParts packages, and duplicate definitions of existing external data structures within the IntegratedSCS package are prohibited. No custom communication bus definitions, including both physical hardware interconnection buses and logical software communication channels, shall be created within the IntegratedSCS package in the current baseline version. All communication links between field devices and system instances, as well as between internal software and hardware subcomponents of the ControlSystem, shall reuse physical bus definitions provided by the PhysicalParts package and software communication middleware abstractions provided by the SoftwareParts package in subsequent configuration. Bus access rules shall match the physical and logical characteristics of the interfaces of connected subcomponents after interface refinement to ensure compatible interconnection.

A public AADL package named PhysicalParts shall be defined as the top-level naming container for all modeling elements associated with embedded hardware physical components. All elements contained within this package shall fall within the physical parts modeling domain, and no dependencies on elements imported from external packages shall be introduced, with all type references resolved to locally defined entries within the package. The package shall contain five categories of top-level type definitions, covering a processor type, a communication bus type, a memory type, a system type, and an abstract type. The system type named main_board shall include one implementation variant identified as single, and this implementation shall exclusively rely on the locally defined powerpc processor type, main_memory memory type, and CANbus bus type to construct its internal subcomponent structure, with no additional external component or type dependencies.

All top-level component types defined within the package, including the powerpc processor, CANbus bus, main_memory memory, main_board system, and Power abstract type, shall be constructed as base type placeholders with no externally exposed ports, functional access points, or data interaction interfaces; no input ports, output ports, provided service points, required service points, or parameter interfaces shall be declared for these top-level types. The main_board.single system implementation shall declare three internal subcomponent instances: a processor instance named cpu typed as powerpc, a memory instance named ram typed as main_memory, and a bus instance named canbus typed as CANbus. No explicit interface connections between internal subcomponents shall be defined in this implementation, no internal ports or access points shall be declared for the implementation’s external boundary, and all contained subcomponents shall carry no dedicated interaction interfaces to support cross-component communication.

No explicit data interaction ports, connection paths, or data access links shall be defined across all component types and the system implementation within the package. No fixed end-to-end data transmission path across components shall be specified within the current modeling scope, and no preconfigured data interaction channel shall exist between internal subcomponents, or between the main_board system and its external operating environment.

No scheduling attributes, periodic execution attributes, execution time attributes, or latency constraint attributes shall be configured for any component defined within the package. The powerpc processor shall not be bound to a specific scheduling policy, the main_memory memory shall not define mandatory memory access latency parameters, and the CANbus bus shall not define transmission latency or bus arbitration timing rules. The main_board system and its single implementation shall not declare timing-related constraints including end-to-end latency, scheduling period, or execution deadline, with all timing-related properties reserved for subsequent model extension and refinement.

A single abstract base type named Power shall be defined within the package; this type shall serve as a base placeholder with no internal fields, value constraints, or structural definitions, to support subsequent extension of power-related attributes without defining concrete data structures, value ranges, or encoding rules at the current modeling stage. A single communication bus type named CANbus shall be defined within the package as a base bus type placeholder, with no configured transmission protocol parameters, baud rate, frame format, or bus arbitration rules, to support subsequent bus attribute refinement and connection binding for CAN-class physical communication links. The powerpc processor type shall be defined as a base placeholder for general PowerPC architecture processors, with no specified instruction set, core frequency, core count, or other granular hardware parameters. The main_memory memory type shall be defined as a base placeholder for on-board main memory hardware, with no specified storage capacity, access bit width, read/write rate, or other memory-specific parameters. All type definitions within the package shall follow a minimal placeholder rule that only clarifies the AADL category of each element without attaching granular hardware attributes, to support incremental refinement of hardware details in follow-up modeling activities.

The system shall be contained within a top-level AADL package named SoftwareParts, which shall declare a formal import dependency on the external DataModel package to access pre-defined shared data type definitions, with no other external package dependencies. The SoftwareParts package shall define a top-level system type named DigitalControl, with one concrete system implementation identified as DigitalControl.tier1. The DigitalControl.tier1 implementation shall decompose into two generic process subcomponents with no specified concrete process type: a process subcomponent named IO_Process, and a process subcomponent named Command_Process, with no additional subcomponents specified at the top system tier. Two concrete process types shall be defined within the package to support eventual binding to these generic process subcomponents: IO_Process and Command_Process, each with one concrete implementation. The IO_Process.impl process implementation shall contain three thread subcomponents: an instance of the sensor_sense_thread type named sense, a generic thread subcomponent with no specified concrete thread type named mode_change, and an instance of the actuator_output_thread type named actuate. The Command_Process.impl process implementation shall contain three thread subcomponents: an instance of the filterApp thread type named filter, a generic thread subcomponent with no specified concrete thread type named pilot, and an instance of the controlApp thread type named control.

The DigitalControl system type, IO_Process process type, and Command_Process process type shall not define any externally facing port features, as no interface declarations are associated with these component type definitions. The sensor_sense_thread type shall expose two unidirectional data port interfaces: an incoming data port named signalin for reception of raw sensor input, and an outgoing data port named signalout for transmission of acquired sensor data to downstream processing logic. The actuator_output_thread type shall expose two unidirectional data port interfaces: an incoming data port named controlin for reception of computed actuation commands from upstream control logic, and an outgoing data port named actuate for transmission of final actuation signals to external actuator hardware. The filterApp thread type shall expose two unidirectional data port interfaces: an incoming data port named sensorraw for reception of raw sensor data from upstream sensing logic, and an outgoing data port named sensorfiltered for transmission of processed, filtered sensor data to downstream control logic. The controlApp thread type shall expose two unidirectional data port interfaces: an incoming data port named sensorfiltered for reception of filtered sensor data from upstream filtering logic, and an outgoing data port named actuatesensor for transmission of newly calculated actuation commands to downstream output logic. The generic mode_change thread within IO_Process and the generic pilot thread within Command_Process shall not define any explicit port features, as no specialized type or interface declarations are associated with these base thread instances.

The port definitions on the specialized thread types establish type-compatible endpoint pairs that define the intended logical closed-loop control data path, though explicit port connections and required cross-hierarchy port delegations are not specified in the current component structure, as no port features are declared on process or system component types and no connection declarations exist at any hierarchical level. The type-aligned logical path originates at the signalin input port of sensor_sense_thread, which is intended to receive raw sensor data from external sensing sources. The signalout output port of sensor_sense_thread, which carries SensorData type values, is type-compatible with the sensorraw input port of filterApp, which also carries SensorData type values, forming a logical sensing to filtering link. The sensorfiltered output port of filterApp, which carries SensorData type values, is type-compatible with the sensorfiltered input port of controlApp, which also carries SensorData type values, forming a logical filtering to control calculation link. The actuatesensor output port of controlApp, which carries actuatecmd type values, is type-compatible with the controlin input port of actuator_output_thread, which also carries actuatecmd type values, forming a logical control calculation to output link. The actuate output port of actuator_output_thread, which carries actuatecmd type values, is intended to transmit final actuation signals to external actuator hardware. No logical data flow paths are defined for the generic mode_change and pilot thread instances, as these components lack declared port features to support connection to other system elements.

All specialized thread types with defined properties shall support periodic dispatch with a common 20 ms period. The sensor_sense_thread shall be allocated a 10 Kbyte worst-case stack size, with per-dispatch compute execution time bounded between a minimum of 10 ms and a maximum of 12 ms. The actuator_output_thread shall be allocated a 10 Kbyte worst-case stack size, with per-dispatch compute execution time bounded between a minimum of 8 ms and a maximum of 10 ms. The filterApp thread shall be allocated a 25 Kbyte worst-case stack size, plus a 250 Kbyte private data memory region reserved for logging operations, with per-dispatch compute execution time bounded between a minimum of 5 ms and a maximum of 7 ms. The controlApp thread shall be allocated a 25 Kbyte worst-case stack size, plus a 50 Kbyte private data memory region reserved for persistent control state storage, with per-dispatch compute execution time bounded between a minimum of 2 ms and a maximum of 6 ms. No scheduling period, execution time bound, stack size, or private memory allocation properties are specified for the generic mode_change and pilot thread instances, nor for the generic IO_Process and Command_Process process subcomponents at the system tier. No explicit end-to-end latency bounds are defined for any data path in the current specification.

All data exchanged via thread data ports shall use typed data definitions imported from the external DataModel package. The SensorData data type from the DataModel package shall be used for all sensor measurement transfers, including raw sensor data carried on the signalin and signalout ports of sensor_sense_thread, the sensorraw input port of filterApp, and the paired sensorfiltered ports of filterApp and controlApp. The actuatecmd data type from the DataModel package shall be used for all actuation command transfers, including the actuatesensor output port of controlApp, the controlin input port of actuator_output_thread, and the actuate output port of actuator_output_thread. No custom data type definitions shall be declared within the SoftwareParts package. No dedicated communication bus components, bus access interfaces, or bus-associated communication properties shall be defined within the SoftwareParts package, meaning inter-thread and inter-process data transfer mechanisms are not constrained to a specific physical or logical bus implementation at this specification level.

The system defines a public AADL package named heat_source, which holds an explicit import dependency on the isoletteDataModel package to reference shared, standardized data type definitions from the common system data model. The heat_source package encapsulates all structural definitions associated with the heat source hardware device, with no nested sub-packages or additional cross-package dependencies beyond the referenced isoletteDataModel package. The package contains one top-level device component type designated heat_source_dev, and one matching concrete device implementation designated heat_source_dev.impl. The heat_source_dev.impl implementation declares no internal subcomponents, and acts as the realizable instance definition for the heat_source_dev device type.

The heat_source_dev device component exposes a single external interface feature implemented as an input data port named heat_control. This port supports unidirectional data transfer into the device, and is strictly typed to conform to the heat_control data structure defined in the isoletteDataModel package. The heat_source_dev.impl implementation does not define supplementary external interface features beyond those inherited from the heat_source_dev component type, contains no internal subcomponent interface declarations, and specifies no internal connection links as no subcomponents are present in the implementation.

The heat_source_dev component type defines a single formal flow specification named heat_control_flow, which is categorized as a flow sink that terminates entirely within the device hardware boundary. The ingress point of this flow sink is the externally accessible heat_control input data port, and the flow path terminates at the device’s internal heat generation actuation logic, with no defined outbound data flow paths that exit the device boundary. The heat_source_dev.impl implementation does not introduce additional flow specifications or internal flow segments, and fully inherits all flow path declarations from the associated heat_source_dev component type without modification.

No periodic scheduling policies, execution time budgets, worst-case execution time limits, inter-port transmission latency values, or end-to-end flow latency constraints are declared for any component or implementation contained in the heat_source package. All timing and scheduling related properties remain unassigned at the package level, and may be configured during later system integration activities to align with platform-specific performance and real-time requirements.

The heat_source package does not define any local, package-specific data types, and relies exclusively on data type definitions imported from the isoletteDataModel package for all port interfaces to ensure consistent data representation across interconnected system components. The package does not declare any bus components, virtual bus components, or bus access interface features. The heat_source_dev device and its corresponding implementation do not include binding properties that map device ports to specific physical or logical communication buses, and no mandatory bus protocol requirements are specified for data transmitted over the heat_control input port, leaving bus binding and protocol configuration to be applied during physical system integration.

The system is organized under a single root AADL package named isoletteDataModel, with public visibility applied to all contained type and component definitions. The root package declares explicit import dependencies on five external packages: the Data_Model package, which provides standardized data modeling property definitions for consistent type constraint enforcement; the thermostat package, which provides executable implementations of the thermostat control subsystem; the heat_source package, which provides executable implementations of the heat output device; the temperature_sensor package, which provides executable implementations of the ambient temperature measurement device; and the operator_interface package, which provides executable implementations of the user interaction subsystem. All shared data definitions and top-level system integration logic are encapsulated directly within the isoletteDataModel package, with no nested sub-packages defined in the current scope. The top-level system component contained in the package is isoletteSystem, which represents the complete integrated isolette thermal regulation system, with a single implementation named isoletteSystem.impl that defines the first-tier component composition and interconnection logic for the full system.

The top-level isoletteSystem component type does not define any externally exposed ports, as all functional interactions are contained between internal subcomponents, with no external system interfaces specified in the current package scope. The isoletteSystem.impl implementation instantiates four first-tier subcomponents, each aligned with a component type provided by the imported external packages. The first subcomponent is named thermostat, typed as the thermostat subsystem implementation provided by the thermostat package, which exposes four data ports for cross-component interaction: an inbound data port for current temperature measurements, an outbound data port for heat control commands, an inbound data port for operator configuration settings, and an outbound data port for system status feedback to the operator. The second subcomponent is named temperature_sensor, typed as the temperature sensor device implementation provided by the temperature_sensor package, which exposes a single outbound data port for sampled current temperature measurements. The third subcomponent is named heat_source, typed as the heat source device implementation provided by the heat_source package, which exposes a single inbound data port for heat actuation commands. The fourth subcomponent is named operator_interface, typed as the operator interface subsystem implementation provided by the operator_interface package, which exposes two data ports for cross-component interaction: an outbound data port for user-entered configuration settings, and an inbound data port for system status feedback to be presented to the user. For contained data components, the operator_feedback data type defines an implementation that includes four internal data subcomponents to structure feedback payloads: a regulator_status field, a monitor_status field, a display_temperature field, and an alarm field. No data components define externally exposed ports, as all data types are used exclusively as structured payloads for port-based communication between system components.

All inter-component data exchange within the integrated isoletteSystem is routed via direct unidirectional point-to-point data port connections defined in the isoletteSystem.impl implementation, with no intermediate routing components between connected endpoints. The first data flow path originates at the temperature_sensor subcomponent, where sampled current temperature data is transmitted from the sensor’s outbound current_temperature port to the matching inbound current_temperature port on the thermostat subcomponent, delivering real-time temperature measurements to the core control logic. The second data flow path originates at the operator_interface subcomponent, where user-entered configuration settings are transmitted from the interface’s outbound operator_settings port to the matching inbound operator_settings port on the thermostat subcomponent, delivering user-defined setpoints and alarm thresholds to the control logic. The third data flow path originates at the thermostat subcomponent, where generated heat actuation commands are transmitted from the thermostat’s outbound heat_control port to the matching inbound heat_control port on the heat_source subcomponent, delivering binary control signals to adjust heat output to maintain desired temperature levels. The fourth data flow path originates at the thermostat subcomponent, where compiled system status, temperature readout, and alarm state data is transmitted from the thermostat’s outbound operator_feedback port to the matching inbound operator_feedback port on the operator_interface subcomponent, delivering updated system state information for presentation to the end user. No circular data paths are defined in the top-level system integration, with all flows following a unidirectional path from sensing and user input components to the central thermostat control subsystem, then from the control subsystem to the heat source actuation component and user output interface.

The isoletteDataModel package does not define explicit timing, scheduling, or latency constraints at the top system integration layer. No thread, process, virtual processor, or processor components are declared within the package scope, meaning all execution timing rules, dispatch protocols, scheduling partition assignments, component execution periods, deadline requirements, and end-to-end latency budgets are encapsulated within the imported external component packages for the thermostat, temperature_sensor, heat_source, and operator_interface subsystems and devices. No cross-component timing synchronization requirements, transmission delay limits, or jitter constraints are specified for the point-to-point port connections defined in the top-level system implementation, as these timing properties are deferred to the lower-level implementation details of each connected component.

No dedicated communication bus, virtual bus, or bus access components are defined within the isoletteDataModel package. All inter-component data exchange is implemented via the direct point-to-point data port connections previously described, with no intermediate bus routing, protocol encapsulation, or shared communication media defined in the current integration scope. All data transmitted across these port connections must strictly conform to the shared data type definitions contained in the package, with type conformance enforced at connection binding time. All data type constraints are specified using properties from the imported Data_Model package to ensure consistent representation and valid value ranges across all system components. Three base enumerated data types are defined for general use across the system. The first enumerated type is valid_flag, which uses an enum data representation with two allowed enumerator values: Invalid and Valid, used to indicate the trustworthiness and validity of associated measurement or configuration data. The second enumerated type is on_off, which uses an enum data representation with two allowed enumerator values: On and Off, used to represent binary actuation states and alarm activation states. The third enumerated type is status, which uses an enum data representation with two allowed enumerator values: Ok and Error, used to represent the operational health state of functional control and monitoring modules. Two base real-valued range types are defined for temperature data, with measurement units specified as degrees Fahrenheit. The first real type is measured_temperature_range, which enforces a valid real number range of 68.0 to 105.0 for raw temperature sensor measurements. The second real type is temperature_range, which enforces a base valid real number range of 0.0 to 105.0, with five specialized implementations that narrow the valid range for specific use cases: the measured_temperature_range implementation narrows the range to 68.0 to 105.0 as a subtype of the generic temperature_range, the lower_desired_range implementation narrows the range to 97.0 to 99.0 for user-configured lower temperature setpoints, the upper_desired_range implementation narrows the range to 98.0 to 100.0 for user-configured upper temperature setpoints, the lower_alarm_range implementation narrows the range to 93.0 to 98.0 for lower temperature alarm thresholds, and the upper_alarm_range implementation narrows the range to 99.0 to 103.0 for upper temperature alarm thresholds. Composite and structured data types are defined to package related data elements for port transmission and internal storage. The first composite data type is current_temperature, which defines two named elements without an explicit struct data representation marker: a temperature value element constrained to the top-level measured_temperature_range real type, and a validity status element constrained to the valid_flag enumerated type, intended for direct use as the payload for the current temperature sensor data port between the temperature sensor and thermostat. The second structured type is temperature, which explicitly uses a struct data representation with two named elements: a temperature value element constrained to the base temperature_range real type, and a validity status element constrained to the valid_flag enumerated type, used as the generic temperature type for setpoints, alarm thresholds, and user display values, with five specialized implementations that bind the temperature value element to specific range types: the current_temperature_impl implementation binds the temperature value element to the top-level measured_temperature_range real type for transmission of current sensor readings in generic temperature struct format, the lower_desired_temperature implementation binds the temperature value element to the temperature_range.lower_desired_range implementation for lower setpoint storage and transmission, the upper_desired_temperature implementation binds the temperature value element to the temperature_range.upper_desired_range implementation for upper setpoint storage and transmission, the lower_alarm_temperature implementation binds the temperature value element to the temperature_range.lower_alarm_range implementation for lower alarm threshold storage and transmission, and the upper_alarm_temperature implementation binds the temperature value element to the temperature_range.upper_alarm_range implementation for upper alarm threshold storage and transmission. Three top-level communication payload data types are defined for cross-component port exchange. The first payload type is heat_control, with a single implementation named heat_control.impl that binds the type’s base value to the on_off enumerated type, to carry binary heat source activation and deactivation commands between the thermostat and heat source. The second payload type is operator_settings, defined as an abstract data type for carrying user configuration values between the operator interface and thermostat, with no internal structure or implementation defined in the current package scope, as structure details are deferred to the connected component implementations. The third payload type is operator_feedback, with a single implementation named operator_feedback.impl that defines four internal data fields to structure status reports: a regulator_status field typed as the status enumerated type to report the health of the temperature regulation function, a monitor_status field typed as the status enumerated type to report the health of the temperature monitoring function, a display_temperature field typed as the generic temperature structured type to carry the current measured temperature for user display, and an alarm field typed as the dedicated alarm data type to carry current alarm state. The alarm data type is defined as a dedicated type that binds its base value to the on_off enumerated type, to represent binary alarm activation and deactivation states for user notification.

The top-level modeling package shall be named isoletteSystem, with public access scope and explicit import dependencies on four external packages: thermostat, heat_source, temperature_sensor, and operator_interface. A top-level system component type designated isoletteSystem shall be defined within the package to act as the root encapsulation container for all isolette system elements, with no externally accessible ports declared at this top system type boundary. A system implementation identified as isoletteSystem.impl shall be specified as the first-tier integration realization of the top-level system, hosting four directly contained subcomponents. The first subcomponent shall be named thermostat, classified as a system component that references the thermostat_ss.impl implementation from the thermostat package, to deliver core closed-loop temperature regulation functionality. The second subcomponent shall be named temperature_sensor, classified as a device component that references the temperature_sensor_dev.impl implementation from the temperature_sensor package, to perform continuous ambient temperature measurement and sampling. The third subcomponent shall be named heat_source, classified as a device component that references the heat_source_dev.impl implementation from the heat_source package, to produce adjustable heat output in response to received control commands. The fourth subcomponent shall be named operator_interface, classified as a system component that references the operator_interface_ss.impl implementation from the operator_interface package, to handle operator configuration input and system status presentation.

All inter-component interaction interfaces shall take the form of directional data ports, with port contracts fully inherited from the referenced external component implementations to avoid redundant interface definition at the top integration level. The temperature_sensor device subcomponent shall provide an output data port named current_temperature for transmission of sampled real-time temperature measurements. The thermostat subcomponent shall expose four directional data ports: an input data port named current_temperature for reception of sampled temperature data from the sensing device, an input data port named operator_settings for reception of configuration parameters from the operator interface, an output data port named heat_control for transmission of heating adjustment commands to the heat source device, and an output data port named operator_feedback for transmission of operational status data to the operator interface. The heat_source device subcomponent shall provide an input data port named heat_control for reception of heating control commands from the thermostat. The operator_interface subcomponent shall expose two directional data ports: an output data port named operator_settings for transmission of user-entered configuration parameters, and an input data port named operator_feedback for reception of system status feedback from the thermostat. No additional ports shall be added to subcomponents within the top-level system implementation.

Four point-to-point port connections shall be instantiated between matching subcomponent ports to enable unobstructed inter-component data transfer. The first connection, named current_temperature, shall connect the current_temperature output port of the temperature_sensor subcomponent to the current_temperature input port of the thermostat subcomponent, carrying continuous real-time temperature sampling data. The second connection, named heat_control, shall connect the heat_control output port of the thermostat subcomponent to the heat_control input port of the heat_source subcomponent, carrying heating actuation commands. The third connection, named operator_settings, shall connect the operator_settings output port of the operator_interface subcomponent to the operator_settings input port of the thermostat subcomponent, carrying user-configured operating parameters. The fourth connection, named operator_feedback, shall connect the operator_feedback output port of the thermostat subcomponent to the operator_feedback input port of the operator_interface subcomponent, carrying system operational status data for operator display. An end-to-end flow path designated path1 shall be declared to represent the core closed-loop temperature control data pathway, originating at the internal current_temperature_flow flow source within the temperature_sensor subcomponent, passing sequentially through the current_temperature inter-component port connection, the internal current_temperature_flow processing segment within the thermostat subcomponent, and the heat_control inter-component port connection, before terminating at the internal heat_control_flow flow sink within the heat_source subcomponent.

Deterministic latency constraints shall be assigned to each inter-component port connection and the defined end-to-end flow path to meet real-time system performance requirements. The current_temperature connection between the temperature_sensor and thermostat shall enforce an allowed one-way transmission latency range of 2 milliseconds to 4 milliseconds. The heat_control connection between the thermostat and heat_source shall enforce an allowed one-way transmission latency range of 5 milliseconds to 6 milliseconds. The operator_settings connection between the operator_interface and thermostat shall enforce an allowed one-way transmission latency range of 1 millisecond to 2 milliseconds. The operator_feedback connection between the thermostat and operator_interface shall enforce an allowed one-way transmission latency range of 2 milliseconds to 4 milliseconds. The end-to-end flow path path1, spanning the full operational chain from initial temperature sampling to delivery of heating commands to the actuation device, shall enforce a cumulative end-to-end latency range of 5 milliseconds to 9 milliseconds, with this bound covering all data transmission delays across inter-component links and internal processing delays within traversed subcomponents.

No custom data type definitions shall be declared within the isoletteSystem package. All data payloads exchanged across inter-component ports shall adhere strictly to the data type specifications defined for corresponding ports in the referenced external dependent packages, with no redundant type redefinition or override at the top system integration level. No dedicated shared bus components shall be defined within the isoletteSystem package to mediate inter-component communication. All inter-component data transfer shall be implemented via direct point-to-point port connections, with communication quality attributes including latency bound directly to individual port connection instances, with no intermediate bus abstraction layer inserted between communicating components.

The system shall define a public AADL package named operator_interface. This package shall declare a single import dependency on the isoletteDataModel package, with all cross-namespace references restricted to elements from the imported isoletteDataModel package, and no additional external package imports shall be permitted. The operator_interface package shall contain one system type component designated operator_interface_ss, and one matching system implementation component designated operator_interface_ss.impl within its public scope. No additional component types, component implementations, native data type definitions, bus definitions, virtual bus definitions, subprogram definitions, or property set definitions shall be included in the operator_interface package.

The operator_interface_ss system type shall define two data ports as its complete external feature set, with no additional interface elements including event ports, event data ports, bus access points, subprogram access points, parameter ports, or feature groups exposed at the system boundary. The first port shall be an outgoing data port named operator_settings, and the second port shall be an incoming data port named operator_feedback. The operator_interface_ss.impl system implementation shall not introduce any supplementary external interface features beyond those specified in the operator_interface_ss system type. This system implementation shall not declare any internal subcomponents, internal port instances, internal connection paths, or internal feature groups, maintaining a flat component structure with no nested hierarchical composition.

All data exchange associated with the operator_interface_ss system shall occur at the system boundary through the two defined data ports. The system shall send operator setting data to external peer components via the outgoing operator_settings data port, and shall accept operator feedback data from external peer components via the incoming operator_feedback data port. Since the operator_interface_ss.impl implementation contains no internal subcomponents or internal connections, no internal data routing, transformation, or forwarding paths shall exist within the system boundary.

No explicit scheduling policies, dispatch triggers, periodic execution attributes, worst-case execution time bounds, deadline constraints, or end-to-end latency requirements shall be defined at the package level, system type level, or system implementation level within the operator_interface package. No fixed scheduling protocol bindings or timing property assignments shall be specified for the contained system components, reserving all timing-related configuration for higher-level system integration activities.

All data types conveyed through the system’s external data ports shall be referenced directly from the imported isoletteDataModel package, and no local custom data type definitions shall be present in the operator_interface package. The outgoing operator_settings data port shall transmit data conforming to the operator_settings data type defined in the isoletteDataModel namespace. The incoming operator_feedback data port shall receive data conforming to the operator_feedback data type defined in the isoletteDataModel namespace. The operator_interface package shall not define any native bus components, virtual bus components, or bus access interfaces, and shall not mandate specific bus bindings for the exposed data ports, permitting port communication mappings to be established during upper-level system integration.

The system shall define a public AADL package named temperature_sensor to contain all structural modeling elements associated with temperature sensor functionality. This package shall establish an explicit import dependency on the external isoletteDataModel package to access pre-defined shared data type specifications, and shall not include nested sub-packages, undeclared external dependencies, or encapsulated elements unrelated to temperature sensor representation.

The temperature_sensor package shall declare a device component type named temperature_sensor_dev to serve as the formal abstraction of the physical temperature sensing hardware. This device component type shall expose a single external interface feature in the form of an outgoing data port identified as current_temperature. The component type shall be paired with a concrete device implementation named temperature_sensor_dev.impl, which shall not define internal subcomponents, private functional features, internal interaction ports, or internal connection pathways. No internal interfaces shall be exposed by the implementation that are not specified at the component type level.

The current_temperature output port defined on the temperature_sensor_dev component shall strictly adhere to the data structure of the current_temperature type imported from the isoletteDataModel package, with no alteration to port direction, data type reference, or port identifier permitted in the associated implementation.

The temperature_sensor_dev component type shall specify a named flow source called current_temperature_flow, which takes the component’s current_temperature output port as its originating point. This flow specification defines the complete internal data path for temperature measurements generated by the sensor, with no internal flow segments, branching routes, intermediate processing stages, or incoming data flow paths contained within the device boundary. All sensed temperature data produced by the device shall be transmitted externally exclusively through the current_temperature output port, which acts as the sole data egress point for the sensor component.

No mandatory timing, scheduling, or latency constraints shall be defined for the temperature_sensor_dev component or its impl implementation within the package scope. This includes, but is not limited to, periodic execution schedules, execution deadline thresholds, port transmission latency limits, worst-case response time requirements, and execution priority assignments. Timing-related properties for the sensor device may be added during subsequent higher-level system integration without modifying the core structural definition of the component.

All data conveyed through the current_temperature output port shall utilize the shared current_temperature data type defined in the imported isoletteDataModel package, and no local, duplicate, or modified definition of this temperature data type shall be created within the temperature_sensor package. No dedicated communication bus definitions, bus access features, or static port-to-bus binding rules shall be declared within the temperature_sensor package. The current_temperature output port shall not be pre-associated with any specific physical or logical communication bus, leaving bus binding configuration to be completed during system-level deployment modeling per integration requirements.

A public AADL package named thermostat shall be defined to encapsulate all modeling elements associated with the thermostat system. This package shall declare an explicit import dependency on the external data package isoletteDataModel, and no additional cross-package dependencies shall be included. The package shall contain one top-level system component type designated thermostat_ss, which represents the core thermostat subsystem. A single concrete system implementation identified as thermostat_ss.impl shall be provided for the thermostat_ss component type. This implementation shall contain no nested internal subcomponents, internal connection declarations, or resource binding statements in its current baseline.

The thermostat_ss system type shall expose four external data port interfaces, comprising two unidirectional input data ports and two unidirectional output data ports. The first input port shall be named current_temperature, configured with an in direction, and shall transport data values conforming to the isoletteDataModel::current_temperature data type to receive real-time current temperature measurements from external sensing components. The second input port shall be named operator_settings, configured with an in direction, and shall transport data values conforming to the isoletteDataModel::operator_settings data type to receive configuration parameters submitted by system operators. The first output port shall be named heat_control, configured with an out direction, and shall transport data values conforming to the isoletteDataModel::heat_control data type to send actuation commands to external heating control hardware. The second output port shall be named operator_feedback, configured with an out direction, and shall transport data values conforming to the isoletteDataModel::operator_feedback data type to deliver operational status information to the operator-facing interface. The thermostat_ss.impl system implementation shall not define internal private ports, subcomponent-level interfaces, or internal cross-component connection constructs in the current baseline.

The thermostat_ss system type shall declare one formal end-to-end flow path named current_temperature_flow. This flow path shall specify a contiguous data propagation route that originates at the current_temperature input port as the source endpoint and terminates at the heat_control output port as the sink endpoint, representing the core functional data path from incoming temperature sensing input to outgoing heating actuation output. No additional end-to-end flow paths covering the remaining external ports shall be specified in the current model version, and the declared flow path shall not define intermediate internal processing hops, as no internal subcomponents are present in the associated implementation.

No explicit component scheduling policies, periodic or aperiodic triggering rules, port communication latency values, end-to-end flow latency constraints, thread execution time budgets, or deadline requirements shall be defined within the current thermostat package model. All timing, scheduling, and latency related specifications shall be reserved for subsequent model refinement and implementation expansion.

All data types utilized for inter-component communication across system ports shall be defined within the externally imported isoletteDataModel package. No native custom data type definitions shall be contained within the thermostat package itself. All external interaction points of the thermostat system shall use sampled data ports as the sole communication abstraction, with no event ports, event-data ports, subprogram access points, or bus access features declared as part of the system’s external interface. No logical or physical communication bus definitions, bus access interfaces, or port-to-bus binding rules shall be declared within the thermostat package in the current baseline. All bus architecture and communication medium specifications shall be reserved for subsequent model extension.

The system shall define a standalone public AADL package named DataDictionary that operates as the centralized shared data type repository for the full system model. This package shall not declare dependencies on any other custom component packages, domain-specific model libraries, or user-defined property sets, and shall only reference the AADL standard predefined core property set to support configuration of built-in data attributes. All type definitions contained in the DataDictionary package shall have public visibility, allowing unconstrained reference by all other packages and components across the system model to ensure consistent data typing for cross-component interactions.

The DataDictionary package shall contain two data component type definitions, designated SensorData and BrakeSignal respectively. Neither data component shall declare external interaction interfaces, including required or provided data ports, event ports, event data ports, subprogram access points, or bus access interfaces. Neither data component shall define internal subcomponent hierarchies, internal connection logic, or separate implementation artifacts, as both components serve exclusively as typed data carriers for cross-component data exchange rather than executable functional entities.

The DataDictionary package shall not define executable functional components, hardware devices, communication links, or component interconnection bindings, and as such shall not specify end-to-end data flow paths, data routing rules, or in-line data processing sequences. All data flow interactions that leverage the data types defined in this package shall be specified within the corresponding application or platform packages that host the connected functional components, with no data forwarding, transformation, or routing logic encapsulated within the DataDictionary package.

The DataDictionary package shall not contain any schedulable execution entities, including threads, thread groups, processes, virtual processors, or physical processors, and thus shall not define scheduling policies, execution periods, dispatch protocols, hard or soft deadline constraints, allowable jitter limits, or end-to-end latency requirements. All timing and scheduling attributes for components that reference data types from this package shall be configured within the defining scope of the respective component’s parent package, with no timing-related constraints applied to the static data type definitions held in the DataDictionary package.

Each data type defined in the DataDictionary package shall be assigned a fixed Data_Size property to guarantee consistent serialization length across all communication transmission and persistent storage scenarios. The SensorData data type shall be configured with a Data_Size property value of 8 bytes. The BrakeSignal data type shall be configured with a Data_Size property value of 8 bytes. The DataDictionary package shall not define communication bus types, bus implementations, bus access protocols, or bus property constraints, as all communication medium definitions shall be captured in dedicated platform architecture packages separated from the shared data type repository.

The system shall define a top-level public AADL package named Brake, which shall explicitly declare import dependencies on three pre-existing external packages: the DataDictionary package containing shared system data type definitions, the Infrastructure package containing pre-modeled communication and power bus definitions, and the SEI package containing standard reusable non-functional property definitions. The Brake package shall contain all component definitions related to the brake actuator unit, with no nested sub-packages declared within its scope. Within the Brake package, a device component type named SimpleBrake shall be defined to represent the basic hardware brake actuator, and a corresponding device implementation named SimpleBrake.i shall be defined to specify the concrete property values and implementation characteristics of the SimpleBrake device type.

The SimpleBrake device type shall expose three external features as its complete external interface, with no additional provided or required interfaces defined on the component type. The first feature is a data input port named dataIn, configured as an in-direction data port for reception of incoming brake signal data. The second feature is a required bus access port named busIn, which declares the device’s need to access a specified communication bus instance. The third feature is a required bus access port named powerIn, which declares the device’s need to access a specified power supply bus instance. The SimpleBrake.i device implementation shall not define any internal subcomponents, internal connection paths, call sequences, or private internal interfaces, and shall realize the device functionality as a self-contained hardware unit interacting with external elements solely through the three external features defined on the SimpleBrake device type.

The SimpleBrake device shall define a dedicated sink flow path named brakeFlow, which takes the dataIn input port as its sole ingress point and terminates within the device’s internal actuation logic. No egress segment shall be defined for the brakeFlow path, as the path represents a unidirectional flow of brake command data into the device for actuation processing. The device shall process incoming brake signal data received via the dataIn port to execute physical brake actuation actions aligned with the received signal value.

The brakeFlow end-to-end path within the SimpleBrake.i implementation shall satisfy a bounded latency constraint, with the total propagation delay from the point a valid brake signal arrives at the dataIn port to the point the device completes the corresponding actuation action for that signal falling within the closed range of 3 milliseconds to 5 milliseconds. No periodic dispatch or time-triggered scheduling configuration shall be defined for the SimpleBrake device, as the unit operates as a hardware actuator that responds directly to valid input signals received at its dataIn port. The SimpleBrake.i implementation shall comply with defined non-functional resource constraints, including a total device weight limit of 1.0 kilograms applied to the entire device assembly, and a power consumption budget of 4.0 watts applied specifically to the powerIn bus access interface, such that the maximum power the device draws through the powerIn port during normal operation shall not exceed the 4.0 watt budget.

All data transmitted through the dataIn input port shall strictly conform to the BrakeSignal data type defined in the imported DataDictionary package, with no alternative or custom data types permitted for brake signal transmission on this port. The busIn required access port shall only connect to the i instance of the canBus controller area network bus defined in the imported Infrastructure package, representing the device’s required access to the specified CAN bus instance. The powerIn required access port shall only connect to the generic instance of the power supply bus defined in the imported Infrastructure package, through which the device draws all required operating power. All non-functional property assignments for weight limit and power budget shall reference the standard property definitions contained in the imported SEI package, with the WeightLimit property applied to the full scope of the SimpleBrake.i implementation and the powerBudget property applied exclusively to the powerIn bus access port.

The system shall define a top-level AADL package named Infrastructure, which shall establish an explicit import dependency on the SEI pre-defined property package to support configuration of SEI-namespaced architecture properties. The Infrastructure package shall encapsulate all base infrastructure elements, including communication bus types and implementations, power transmission bus types and implementations, and power source system components and their implementations, and shall not contain application-specific functional logic components, executable thread components, or standalone data type definitions.
