The top-level system type defined within this package shall carry the identifier CommandControl, and shall inherit all core characteristics from the GenericFunction system type hosted in the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to ensure compliance with universal wheel brake function interface and behavior constraints. The concrete, deployable implementation of the CommandControl system shall carry the identifier CommandControl.basic, and shall inherit core implementation logic from the GenericFunction.basic implementation hosted in the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to reuse common function capabilities. The CommandControl.basic implementation shall contain two internal subsystem subcomponents, identified as Control_Primary and Control_Secondary respectively; both subcomponents shall be instantiated directly from the Generic.basic system implementation hosted in the functional::GenericFunctions package, corresponding to the primary command processing channel and secondary command processing channel of the command control function. The CommandControl.basic implementation shall configure the WBSPS::IsFunction property to a boolean value of true to mark the component as a recognized wheel brake system functional element.

The CommandControl system type shall declare a single external feature identified as fromBSCU, which serves as the component’s only externally exposed interaction endpoint. Per defined error propagation interface rules, the fromBSCU feature shall operate as an outbound error propagation port with the capability to transmit any functional error type defined in the wheel brake functional error library. The two internal subcomponents, Control_Primary and Control_Secondary, shall fully adhere to the standard interface specifications defined for the generic Generic function component, with no additional custom internal interfaces introduced in the basic implementation variant. The command control component shall define an internal error event identified as lossBrakingCommand, which falls under the WBErrorSet error classification and corresponds to the internal fault scenario of complete braking command output loss. The component shall also support an inbound error propagation path for errors originating from the aircraft electrical system, with the capability to receive any class of functional error transmitted from upstream electrical system components.

Functional data interaction and data flow logic for the command control component shall inherit default flow rules defined in the GenericFunction base class, with no custom functional data flow paths specified in the basic implementation variant. For error flow routing, a top-level error propagation path identified as f1 shall be defined, which originates at the fromBSCU external port and propagates errors of the AnyFunctionalError classification to external connected components. When the component enters the Failed error state, all generated functional errors shall be propagated outward through the fromBSCU port per propagation rule p1, with no conditional filtering applied to the set of propagated error types. Composite error state aggregation across internal subcomponents shall follow a logical OR evaluation rule: if either the Control_Primary subcomponent or the Control_Secondary subcomponent enters the Failed error state, the top-level CommandControl component shall immediately transition to the Failed error state.

The CommandControl.basic implementation shall not define custom thread scheduling policies, execution period constraints, deadline parameters, or end-to-end latency requirements in the current variant; all applicable timing and scheduling rules shall be inherited directly from the GenericFunction.basic base implementation. The occurrence of the internal lossBrakingCommand error event shall follow a Poisson probability distribution, with a per-operational-exposure occurrence probability value of 3.3e-5, aligned with the reliability requirement specified in AIR6110 document page 49. Component error state transitions shall execute immediately upon satisfaction of defined transition guard conditions, with no intentional delay applied to error state switching logic. Two valid error state transitions shall be supported for the component: the first transition, identified as t1, shall activate when the internal lossBrakingCommand error event occurs while the component is in the Operational state, moving the component to the Failed state; the second transition, identified as t2, shall activate when any functional error is received from the electrical system propagation path while the component is in the Operational state, moving the component to the Failed state and associating the failure with the TotalWBLossUnanunciated failure effect. The component error behavior shall be based on the two-state (Twostate) error state machine imported from the WBSFunctionalErrorLib, with valid states limited to Operational and Failed.

The CommandControl.basic implementation shall not define custom AADL data types within the local package; all data types used for functional interaction shall be inherited from imported dependent packages and the GenericFunction base class. The implementation shall not define custom bus components, bus access features, or bus binding rules in the current variant; all communication bus-related configurations shall follow default specifications defined in the upper-level generic function base class. All error types referenced in the component error model shall be imported from the WBSFunctionalErrorLib error library, including the Twostate error behavior state machine definition, the AnyFunctionalError error type set, the WBErrorSet error classification, and the TotalWBLossUnanunciated failure effect type.

The system is organized under the AADL package named functional::WheelBrake::Generic, with public scope enabled for all top-level declarations within the package. The package explicitly declares a dependency on the WBSPS property set to support domain-specific property assignment. All components within the package that include EMV2 error model annexes hold a dependency on the external WBSFunctionalErrorLib error type library, and the GenericBrakeSystem component holds an additional dependency on the Twostate error behavior definition contained in WBSFunctionalErrorLib. The package defines two top-level system type components, namely GenericFunction and GenericBrakeSystem, and each system type is paired with a dedicated system implementation named basic. Both system type components are assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true to mark them as valid functional elements of the wheel brake system domain.

The GenericFunction system type exposes five untyped abstract features as its external interface, with identifiers fromElectrical, fromHydraulic, fromAlert, fromSteering, and fromStatus respectively. Each feature is configured with defined inbound error propagation rules per EMV2 specifications, allowing functional errors to propagate from externally connected components into the GenericFunction component through these features: the fromElectrical feature accepts propagated errors belonging to the AnyFunctionalError set; the fromHydraulic feature only accepts propagated errors belonging to the HydraulicErrors set; the fromAlert, fromSteering, and fromStatus features each accept propagated errors belonging to the AnyFunctionalError set. The GenericFunction.basic system implementation is defined as a minimal base implementation, with no nested subcomponents, internal feature declarations, connection bindings, or additional property and annex declarations contained in its structure. The GenericBrakeSystem system type does not expose any outward-facing abstract features, ports, or access points as part of its external interface. This component defines an internal EMV2 error behavior model that includes a single error event named Failure, which is associated with the WBErrorSet error collection; the error behavior follows a two-state logic, where Operational is defined as the normal operating state and Failed is defined as the fault state. A single state transition t1 is defined for this behavior, which triggers a switch from the Operational state to the Failed state when the Failure error event is detected, with no reverse recovery transition defined. The GenericBrakeSystem.basic system implementation is defined as a minimal base implementation, with no nested subcomponents, internal feature declarations, connection bindings, or additional property and annex declarations contained in its structure.

Within the GenericFunction component, five dedicated error flow paths are defined, all configured as error sink paths that terminate at the corresponding inbound features. The first error flow path f1 terminates at the fromElectrical feature and carries errors of the AnyFunctionalError set; the second error flow path f2 terminates at the fromHydraulic feature and carries errors of the HydraulicErrors set; the third error flow path f3 terminates at the fromAlert feature and carries errors of the AnyFunctionalError set; the fourth error flow path f4 terminates at the fromSteering feature and carries errors of the AnyFunctionalError set; the fifth error flow path f5 terminates at the fromStatus feature and carries errors of the AnyFunctionalError set. No error propagation paths are defined to route errors from the inbound features to the interior of the GenericFunction component or to any outbound interface, meaning all inbound errors are contained at the feature boundary as terminal sink points with no further internal propagation. The GenericBrakeSystem component does not define any cross-port functional data flows or error flow paths, as it holds no external interface features; no data exchange across the component boundary is specified for this element, and all internal logic is limited to self-contained error state management.

No explicit scheduling protocols, periodic execution rules, priority assignments, or timing constraint definitions are specified for the basic implementations of both system components. Neither component is bound to a time-triggered, rate-monotonic, or priority-based preemptive scheduling mechanism, and no mandatory requirements for worst-case execution time, end-to-end transmission latency, dispatch jitter, or response time are defined for component operations. The state transition logic defined for GenericBrakeSystem operates in an event-triggered mode, where the transition from Operational to Failed is executed immediately upon detection of the Failure error event, with no required delay, timing offset, or transition latency specified for the process.

No custom AADL data type components are defined within the scope of the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package. All features exposed by the GenericFunction component are untyped abstract features, serving as generic access points without binding to specific structured data definitions. No standalone bus components or virtual bus components are declared within the package, and no explicit bus protocol, bus access rule, or physical communication medium is specified for inter-component communication via the exposed features, leaving communication mechanisms unconstrained at this package level. All error types, error sets, and error behavior models referenced in the package are imported from the external WBSFunctionalErrorLib library, including the AnyFunctionalError general functional error set, HydraulicErrors hydraulic domain error set, WBErrorSet wheel brake system error collection, and Twostate two-state error behavior definition; no local redefinition of these error model elements is included in the package.

The top-level public modeling package is located at the namespace path functional::WheelBrake::Main. This package declares explicit import dependencies on three external property and annex packages: WBSPS, EMV2, and ARP4761, alongside two sibling packages within the functional::WheelBrake namespace: functional::WheelBrake::Generic and functional::WheelBrake::CommandControl. The package defines three core system type hierarchies and two associated system implementation variants, structured to represent hierarchical wheel brake system functional elements. The first system type, NormalBrakeSystem, extends the GenericBrakeSystem type defined in the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to inherit all base structural and property characteristics of a generic brake system. The second system type, DecelerateOnGround, extends the GenericFunction type defined in the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to inherit all base structural and property characteristics of a generic system function, with one associated implementation variant labeled basic that extends the GenericFunction.basic implementation from the same Generic package. The third system type, DecelerateWheels, is defined as a standalone top-level functional system type with no parent type extension, with one associated implementation variant labeled basic. The NormalBrakeSystem element represents the normal operating mode brake function channel. The DecelerateOnGround element represents the integrated ground deceleration function that encapsulates normal, alternate, and emergency brake operating channels. The DecelerateWheels element represents the top-level wheel deceleration function that aggregates all relevant sub-functions for wheel speed management during ground operations. The DecelerateOnGround.basic implementation instantiates one NormalBrakeSystem instance to serve as the normal brake channel, alongside two instances of GenericBrakeSystem from the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to serve as the alternate and emergency brake channels respectively. The DecelerateWheels.basic implementation instantiates one DecelerateOnGround.basic instance to serve as the ground deceleration sub-function, one CommandControl.basic instance from the functional::WheelBrake::CommandControl package to serve as the directional control sub-function, and two instances of GenericFunction.basic from the functional::WheelBrake::Generic package to serve as the main landing gear stop function and unintended motion prevention function respectively. All system types marked with the WBSPS::IsFunction property set to true are classified as functional system elements. The NormalBrakeSystem type exposes two external input features, named fromHydraulic and fromBSCU. For error propagation interfaces, NormalBrakeSystem accepts incoming error propagations on the fromHydraulic feature limited to the HydraulicErrors error set, and accepts incoming error propagations on the fromBSCU feature covering the full AnyFunctionalError error set; both features act as dedicated error sink points for their respective incoming error sets. The DecelerateOnGround type explicitly declares one external input feature named fromBSCU, and inherits the full standard input feature set from its parent GenericFunction type, including features named fromElectrical, fromHydraulic, fromAlert, fromSteering, and fromStatus. For error propagation interfaces, DecelerateOnGround accepts incoming error propagations on the fromBSCU feature covering the AnyFunctionalError error set, with the fromBSCU feature acting as an error sink point for that error set. The DecelerateOnGround.basic implementation defines internal interface mappings that connect the parent implementation’s fromBSCU input feature directly to the fromBSCU feature of the internal normal brake subcomponent. Composite error behavior for DecelerateOnGround.basic defines that the component enters a Failed state if any of its three internal subcomponents (normal, alternate, emergency) enters its own Failed state. The DecelerateWheels type exposes five external input features, named fromElectrical, fromHydraulic, fromAlert, fromSteering, and fromStatus. For error propagation interfaces, DecelerateWheels accepts incoming error propagations on each input feature aligned to defined error sets: the fromElectrical feature carries AnyFunctionalError set propagations, the fromHydraulic feature carries HydraulicErrors set propagations, the fromAlert feature carries AnyFunctionalError set propagations, the fromSteering feature carries AnyFunctionalError set propagations, and the fromStatus feature carries AnyFunctionalError set propagations. The directionalcontrol subcomponent within DecelerateWheels.basic exposes a fromBSCU feature to support internal cross-connection to the decelerateonground subcomponent, and all four internal subcomponents within DecelerateWheels.basic inherit the standard five input features (fromElectrical, fromHydraulic, fromAlert, fromSteering, fromStatus) from their respective parent function types to accept incoming signals from the parent DecelerateWheels external interfaces. All inter-component connections within the package are implemented as unidirectional point-to-point feature connections. Within the DecelerateWheels.basic implementation, each external input feature is fanned out to all four internal subcomponents via dedicated connections: the external fromElectrical input routes to the fromElectrical feature of the decelerateonground, directionalcontrol, stopmainlanding, and preventmotion subcomponents; the external fromHydraulic input routes to the fromHydraulic feature of each of the four subcomponents; the external fromAlert input routes to the fromAlert feature of each of the four subcomponents; the external fromSteering input routes to the fromSteering feature of each of the four subcomponents; the external fromStatus input routes to the fromStatus feature of each of the four subcomponents. An additional internal cross-connection routes the fromBSCU feature of the directionalcontrol subcomponent to the fromBSCU input feature of the decelerateonground subcomponent, carrying brake command outputs from the directional control function to the ground deceleration function. Within the DecelerateOnGround.basic implementation, the incoming fromBSCU signal received from the directionalcontrol subcomponent is routed directly to the fromBSCU input of the normal brake subcomponent, with no direct connections defined from parent DecelerateOnGround inputs to the alternate or emergency brake subcomponents in this basic implementation variant. Error flow and behavior logic is defined for each component via EMV2 annex specifications. The NormalBrakeSystem component initializes in the Operational state, and defines three error-triggered state transitions: a transition to the Failed state with PartialSymmetricalWBLossAnunciated error effect when a HydraulicLossGreen error is received on the fromHydraulic feature, a transition to the Failed state with PartialSymmetricalWBLossAnunciated error effect when a HydraulicLossComponents error is received on the fromHydraulic feature, and a transition to the Failed state with TotalWBLossUnanunciated error effect when any functional error is received on the fromBSCU feature. The Failed state of NormalBrakeSystem has an associated occurrence distribution following a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.0e-4, calculated in accordance with AIR6110 guidance. For the DecelerateOnGround.basic implementation, the Failed state of the alternate brake subcomponent and the Failed state of the emergency brake subcomponent each have an associated occurrence distribution following a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 5.0e-3, per AIR6110 guidance. Composite error behavior for the DecelerateWheels.basic implementation defines two distinct Failed state effects tied to the state of the decelerateonground subcomponent and incoming error state on the fromAlert feature: a Failed state with TotalWBLossUnAnunciated effect is triggered when the decelerateonground subcomponent enters Failed state with no concurrent functional error present on the fromAlert feature, and a Failed state with TotalWBLossAnunciated effect is triggered when the decelerateonground subcomponent enters Failed state concurrently with any functional error present on the fromAlert feature. Hazard classifications per ARP4761 are assigned to each defined failure state of DecelerateWheels, aligned exactly to specified state bindings. The Failed.TotalWBLossAnunciated state is associated with the hazard describing unannunciated total loss of wheel braking, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, applicable during Landing and Rejected Takeoff flight phases, classified as Hazardous with a Remote qualitative probability objective, describing a scenario where crew detects brake failure only when the brakes are operated, then uses maximum available spoiler and thrust reverser capability, with potential for runway overrun. The Failed.TotalWBLossUnanunciated state is associated with two property assignments: first, the hazard describing annunciated total loss of wheel braking, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, applicable during the Landing flight phase, classified as Hazardous with a Remote qualitative probability objective, describing a scenario where crew is aware of brake failure prior to landing, allowing diversion to a suitable airport, notification of emergency ground support, and occupant preparation for overrun while using maximum available spoiler and thrust reverser capability; second, an occurrence distribution following a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 5.0e-7, defined per AIR6110 guidance. The Failed.PartialSymmetricalWBLossUnAnunciated state is associated with the hazard describing unannunciated partial symmetrical loss of wheel braking, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, applicable during Landing or Rejected Takeoff flight phases, classified as Hazardous with a Remote qualitative probability objective, describing a scenario where crew detects partial symmetrical brake loss upon brake application, uses maximum available braking, spoiler, and thrust reverser capability, with risk of brake overheating, wheel or fire failure, and potential runway overrun, with an attached note indicating potential catastrophic effect pending further analysis. The Failed.PartialSymmetricalWBLossanunciated state is associated with the hazard describing annunciated partial symmetrical loss of wheel braking, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, applicable during the Landing flight phase, classified as Major with a Remote qualitative probability objective, describing a scenario where crew is aware of partial symmetrical brake loss prior to landing, uses maximum available deceleration devices, with risk of brake overheating and potential runway overrun. No explicit temporal scheduling parameters, component dispatch protocols, execution time budgets, deadline values, end-to-end latency limits, or signal jitter constraints are defined for any component within this package. All inter-component feature connections represent immediate logical signal transfers without specified temporal buffering, delay, or scheduling arbitration requirements. No thread or process component types are defined within this package, as all elements represent abstract functional system components without mapped software or hardware execution resources. All inter-component features within this package are declared as untyped abstract feature elements, with no explicit structured data type definitions assigned to feature payloads within the package scope. No dedicated communication bus components, bus access interfaces, bus protocol definitions, or data serialization/deserialization rules are defined within this package; all inter-component interactions use direct point-to-point logical feature connections without reliance on an intermediate communication bus abstraction. All error type sets and error behavior state machine definitions referenced in EMV2 annex clauses are imported from the external WBSFunctionalErrorLib, including the HydraulicErrors and AnyFunctionalError error sets, the Twostate and TwostateWBS error behavior models, and all associated error state values used to specify component error transitions and composite error states. All property sets used for functional classification, error occurrence distribution modeling, and ARP4761 safety hazard assessment are imported as external dependencies without redefinition or extension within this package.

A standalone public AADL package named WBSImplementationErrorLib shall be constructed to serve as the dedicated error model definition library for the implementation layer of the wheel brake system. Only the standard EMV2 error model annex shall be embedded within the public scope of the package, and no other categories of AADL component structures shall be defined in the package. The error behavior definition units contained in the EMV2 annex of the package shall import the functional-layer error types defined in the separate external package WBSFunctionalErrorLib as a dependency. No other cross-package dependencies or circular package dependencies shall exist, and all definition elements within the package shall be publicly accessible for reference by other modeling packages associated with the wheel brake system.

This package functions as a static modeling metadata repository, and does not define runtime-capable components including hardware, software, process, or thread elements. Accordingly, no runtime interaction ports, bus access points, data access points, service provision points, or service request interfaces shall be configured. All error type and error behavior state machine definitions within the package shall be exposed as publicly referenceable modeling elements without access permission restrictions, for direct invocation when other components bind error models. No private internal interaction interfaces shall be defined in the package, and all definition elements shall reside at the public visibility level.

This package contains no definitions of runtime component instances, communication links, or data interaction paths, so no runtime cross-component data transmission or event-triggered data flow logic shall be specified. All elements within the package are static structural definitions for the modeling phase, and shall not participate in the data flow process during system runtime.

This package does not define schedulable runtime entities, communication transmission links, or temporal trigger logic. Accordingly, no temporal-related constraints including periodic scheduling rules, execution delay limits, communication transmission delay requirements, deadline restrictions, or priority configurations shall be specified. All error behavior state machines shall only describe the static structure of component state transition logic, and shall not be bound to specific temporal trigger conditions.

No communication bus types, bus instances, or associated bus access protocols shall be defined in the package. A structured error type system shall be defined within the EMV2 annex. Top-level independent error types with no parent type include AnyImplementationError, HydraulicLossBlue, HydraulicLossGreen, HydraulicLossComponents, SoftwareFailure, and HardwareFailure. AnyImplementationError serves as the abstract base type for all core implementation-layer functional errors of the wheel brake system, and relevant wheel brake function error types shall inherit directly or indirectly from this base type. The first-level subtypes directly inheriting from AnyImplementationError include NoService, TotalWBLoss, PartialSymmetricalWBLoss, AssymetricalWBLoss, and InadvertentWB. Among the second-level derived types, NoService acts as the intermediate base type for service-missing errors, and further derives two subtypes: NoValue and NoPower, which correspond to the failure scenarios of missing value output and missing power supply respectively. TotalWBLoss acts as the intermediate base type for total wheel brake loss errors, and further derives two subtypes: TotalWBLossAnunciated and TotalWBLossUnanunciated, which correspond to total wheel brake loss failure scenarios with active alarm notification and without active alarm notification respectively. PartialSymmetricalWBLoss acts as the intermediate base type for symmetrical partial wheel brake loss errors, and further derives two subtypes: PartialSymmetricalWBLossAnunciated and PartialSymmetricalWBLossUnanunciated, which correspond to symmetrical partial wheel brake loss failure scenarios with active alarm notification and without active alarm notification respectively. The independent top-level types HydraulicLossBlue, HydraulicLossGreen, and HydraulicLossComponents correspond to pressure loss failures of the blue hydraulic circuit, green hydraulic circuit, and generic hydraulic components respectively. The independent top-level types SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure correspond to generic software failure and generic hardware failure scenarios respectively, with no inheritance relationship to the AnyImplementationError base type. Two error set types shall be defined for batch failure scenario matching. The first set type is WBErrorSet, with fixed members including TotalWBLossAnunciated, TotalWBLossUnanunciated, PartialSymmetricalWBLoss, AssymetricalWBLoss, and InadvertentWB, covering all core wheel brake function failure scenarios. The second set type is HydraulicErrors, with fixed members including HydraulicLossBlue, HydraulicLossGreen, HydraulicLossComponents, and NoService, covering all failure scenarios related to the hydraulic pressure supply chain. Two reusable two-state error behavior state machine templates shall be defined in the package. The first template is named Twostate, which shall reference error type definitions from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, and configure two mutually exclusive states. The Operational state is set as the initial state, representing that the bound component is in a normal available operational state, while the failed state is a general failure state representing that the bound component is in an invalid unavailable state. The failure state of this state machine is not bound to a specific error type set, and can be reused as a basic two-state failure model for general system components. The second template is named TwostateWBS, which shall reference error type definitions from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, and configure two mutually exclusive states. The Operational state is set as the initial state, representing that bound wheel brake components are in a normal available operational state, while the Failed state is a hydraulic-related failure state. This Failed state shall be associated with the HydraulicErrors error set, meaning the state shall transition to the Failed state when the bound component triggers any error contained in the HydraulicErrors set. This state machine is dedicated for binding to components associated with the wheel brake hydraulic supply chain.

The top-level public package is named impl::bscu, which declares explicit import dependencies on the common package, platform package, Base_Types package, EMV2 annex library, and ARP4761 annex library to access shared data types, bus definitions, platform component models, error modeling constructs, and safety assessment property sets respectively. The package is structured in a hierarchical component composition model, containing two process component types with associated implementations, three system component types with a total of five associated implementations, including two extended implementation variants for different deployment platforms. Component dependency relationships follow a strict top-down hierarchy: the top-level brake system control unit (BSCU) system depends on instances of the BSCU subsystem component and the alternate selection logic component for redundant operation, each BSCU subsystem depends on instances of the command process and monitor process to execute core control and monitoring functions, and the federated and integrated modular avionics (IMA) deployment variants of the BSCU depend on corresponding platform components from the imported platform package to support processor resource binding. No circular dependencies are permitted across component boundaries.

All component functional interfaces are defined at the component type level, with implementation-specific extensions limited to internal subcomponents, connections, error behavior, and deployment properties. The command process type exposes three external data ports: one input data port named pedalvalue typed to common::command.pedal for incoming pedal position data, two output data ports named brake and skid typed to common::command.brake and common::command.skid respectively for generated brake and skid command outputs. The command.i process implementation adds no external functional features, and defines internal error propagation points including an implicit processor-facing input propagation point carrying SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure error types, an incoming NoService error propagation on the pedalvalue port, and outgoing NoValue error propagation on the brake and skid ports. The monitor process type exposes three external data ports: two input data ports named brake and skid typed to common::command.brake and common::command.skid respectively for incoming command data to validate, one output data port named valid typed to Base_Types::Boolean for validity status output. The monitor.i process implementation adds no external functional features, and defines internal error propagation points including an implicit processor-facing input propagation point carrying SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure error types, incoming NoValue error propagation on the brake and skid ports, outgoing NoValue error propagation on the valid port, plus an internal InvalidReport error event representing spontaneous incorrect validity reporting. The bscu_subsystem system type exposes five external interfaces: one required bus access port named pwr for connection to the common::power.generic power bus, one input data port named pedal typed to common::command.pedal for incoming pedal position data, two output data ports named cmd_brk and cmd_skid typed to common::command.brake and common::command.skid respectively for processed command outputs, one output data port named valid typed to Base_Types::Boolean for subsystem validity status. The bscu_subsystem.generic implementation encapsulates two internal subcomponents: one instance of monitor.i named mon, one instance of command.i named cmd, with internal port connections routing external pedal input to the command process, routing command process brake and skid outputs to the monitor process for validation, routing command process brake and skid outputs to the external cmd_brk and cmd_skid ports respectively, and routing monitor process validity output to the external valid port. The select_alternate system type exposes three external data ports: two input data ports named input1 and input2 typed to Base_Types::Boolean for incoming subsystem validity signals, one output data port named result typed to Base_Types::Boolean for alternate selection control output. The select_alternate component defines internal error propagation points including incoming NoValue error propagation on both input ports, outgoing NoValue error propagation on the result port, plus an internal InternalError event representing spontaneous incorrect selection behavior. The top-level bscu system type exposes seven external interfaces: two required bus access ports named pwr1 and pwr2 for connection to independent common::power.generic power buses, two input data ports named pedal1 and pedal2 typed to common::command.pedal for independent pedal position inputs to each redundant channel, one output data port named Select_Alternate typed to Base_Types::Boolean for subsystem selection control output, two output data ports named cmd_nor and cmd_alt typed to common::command.skid for normal and alternate mode skid command outputs respectively. The bscu.basic implementation provides a non-redundant configuration with no internal subcomponents, and adds incoming NoPower error propagation on both power access ports. The bscu.generic implementation encapsulates three internal subcomponents: two instances of bscu_subsystem.generic named sub1 (primary channel) and sub2 (alternate channel), one instance of select_alternate named select, with internal connections routing external power and pedal inputs to the corresponding BSCU subsystem, routing subsystem validity outputs to the select component inputs, routing select component output to the external Select_Alternate port, and routing subsystem skid command outputs to the corresponding external cmd_nor and cmd_alt ports; the subsystem brake command ports have no connection to top-level BSCU ports in this implementation. The bscu.federated implementation extends bscu.generic without modifying external interfaces, adding one internal subcomponent instance of platform::platform.federated named platform to represent federated avionics hardware. The bscu.ima implementation extends bscu.generic without modifying external interfaces, adding one internal subcomponent instance of platform::platform.ima named platform to represent integrated modular avionics hardware.

Nominal data flow through the system follows fixed, unidirectional paths from input interfaces to output interfaces, with no cyclic data paths. Power is supplied via independent external connections to pwr1 and pwr2, with power from pwr1 delivered exclusively to the primary BSCU subsystem sub1, and power from pwr2 delivered exclusively to the alternate BSCU subsystem sub2 to maintain power supply isolation between redundant channels. Pedal position data received on the pedal1 input is routed directly to the pedal input of sub1, while pedal position data received on the pedal2 input is routed directly to the pedal input of sub2 to maintain input signal isolation between redundant channels. Within each BSCU subsystem, incoming pedal data is passed to the pedalvalue input of the internal command process, which processes raw pedal position values to generate calibrated brake and skid command data. The brake and skid command data from the command process is split along two parallel paths: one path delivers the command data to the corresponding inputs of the internal monitor process for validity checking, while the other path delivers the brake command data to the subsystem cmd_brk port and skid command data to the subsystem cmd_skid port. The monitor process evaluates received brake and skid command data to confirm data integrity and validity, producing a Boolean validity signal that is routed to the external valid port of the BSCU subsystem. The validity signal from the primary subsystem sub1 is routed to the input1 port of the select_alternate component, while the validity signal from the alternate subsystem sub2 is routed to the input2 port of the select_alternate component. The select_alternate component executes fixed selection logic based exclusively on the primary subsystem validity signal received on input1: if the primary subsystem validity signal indicates valid operation (true value), the component outputs a false value on the result port to select the primary subsystem for active operation; if the primary subsystem validity signal indicates invalid operation (false value), the component outputs a true value on the result port to select the alternate subsystem for active operation. The validity signal from the alternate subsystem received on input2 is used solely for error detection purposes, with no impact on nominal selection logic. The result output of the select_alternate component is routed directly to the external Select_Alternate port of the top-level BSCU to communicate active channel status to downstream components. Skid command data from the primary subsystem sub1 is routed to the external cmd_nor output for delivery during normal primary operation, while skid command data from the alternate subsystem sub2 is routed to the external cmd_alt output for delivery during alternate backup operation. Error propagation flows follow defined paths aligned with nominal data connections: loss of pedal input service propagates into the command process, which transforms the NoService error to a NoValue error on outgoing brake and skid command ports; NoValue errors on command data ports propagate into the monitor process, which triggers a NoValue error on the outgoing validity port; loss of power to a BSCU subsystem propagates to trigger a NoValue error on the subsystem validity port; NoValue errors on both select_alternate inputs, or internal select component errors, trigger a NoValue error on the select result output. Composite error state logic for each BSCU subsystem defines a failed state if either the internal command or monitor process is in a failed state, and an operational state only if both processes are operational. Composite error state logic for the redundant bscu.generic, bscu.federated, and bscu.ima implementations defines a total failed state only if both BSCU subsystems are failed, an alternate operational state if the primary subsystem is failed and the alternate is operational, or if both subsystems are operational but the select component is failed, and a fully operational state only if both subsystems and the select component are operational.

Scheduling and resource allocation rules are defined via explicit processor binding properties for each deployment variant, with no implicit resource sharing permitted across bound execution contexts. For the bscu.federated deployment variant, the command and monitor processes of the primary subsystem sub1 are bound exclusively to the cpu1 processor of the federated platform, while the command and monitor processes of the alternate subsystem sub2 are bound exclusively to the cpu2 processor of the federated platform, establishing independent scheduling domains for each redundant channel on separate physical processors to eliminate cross-channel compute interference. For the bscu.ima deployment variant, the primary subsystem command process is bound exclusively to partition1 of the IMA platform CPU, the primary subsystem monitor process is bound exclusively to partition2 of the IMA platform CPU, the alternate subsystem command process is bound exclusively to partition3 of the IMA platform CPU, and the alternate subsystem monitor process is bound exclusively to partition4 of the IMA platform CPU, enforcing strict time and space partitioning between all four process instances per IMA scheduling rules to prevent cross-partition fault propagation. Error state transitions are event-driven, triggering immediately upon detection of a qualifying error condition without intentional delay: the command process transitions from operational to failed state immediately upon detection of a NoService error on the pedal input, or a SoftwareFailure or HardwareFailure from the hosting processor; the monitor process transitions from operational to failed state immediately upon detection of a NoValue error on brake or skid inputs, a SoftwareFailure or HardwareFailure from the hosting processor, or an internal InvalidReport event; each BSCU subsystem transitions from operational to failed state immediately upon detection of a NoPower error on the power input; the select_alternate component transitions from operational to failed state immediately upon detection of NoValue errors on both input ports simultaneously, or an internal InternalError event that causes an uncommanded switch to alternate mode; the non-redundant bscu.basic implementation transitions from operational to failed state immediately upon detection of a NoPower error on either individual power input, while the redundant bscu.generic, bscu.federated, and bscu.ima implementations transition to total failed state only upon detection of NoPower errors on both independent power inputs. Safety-related occurrence and classification constraints are defined per ARP4761 requirements: the InvalidReport event in the monitor process is classified as a Minor hazard with a Probable qualitative probability objective, representing an erroneous monitor report that could trigger an invalid switch to alternate mode; failure of a single BSCU subsystem is classified as a Major hazard with a Probable qualitative probability objective, with a fixed occurrence rate of 3.3e-5 per operational hour, with critical consequence only if both redundant subsystems fail simultaneously; the InternalError event in the select_alternate component is classified as a Hazardous hazard with an ExtremelyImprobable qualitative probability objective, with a Poisson distributed occurrence rate of 3.6e-6 per operational hour; loss of a single power supply line is classified as a Hazardous hazard with a Remote qualitative probability objective, with critical consequence only if both independent power supplies are lost.

All communication buses and data types used across the system are sourced from imported shared packages to ensure consistent type definition across the full system model. The only bus type used for power delivery is common::power.generic, which is accessed via required bus access ports on each BSCU subsystem, supporting unidirectional power delivery from external power sources to subsystem components, with a defined NoPower error state representing complete loss of bus supply. All data port communications use sampled, most-recent-value data transfer semantics with no event queuing, consistent with standard AADL data port behavior for periodic or sampled control systems. Data type assignments for all ports are fixed and cannot be modified without updating the shared type definitions: pedal position input ports use the common::command.pedal data type to represent raw pedal position measurements, brake command ports use the common::command.brake data type to represent calibrated brake command values, skid command ports use the common::command.skid data type to represent calibrated skid correction command values, all validity status ports and selection control ports use the Base_Types::Boolean data type to represent binary true/false state values. Error types associated with communication interfaces are sourced from the WBSImplementationErrorLib error library, with fixed propagation rules: pedal input ports carry the NoService error type to indicate absence of valid pedal input data, command and validity output ports carry the NoValue error type to indicate absence of valid output data, processor binding points carry SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure error types to indicate compute platform faults, power bus access points carry the NoPower error type to indicate loss of electrical supply. All safety property assignments adhere to ARP4761 standard definitions for hazard classification, probability objectives, and cross-referencing to system safety assessment artifacts.

The system shall define a standalone public shared package with the fully qualified identifier impl::common. All elements declared within this package shall be configured with public access permissions to support unobstructed cross-module reference by upper-layer functional components across the system. This package shall not declare dependencies on any other external packages, and shall function as the centralized storage location for universally reusable bus definitions and data type definitions required for full system modeling.

This common package shall only define foundational interaction carriers and data classification entities, and shall not contain executable functional component definitions including processes, threads, devices, subsystems, or abstract components. No dedicated external interaction ports, internal subcomponent slots, or pre-defined connection interfaces shall be specified within this package. All bus and data type entities defined in this package shall serve as standardized foundational interface elements that upper-layer functional components may instantiate and reference when constructing their own external service interfaces and internal interconnection interfaces.

This common package shall not define fixed end-to-end data flow paths, as it does not bind to specific functional execution nodes, hardware endpoints, or logical connection links. The transmission direction, source endpoints, destination endpoints, and data mapping rules for information carried by instances of the buses and data types defined in this package shall be explicitly specified by upper-layer business components during component implementation, subsystem integration, and system deployment stages.

This common package shall not attach fixed scheduling policies, periodic execution triggers, transmission latency budgets, response time requirements, or hard deadline constraints to the defined buses and data types, as these definitions are designed for universal reuse across diverse application scenarios. All timing, scheduling, and latency related constraints associated with deployed instances of these buses and data types shall be configured by upper-layer application components in alignment with specific business scenario performance requirements during system integration and deployment.

For communication bus definition rules, the system shall define a power bus type named power, paired with a generic implementation named power.generic. This bus type shall be used to carry electrical power supply transmission between connected system components, and the generic implementation shall be directly applicable to all general power supply scenarios that do not require customized transmission protocols or special signal characteristics. The system shall define a pulse width modulation bus type named pwm, paired with a generic implementation named pwm.generic. This bus type shall be used to carry pulse width modulation signal transmission between connected components, and the generic implementation shall be directly applicable to all general PWM signal interaction scenarios that do not require customized encoding rules or special timing configurations. The system shall define a pressure signal bus type named pressure, paired with a dedicated implementation named pressure.i. This bus type shall be used to carry pressure measurement and control signal transmission between field sensing devices, pump actuators, and other pressure-related components, and shall act as the mandatory standard carrier for all pressure-related interaction across the system. For data type definition rules, the system shall define a base control command data type named command, which serves as the parent type for all control command class data transmitted across the system. Four concrete, scenario-specific implementations shall be defined under the base command data type. The command.brake implementation shall be used to encapsulate and carry braking-related control instructions for vehicle deceleration and stopping functions. The command.skid implementation shall be used to encapsulate and carry control instructions for skid condition detection, response, and vehicle stability regulation functions. The command.pedal implementation shall be used to encapsulate and carry control instructions generated in response to driver accelerator or brake pedal operation inputs. The command.announce implementation shall be used to encapsulate and carry control instructions for in-vehicle audio announcement, status prompt, and human-machine interaction notification functions.

A public AADL package named impl::communication shall be defined, with explicit import dependencies on three external packages: the common package that provides shared public data type definitions, the EMV2 standard annex package that supplies formal error modeling constructs, and the ARP4761 standard annex package that provides aviation system safety assessment constructs. This package shall encapsulate components associated with system annunciation communication functions, and shall not contain nested sub-packages at the current abstraction level. A top-level device component typed as annunciation shall be declared within the package, alongside its corresponding device implementation identified as annunciation.i. The annunciation.i implementation shall maintain an empty internal structure at the current abstraction level, with no declared subcomponents, internal connections, or internal execution logic, serving only as a concrete instantiation carrier for the annunciation device type.

The annunciation device type shall define a single outward-facing unidirectional out data port named information as its only external feature, with no additional input ports, event ports, event data ports, bus access points, or subprogram access points declared on the device type. The information port shall be typed to carry data instances matching the announce data type defined under the command namespace of the imported common package. The annunciation.i device implementation shall not define additional external interfaces beyond those inherited from the annunciation device type, shall not declare internal private interfaces, and shall not define port mappings for non-existent internal subcomponents. An EMV2 annex shall be attached to the annunciation device type to formalize its error behavior, which shall import error type definitions from the WBSImplementationErrorLib error library, and reference the Twostate error behavior state machine definition from that same library to structure the device’s dual-state error model. Per the EMV2 error propagation configuration, the information out port shall support outward error propagation, allowing NoService category errors to be transmitted out of the device through this port.

The logical data and error flow associated with the annunciation device shall follow paths aligned with device operational state. When the device operates in a non-faulted state, valid annunciation command data conforming to the common::command.announce type specification shall be transmitted out of the device through the information port to connected downstream components. When the device enters a faulted state, no valid annunciation data shall be transmitted through the information port, and a NoService error state shall be propagated outward through the port to indicate total loss of annunciation capability; this fault represents a communication-related error source that propagates to the top-level system for inclusion in system-level fault tree analysis aligned with ARP4761 guidance, at a level of abstraction sufficient to represent annunciation capability loss without requiring detailed lower-level communication mechanism modeling. A dedicated error flow path identified as f1 shall be defined within the EMV2 annex to mark the NoService error present on the information port as an error source originating directly from the annunciation device itself, with no cross-subcomponent error transfer paths defined given the empty internal structure of the annunciation.i implementation.

At the current abstraction level, no periodic scheduling rules, execution time budgets, data transmission latency constraints, or hardware binding rules for processors, memory, or buses shall be defined for the annunciation device or its annunciation.i implementation. The device’s error behavior state machine shall follow explicit transition and propagation rules: the device shall initialize in the Operational working state as defined by the referenced Twostate behavior model, and shall transition to the Failed state via transition t1 immediately when the internal LossAnnunciation error event is triggered. When the device resides in the Failed state, it shall unconditionally propagate a NoService error to the information port via propagation rule p1, with no additional triggering events or guard conditions required for this error propagation. The LossAnnunciation error event shall be assigned an EMV2 OccurrenceDistribution property, following a Fixed distribution type with a probability value of 1.00. Per ARP4761 safety assessment requirements, the LossAnnunciation error event shall be associated with a formal hazard record: the hazard shall carry a cross-reference to AIR6110 and ARP4761 documentation, specifically aligned with the fault tree construct for annunciation loss defined on page 199, figure L.3 of the ARP4761 standard, the failure condition shall be titled "Loss of Annunciation", the hazard shall apply across all system operational phases, the hazard effect shall be described as total inability of the system to annunciate error conditions, the failure condition classification shall be set to Catastrophic, the associated qualitative probability objective shall be set to Extremely Improbable, and no additional comment text shall be attached to the hazard record.

The impl::communication package shall not define custom native data types for inter-component communication, and shall instead reuse the pre-defined common::command.announce data type from the imported common package for all payload data transmitted through the information port. All data and error transfer associated with the device shall be modeled via abstract data port connections at the current abstraction level. The package shall not define dedicated physical bus components, virtual bus components, or custom bus protocol specifications, and no explicit bus binding properties shall be assigned to the information port at this level of design abstraction, as the port serves only as an abstract representation of internal system communication for annunciation data.

The system shall define a publicly accessible AADL package named impl::pedals to encapsulate all model elements related to the pedal input unit. This package shall declare explicit import dependencies on two external packages: the common package to access shared command data type definitions, and the ARP4761 package to access standardized aviation safety assessment property sets. The impl::pedals package shall contain one top-level system component type named pedals, which represents a stub representation of the pedal input hardware, and one corresponding system implementation instance named pedals.generic that realizes the pedals system type.

The pedals system type shall expose two external outbound data port features for inter-component communication. The first port, designated signal1, shall be defined as an out data port typed to the common::command.pedal data type. The second port, designated signal2, shall be defined as an out data port also typed to the common::command.pedal data type. Both outbound ports shall support declared outbound propagation of the NoService error state to enable formal safety analysis. The pedals.generic system implementation shall not define any internal subcomponents, internal connection paths, private features, or subcomponent-level property assignments, consistent with its purpose as a minimal stub component.

The pedals component shall operate as an originating source of pedal command data for downstream aircraft braking system components. During normal operation, pedal position command data generated by the pedal unit shall be transmitted outward through both signal1 and signal2 data ports to connected receiving components, with no inbound data or event flows defined for the component. For safety-related error flows, the component shall define two distinct error source paths: the first error flow, identified as f1, shall treat the signal1 port as an originating source of the NoService error state, and the second error flow, identified as f2, shall treat the signal2 port as an originating source of the NoService error state, with no internal error propagation waypoints defined between component internal states and the port error outputs.

The pedals component shall implement error behavior aligned with the Twostate behavior definition sourced from the WBSImplementationErrorLib library, and shall reference error type definitions from the same WBSImplementationErrorLib library for error state and event specification. The component shall define a single internal error event named InternalFault that triggers operational state transitions. The component shall default to the Operational state during normal function, where valid pedal command data is transmitted across both output ports. Upon occurrence of the InternalFault event, the component shall execute an immediate state transition from the Operational state to the Failed state. When in the Failed state, the component shall unconditionally propagate the NoService error state out through both signal1 and signal2 ports, with no additional guard conditions or processing delay applied to this error propagation. The NoService error condition present on both signal1 and signal2 ports shall be mapped to an ARP4761 hazard entry classified as Catastrophic, with a qualitative probability objective of ExtremelyImprobable. The hazard shall be documented as a total loss of pedal signal input that prevents the BSCU from generating valid brake control outputs, with an associated comment noting the condition reaches critical severity in the event of dual power supply loss. All hazard cross-reference identifiers, applicable operational flight phases, and associated detailed reference fields shall be marked as TBD for subsequent design refinement. No explicit periodic scheduling rules, execution deadline constraints, data transmission latency limits, or clock synchronization requirements shall be defined for the pedals.generic stub implementation, with such timing parameters reserved for definition in future detailed, non-stub implementations of the pedal component.

All data transmitted across the signal1 and signal2 output ports shall strictly conform to the structure and semantics of the common::command.pedal data type defined in the imported common package. No custom data type definitions shall be declared within the impl::pedals package, as all interface data types are sourced from shared common definitions. No dedicated communication bus components, bus access features, or protocol binding rules shall be defined within the impl::pedals package, as the generic stub implementation uses unbound direct data port interfaces for signal transmission without explicit underlying communication network specification.

The modeled platform domain is encapsulated within the impl::platform package, which explicitly imports the EMV2 error modeling annex library and ARP4761 safety assessment property library as mandatory external dependencies. All error behavior definitions within the package rely on types and behavior constructs from the external WBSImplementationErrorLib error library, specifically its Twostate dual-state error behavior state machine and associated error type set. The package defines a hierarchical component structure starting with the virtual processor type partition and its generic, feature-free implementation partition.generic, the processor type cpu and its two architecture-specific implementations, namely cpu.ima for integrated modular avionics deployments and cpu.single for federated architecture deployments, as well as the abstract top-level system type platform and its two corresponding concrete implementations, namely platform.ima for IMA platform configurations and platform.federated for federated platform configurations. No additional component types, implementations, or library elements are defined within the package scope.

For component external interfaces and internal structural specifications, the virtual processor partition type defines two error propagation ports: an outbound propagation port named bindings that supports transmission of SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure error types, and an inbound propagation port named processor that supports reception of HardwareFailure error types. Internally, the partition component declares a SoftwareFailure error event, initializes to the Operational state upon activation, and triggers a state transition to the Failed state when the SoftwareFailure event occurs. When operating in the Operational state, the component propagates a NoError status through the outbound bindings port; when operating in the Failed state, the component propagates a SoftwareFailure error through the same bindings port. The partition.generic implementation is a general-purpose realization of the partition type that adds no supplementary subcomponents, ports, properties, or behavior logic beyond the definitions inherited from the base partition type. The processor cpu type defines a single outbound error propagation port named bindings that supports transmission of HardwareFailure error types. Internally, the cpu component declares an InternalFailure error event, initializes to the Operational state upon activation, and triggers a state transition to the Failed state when the InternalFailure event occurs. When operating in the Operational state, the component propagates a NoError status through the outbound bindings port; when operating in the Failed state, the component propagates a HardwareFailure error through the same bindings port. The cpu.ima implementation, built to support IMA architecture configurations, contains four identical virtual processor subcomponents named partition1, partition2, partition3, and partition4, each instantiating the partition.generic implementation. This processor implementation does not define independent software failure propagation logic at the processor hardware level, as all software-related failure behavior is encapsulated within the nested partition subcomponents. The cpu.single implementation, built to support federated architecture configurations, inherits the base cpu type’s bindings port for hardware failure propagation, and adds an additional outbound error propagation port named processor that supports transmission of SoftwareFailure error types. Internally, this implementation declares a dedicated SoftwareFailure error event, propagates a NoError status through the processor port when in the Operational state, triggers a state transition from Operational to Failed when the SoftwareFailure event occurs, and propagates a SoftwareFailure error through the processor port when in the Failed state. This implementation contains no nested virtual processor partition subcomponents. The top-level platform system type acts as an abstract root for platform configurations, with no predefined external ports or internal subcomponents at the type level. The platform.ima implementation, representing a complete IMA platform, contains a single processor subcomponent named cpu that instantiates the cpu.ima processor implementation. The platform.federated implementation, representing a complete federated platform, contains two processor subcomponents named cpu1 and cpu2, both of which instantiate the cpu.single processor implementation.

For system propagation flow paths, the partition component defines two dedicated error flows. The first flow, named fsoft, acts as an error source that routes internally triggered SoftwareFailure events directly outward through the bindings port. The second flow, named fhard, acts as a pass-through error path that routes HardwareFailure errors received on the inbound processor port directly outward through the bindings port, with no internal error transformation, filtering, or aggregation applied. The base cpu component defines a single error source flow named f1 that routes HardwareFailure errors caused by internal InternalFailure events directly outward through the bindings port. The cpu.single implementation defines an additional error source flow named fsoft that routes internally triggered SoftwareFailure events directly outward through the dedicated processor error propagation port. All defined error flows follow unidirectional propagation rules aligned with port directionality.

For timing, scheduling, and associated constraint specifications, all platform components use an event-triggered execution model for both operational state management and error state transitions, with no defined periodic scheduling policies, task worst-case execution time budgets, or end-to-end communication latency requirements specified for platform elements. All declared error events adhere to defined occurrence probability distributions: the SoftwareFailure event on partition components follows a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5, the InternalFailure event on base cpu components follows a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5, and the SoftwareFailure event on cpu.single implementations follows a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5. In compliance with ARP4761 safety assessment requirements, each of the three defined error events is assigned a Major failure condition classification, a Probable qualitative probability objective, and applicability across all system operational phases. The SoftwareFailure event on partition components corresponds to platform software faults such as operating system exceptions, with an impact scope covering all software components managed by the affected partition. The InternalFailure event on cpu components corresponds to hardware faults affecting processors or attached peripheral devices, with an impact scope covering all software components bound to the affected hardware resource. The SoftwareFailure event on cpu.single implementations corresponds to platform software faults such as operating system exceptions, with an impact scope covering all software components controlled by the affected processor. All hazard entries carry a to-be-determined cross-reference identifier, an empty formal failure identifier field, and descriptive comment text documenting impact scope at the initial modeling stage.

For data type and communication bus definition rules, no custom application-level data types are declared within the package. All values transmitted across component error propagation ports are typed as error constructs imported from the external WBSImplementationErrorLib library, consisting of three discrete valid values: NoError, SoftwareFailure, and HardwareFailure. No dedicated communication bus components, bus protocol specifications, or bus access policy definitions are included within the package, as all modeled interactions are limited to error propagation between hierarchically nested platform components, with no explicit modeling of general-purpose communication fabric for application data exchange.

The system shall define a public AADL package identified as impl::power. This package shall import three required external packages to access pre-defined shared constructs: the common package containing generic cross-package resource specifications, the ARP4761 package containing standardized aviation safety and hazard assessment property definitions, and the EMV2 package containing error modeling language constructs and associated reliability properties. The package shall declare two top-level component types, each paired with a single concrete implementation definition. The first component is categorized as a hardware device, named battery, with a corresponding implementation named battery.generic that contains no internal subcomponents or internal connections. The second component is categorized as a system, named power, with a corresponding implementation named power.generic. The power.generic implementation shall instantiate two identical device subcomponents of type battery.generic, labeled battery1 and battery2, which operate as independent redundant power supply units with no additional nested subcomponents.

The battery device type shall expose one core functional feature: a provided bus access port named socket, typed to match the common::power.generic bus defined in the imported common package. The battery device shall implement EMV2 error modeling constructs that import error type definitions from WBSImplementationErrorLib and reference the Twostate error behavior specification from WBSImplementationErrorLib. The battery device shall define formal error propagation interfaces, including an outbound propagation path for NoPower errors transmitted via the socket port, and an outbound propagation path for AnyImplementationError transmitted via component binding paths. The battery device shall define two root error flow sources: error flow f1 that sources NoPower errors at the socket port, and error flow f2 that sources AnyImplementationError at the component binding layer. The battery device shall define two internal error events: the Depleted event indicating complete discharge of stored electrical energy, and the Explode event indicating catastrophic structural failure of the battery unit. The battery device shall implement a two-state error behavior state machine with two mutually exclusive states: the Operational state representing normal, fully functional operation, and the Failed state representing total loss of intended power supply function. Defined state transitions for the battery shall include a transition from Operational to Failed triggered by occurrence of the Depleted event, and a transition from Operational to Failed triggered by occurrence of the Explode event. Formal error propagation rules for the battery shall specify that the Failed state propagates the NoPower error via the socket port with no conditional guard, and the Operational state propagates the NoError status via the socket port with no conditional guard. Safety and reliability properties for the battery shall be assigned in compliance with ARP4761 and EMV2 requirements. The NoPower error propagated from the socket port shall carry ARP4761 hazard attributes including a cross-reference to ARP4761 page 277 figure 9, a failure mode description of single power source loss that presents critical risk if both primary and redundant power sources are lost, applicability to Landing and RTO flight phases, a hazard description of total electrical power loss to the BSCU, a FailureConditionClassification value of Major, a QualitativeProbabilityObjective value of Probable, and supporting notation that the condition becomes a major hazard when both power sources are lost. The NoPower error at the socket port shall have an EMV2 OccurrenceDistribution property specifying a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5. The Explode error event shall carry ARP4761 hazard attributes including a TBD cross-reference, a failure mode description of battery explosion, applicability to all flight phases, a hazard description of battery explosion as a high-severity hazard, a FailureConditionClassification value of Catastrophic, a QualitativeProbabilityObjective value of ExtremelyImprobable, and supporting notation that the failure causes physical impact to adjacent surrounding components. The Depleted error event shall carry ARP4761 hazard attributes including a TBD cross-reference, a failure mode description of battery charge depletion, applicability to all flight phases, a hazard description of total loss of stored battery energy, a FailureConditionClassification value of Major, a QualitativeProbabilityObjective value of Probable, and supporting notation that the condition presents operational risk if the redundant battery unit also experiences failure. The power system type shall expose two core functional features: two provided bus access ports named line1 and line2, both typed to match the common::power.generic bus defined in the imported common package. The power system shall implement EMV2 error modeling constructs that import error type definitions from WBSImplementationErrorLib and reference the Twostate error behavior specification from WBSImplementationErrorLib. The power system shall define a formal error propagation interface for outbound propagation of AnyImplementationError transmitted via system binding paths, with one root error flow source f0 that sources AnyImplementationError at the system binding layer. The power.generic system implementation shall define two bidirectional bus access connections: connection pwr1 shall link the socket port of subcomponent battery1 to the external system port line1, and connection pwr2 shall link the socket port of subcomponent battery2 to the external system port line2, with no additional internal port connections defined.

Functional power flow within the power.generic implementation shall follow fully isolated, non-interacting redundant paths. Subcomponent battery1 shall supply electrical power exclusively through its socket port, routed via connection pwr1 to the external line1 port for access by connected external consuming systems. Subcomponent battery2 shall supply electrical power exclusively through its socket port, routed via connection pwr2 to the external line2 port for access by connected external consuming systems. No cross-connection, load sharing, or power switching logic shall exist between the two power paths, ensuring fully independent operation of the two supply channels. Error flow within the system shall follow direct, unfiltered propagation paths. Errors generated by internal battery error events shall trigger the defined state transitions in the battery error behavior model, with resulting port-level errors passed directly along the dedicated bus connections to the corresponding external system ports. No system-level error filtering, conversion, masking, or redundancy management logic shall be applied to errors propagated from the battery subcomponents. Implementation errors originating at the binding layers of battery1, battery2, or the top-level power system shall propagate outward via their respective binding paths without modification or aggregation.

All components defined within the impl::power package represent statically deployed hardware elements for electrical power delivery, with no software execution entities such as threads, processes, or scheduled subprograms included in the package structure. No periodic scheduling, priority-based preemption, or time-partitioned execution rules shall apply to these components. All error event detection and associated state transitions shall occur as immediate, event-triggered responses with no mandated execution latency budget. Error propagation along bus connections and binding paths shall occur instantaneously, with no defined minimum or maximum transmission delay requirements for power delivery or error signaling.

The impl::power package shall not define custom abstract data types or custom bus types. All power transmission across component boundaries shall use the imported common::power.generic bus as the sole communication medium. All bus access connections shall support bidirectional access semantics to align with the provided bus access port configuration. The common::power.generic bus shall carry continuous electrical power as its primary service payload, with no defined discrete application data exchange, message framing, or higher-level protocol requirements for communication across the bus.

The system shall define a public AADL package named impl::pump. This package shall declare explicit import dependencies on three external modeling packages, including the common shared definition package, the ARP4761 safety standard property package, and the EMV2 error modeling annex package. The impl::pump package shall contain one top-level system type definition named pump, and one matching system implementation definition named pump.i.
