The pump.i system implementation shall not include internal subcomponent declarations, internal connection definitions, or internal subcomponent binding configurations in the current modeling scope.

The pump system type shall define its external functional interface as a single provided bus access feature named pressure_output. The pump system shall define two outward-facing error propagation points as part of its error modeling interface. The first outward error propagation point is named bindings, which is associated with component implementation binding layers, and shall support propagation of all implementation-level error categories. The second outward error propagation point is mapped directly to the pressure_output functional feature, and shall support propagation of service loss errors. The pump system shall define two top-level error source flow specifications for its error interface: the first error source flow, named nopressure, shall originate at the pressure_output propagation point and carry service loss errors; the second error source flow, named nopressurefunc, shall originate at the bindings propagation point and carry all implementation-level error categories. The pump.i system implementation shall not define any internal private interfaces, as no internal subcomponents are present in the implementation structure.

For functional service flow, the pump component shall provide accessible pressure bus service to external connected components through the pressure_output provided bus access port during normal operation. For error propagation flow, when the component operates without fault, no functional error shall be passed to external components through the pressure_output port, and no binding layer error shall be propagated through the bindings point. When the component encounters an internal hydraulic fault, corresponding error signals shall propagate outward through the two defined error propagation points to reach connected system components and platform binding layers, without blocking or internal error consumption within the pump component. No internal data transformation or routing logic shall be defined in the pump.i implementation, as the component operates as a standalone service provider with no internal subcomponent data exchange paths.

The pump component shall implement a two-state error behavior state machine aligned with the Twostate behavior definition imported from the WBSImplementationErrorLib error library. The component shall initialize to the Operational state upon system power-up and normal startup. The component shall define one internal error event named HydraulicError, which triggers an immediate state transition from the Operational state to the Failed state, with no intermediate wait states or transitional processing steps permitted. No recovery transition from the Failed state back to the Operational state shall be implemented in the current model. When the component remains in the Operational state, it shall continuously propagate a NoError status through the pressure_output error propagation point with no added propagation delay. When the component enters the Failed state, it shall immediately propagate a NoService error through the pressure_output point and an AnyImplementationError through the bindings point, with zero added processing delay for error propagation per the model definition. The HydraulicError event and the associated NoService error propagation on the pressure_output port shall follow a Poisson occurrence distribution, with a fixed probability value of 2.5e-5 per defined operational exposure interval. The HydraulicError event shall be associated with a hazard assessment per ARP4761 requirements, with a cross-reference to ARP4761 page 275 figure L9, a failure description of Hydraulic Error on a pump, applicable operational phases marked as to be determined, a hazard description of Loss of one pump, a failure condition classification of Major, a qualitative probability objective of Probable, and an associated comment noting that a Major hazard condition arises only when both pumps in the overall system experience loss of function.

The pressure_output provided bus access feature shall be bound to the common::pressure.i bus definition imported from the common package, which defines the physical and logical communication rules for pressure-related signal transmission between the pump and connected external components. All error types used in the pump error model shall be imported from the WBSImplementationErrorLib error type library, including the NoService error type for functional service loss, the AnyImplementationError type for binding layer implementation faults, and the NoError type for normal fault-free operation. No custom local data type or bus type definitions shall be declared within the impl::pump package, as all interface and communication type definitions are sourced from imported external packages.

The module set for the valve domain is encapsulated within the impl::valves package, which declares explicit dependencies on two external public packages: the base_types package for fundamental data type definitions, and the common package for shared bus and skid command data type definitions. All component type and implementation definitions are contained in the public section of the package to support unconstrained external reference. The component hierarchy follows a single-inheritance structure to reuse common interface and behavior definitions. A base generic valve system type is defined as the common parent for three specialized valve variants: the generic_pwm_input valve with added PWM control input, the boolean_shutoff valve with added binary shutoff control, and the cmd_shutoff valve with added skid command shutoff control. A base selector system type is defined as the common parent for two specialized pressure selector variants: the selector_basic unit with single consolidated pressure output, and the selector_detailed unit with dual independent channel pressure outputs. System implementation definitions are provided for three of the system types: the base generic valve (generic.i), the PWM-input generic valve (generic_pwm_input.i), and the base selector (selector.i). All three existing implementations contain no internal subcomponents, port groups, connection structures, or internal behavior specifications. The boolean_shutoff valve, cmd_shutoff valve, selector_basic, and selector_detailed system types are defined as formal type specifications only, with no corresponding implementation provided in the current package version.

Each component defines explicit external interfaces aligned with its functional role, with standardized error propagation and behavior specifications defined via the EMV2 annex. All error type definitions referenced across components are sourced from the external WBSImplementationErrorLib; components that define state-based error behavior additionally reference the two-state (Operational/Failed) behavior model from the same library. The base generic valve exposes two bus access ports: an input port with requires bus access semantics to connect to an upstream pressure bus, and an output port with provides bus access semantics to expose pressure output to downstream components. Its error propagation specification defines that the input port may receive incoming NoService errors, the output port may propagate outgoing NoService errors, and a direct error flow path carries NoService errors from the input port to the output port. The generic.i implementation of the base valve adds no additional interfaces or internal structure. The generic_pwm_input valve inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base generic valve, and adds one additional requires bus access port named input_pwm to connect to a generic PWM control bus, with no supplementary error propagation or behavior rules; its generic_pwm_input.i implementation contains no extra internal structure or interface definitions. The boolean_shutoff valve inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base generic valve, and adds one additional input data port named boolean_input typed to Base_Types::Boolean to receive binary shutoff control signals, with no supplementary error propagation or behavior rules, and no provided implementation in the current package. The cmd_shutoff valve inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base generic valve, and adds one additional input data port named cmd_input typed to common::command.skid to receive skid-related shutoff commands. Its error propagation specification defines that the cmd_input port may receive incoming NoValue errors, an error flow path maps NoValue errors on cmd_input to NoService errors on the pressure output port, and the pressure output port may act as an originating source of NoService errors. Its component error behavior, based on the two-state model, defines an initial Operational state, with transitions to a Failed state triggered by either NoValue errors on the cmd_input port or NoService errors on the pressure input port; when in the Failed state, the component unconditionally propagates NoService errors out of the pressure output port. No implementation is provided for the cmd_shutoff valve in the current package. The base selector system exposes three requires bus access ports for pressure inputs: accumulator_input to connect to the accumulator pressure bus, green_input to connect to the green hydraulic system pressure bus, and blue_input to connect to the blue hydraulic system pressure bus. It also exposes three input data ports: select_alternate typed to Base_Types::Boolean to receive alternate source selection control signals, cmd_nor typed to common::command.skid to receive normal channel control commands, and cmd_alt typed to common::command.skid to receive alternate channel control commands. Its error propagation specification defines that the three control data ports may receive incoming NoValue errors, the three pressure input bus ports may receive incoming NoService errors, and all NoValue errors arriving on the three control data ports are treated as error sinks that terminate within the component without outward propagation. The selector.i implementation of the base selector adds no additional interfaces or internal structure. The selector_basic variant inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base selector, and adds one additional provides bus access port named output to deliver selected pressure output to downstream components. Its error propagation specification defines that the output port may propagate outgoing NoService errors, with direct error flow paths carrying NoService errors from each of the three pressure input ports to the single output port. No implementation is provided for selector_basic in the current package. The selector_detailed variant inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base selector, and adds two additional provides bus access ports: green_output to deliver pressure for the green hydraulic channel, and blue_output to deliver pressure for the blue hydraulic channel. Its error propagation specification defines that both output ports may propagate outgoing NoService errors, with mapped error flow paths as follows: NoService errors on green_input propagate to green_output, NoService errors on blue_input propagate to blue_output, NoService errors on accumulator_input propagate to both green_output and blue_output, NoValue errors on cmd_alt propagate to blue_output as NoService errors, NoValue errors on cmd_nor propagate to green_output as NoService errors, and NoValue errors on select_alternate propagate to both green_output and blue_output as NoService errors. Its component error behavior, based on the two-state model, defines an initial Operational state, with transitions to a Failed state triggered by NoValue errors on the select_alternate, cmd_alt, or cmd_nor ports; when in the Failed state, the component unconditionally propagates NoService errors out of both green_output and blue_output ports. No implementation is provided for selector_detailed in the current package.

Functional data flow across all components follows the expected signal paths of a hydraulic valve control system. For all valve types derived from the base generic valve, the core functional flow carries pressure signals from the upstream pressure bus connected to the input port, through the valve’s internal regulation and shutoff logic, to the downstream pressure bus exposed via the output port. The generic_pwm_input valve supplements this core pressure flow with PWM control signals received via the input_pwm bus port, which are used to modulate the valve’s opening level and pressure output. The boolean_shutoff valve supplements the core pressure flow with binary shutoff signals received via the boolean_input data port, which trigger a full block of the pressure output path when the shutoff condition is asserted. The cmd_shutoff valve supplements the core pressure flow with skid command signals received via the cmd_input data port, which trigger a full block of the pressure output path when a valid shutoff command is received. For selector components, the base selector accepts three independent pressure inputs and three control inputs as the complete signal set for pressure source selection logic. The selector_basic variant uses the received alternate selection signal and channel commands to select one of the three input pressure sources, and routes the selected pressure signal to the single output pressure bus port for downstream consumption. The selector_detailed variant uses the received alternate selection signal and channel commands to independently select pressure sources for the green and blue hydraulic channels, routing processed pressure for the green channel to the green_output port and processed pressure for the blue channel to the blue_output port. Error flow follows explicitly defined propagation paths aligned with expected failure modes. For the base generic valve, NoService errors on the pressure input pass directly through to the pressure output with no masking or transformation. For the cmd_shutoff valve, NoValue errors on the command input and NoService errors on the pressure input both trigger a component failure state that generates NoService errors on the pressure output, and the output may also generate NoService errors as an internal fault source. For the base selector, all NoValue errors on control input ports are contained within the component with no outward propagation, regardless of component state. For the selector_basic variant, NoService errors on any of the three pressure inputs pass directly through to the single pressure output with no masking. For the selector_detailed variant, NoService errors on the dedicated green and blue pressure inputs pass directly to their corresponding channel outputs, NoService errors on the accumulator input propagate to both channel outputs, NoValue errors on control inputs either propagate directly to associated outputs as NoService errors or trigger a global component failure that propagates NoService errors to both channel outputs simultaneously.

No internal threads, processes, scheduled subcomponents, or execution timeline constructs are defined in any of the current system type specifications or existing implementations, so no internal scheduling priority, dispatch period, execution time, deadline, or jitter constraints are specified for component internal logic. All defined error propagation paths follow zero-delay instantaneous propagation semantics with no added latency or buffering requirements. Communication across all data ports and bus access ports carries no explicit custom latency constraints, and all signal transmission timings align with the native timing specifications of the connected external buses and imported data types. No end-to-end latency budgets are defined for pressure or control signal paths across any of the valve or selector components in the current package.

All data types used by components in the package are imported from external packages, with no custom data type definitions contained within the impl::valves package. Boolean control signals for shutoff and source selection use the Boolean type defined in the base_types package, while skid command signals for channel control use the command.skid type defined in the common package. All data ports use standard unqueued AADL data port communication semantics with no custom data representation, encoding, endianness, or refresh rate rules specified at the component level. All pressure signal interactions use the pressure.i bus defined in the common package, while all PWM control interactions use the pwm.generic bus defined in the common package. Bus connections follow standard requires/provides access semantics consistent with bidirectional client-server interaction models, where pressure buses carry hydraulic pressure measurement and actuation signals or their equivalent digital representations, and PWM buses carry pulse-width modulated valve actuation control signals. No custom bus protocol, baud rate, electrical characteristic, data framing, or access arbitration rules are defined within the package; components only expose access points to connect to externally defined buses without modifying inherent bus properties or behavior.

The top-level software and hardware package for the wheel brake system shall be defined under the namespace impl::wbs, with public access to all contained elements, and shall declare explicit import dependencies on seven external supporting packages: impl::bscu for brake system control unit components, impl::communication for annunciation device components, impl::valves for all hydraulic valve assembly components, impl::wheel for wheel brake assembly components, impl::pump for hydraulic pump components, impl::power for electrical power supply components, and impl::pedals for pilot brake pedal input components. No private package sections shall be defined for the impl::wbs package. An abstract system type named wbs shall be defined as the root type for all wheel brake system variants, with no inherent features, properties, or subcomponents declared at the type level to support flexible extension across implementation variants. Four concrete system implementations shall be defined under the wbs system type, following a hierarchical extension structure where wbs.generic serves as the common base implementation for all variants, wbs.basic and wbs.detailed directly extend wbs.generic to implement simplified and high-fidelity hydraulic architectures respectively, and wbs.federated and wbs.ima directly extend wbs.detailed to implement federated and integrated modular avionics deployment architectures for the brake system control unit. The base wbs.generic implementation shall define a fixed set of subcomponents retained across all extending variants, including a pedal input subsystem typed as impl::pedals::pedals.generic, an electrical power subsystem typed as impl::power::power.generic, two primary hydraulic pump systems typed as impl::pump::pump.i designated blue_pump and green_pump for the two independent hydraulic supply circuits, an accumulator backup pump system typed as impl::pump::pump.i designated accumulator for emergency pressure supply, an abstract selector valve assembly typed as impl::valves::selector, a generic brake system control unit typed as impl::bscu::bscu.generic designated bscu, an abstract wheel brake assembly typed as impl::wheel::wheel, and a fault annunciation device typed as impl::communication::annunciation.i designated annunciation. The wbs.basic implementation shall apply type extension substitution rules to refine three inherited subcomponents from the base generic implementation, replacing the generic bscu with the basic BSCU variant impl::bscu::bscu.basic, replacing the abstract selector with the simplified selector assembly impl::valves::selector_basic, and replacing the abstract wheel assembly with the single-input wheel variant impl::wheel::wheel_one_input.i, with no additional subcomponents added beyond the refined inherited elements. The wbs.detailed implementation shall apply type extension substitution rules to refine two inherited subcomponents from the base generic implementation, replacing the abstract selector with the high-fidelity detailed selector assembly impl::valves::selector_detailed, and replacing the abstract wheel assembly with the dual-input wheel variant impl::wheel::wheel_two_inputs.i, and shall add three new hydraulic valve subcomponents not present in the base implementation: a boolean-actuated shutoff valve typed as impl::valves::boolean_shutoff designated shutoff for gating the green hydraulic circuit supply, and two command-actuated shutoff valves typed as impl::valves::cmd_shutoff designated green_skid and blue_skid to provide anti-skid modulation for the green and blue hydraulic circuits respectively. The wbs.federated implementation shall inherit all subcomponents and structural elements from wbs.detailed, with a single type refinement to replace the inherited BSCU subcomponent with the federated BSCU variant impl::bscu::bscu.federated, applying valid type extension rules to maintain interface compatibility. The wbs.ima implementation shall inherit all subcomponents and structural elements from wbs.detailed, with a single type refinement to replace the inherited BSCU subcomponent with the integrated modular avionics BSCU variant impl::bscu::bscu.ima, applying valid type extension rules to maintain interface compatibility.

All contained components shall define consistent, extension-compatible interfaces to support substitution across implementation variants without breaking inherited connections. The pedal input subsystem shall expose two unidirectional discrete output ports designated signal1 and signal2, carrying redundant pilot brake pedal position input values. The electrical power subsystem shall expose two provided bus access points designated line1 and line2, delivering independent, redundant electrical power supply feeds. All pump components, including the blue primary pump, green primary pump, and accumulator backup pump, shall expose a single provided bus access point designated pressure_output, delivering pressurized hydraulic fluid supply to connected hydraulic components. The abstract base selector valve assembly shall expose a single required bus access point designated accumulator_input for receiving backup pressure from the accumulator pump. The simplified selector_basic variant used in the basic implementation shall extend the base selector interface to add two required bus access points designated blue_input and green_input for receiving pressure from the blue and green primary pumps, three unidirectional input ports designated Select_Alternate, cmd_nor, and cmd_alt for receiving circuit selection and brake command signals from the BSCU, and a single provided bus access point designated output for delivering regulated brake pressure to the wheel assembly. The high-fidelity selector_detailed variant used in the detailed, federated, and IMA implementations shall extend the base selector interface to add two required bus access points designated blue_input and green_input for receiving pressure from the blue primary pump and gated green supply path respectively, a unidirectional input port designated select_alternate for receiving circuit selection commands from the BSCU, and two provided bus access points designated green_output and blue_output for delivering regulated pressure to the green and blue anti-skid valves respectively. The boolean-actuated shutoff valve used in detailed architecture variants shall expose a required bus access point designated input for receiving incoming hydraulic pressure from the green pump, a provided bus access point designated output for delivering gated pressure to the selector green input, and a unidirectional boolean input port designated boolean_input for receiving open/close actuation commands from the BSCU. Each command-actuated anti-skid shutoff valve shall expose a required bus access point designated input for receiving regulated pressure from the selector assembly, a provided bus access point designated output for delivering modulated brake pressure to the wheel assembly, and a unidirectional command input port designated cmd_input for receiving anti-skid modulation commands from the BSCU. The abstract base wheel brake assembly shall define a common root type for wheel variants, with no concrete interface features declared at the abstract level. The single-input wheel_one_input.i variant used in the basic implementation shall extend the base wheel type to expose a single required bus access point designated input for receiving consolidated brake pressure supply from the simplified selector. The dual-input wheel_two_inputs.i variant used in detailed, federated, and IMA implementations shall extend the base wheel type to expose two required bus access points designated blue_input and green_input for receiving modulated pressure from the blue and green anti-skid valves respectively. All BSCU variants, including the generic, basic, federated, and IMA types, shall expose a consistent core interface to maintain cross-variant compatibility, including two unidirectional input ports designated pedal1 and pedal2 for receiving redundant pedal position signals from the pedal subsystem, two required bus access points designated pwr1 and pwr2 for connecting to the redundant power supply feeds from the power subsystem, a unidirectional output port designated Select_Alternate for transmitting hydraulic circuit selection commands, and two unidirectional output ports designated cmd_nor and cmd_alt for transmitting normal and alternate brake modulation commands to connected valve components. The annunciation device shall expose a state propagation interface supporting error state reporting, with two discrete component states representing fully operational functionality and failed functionality, to support system-level fault state evaluation and pilot annunciation of brake system failures.

All system connections shall be defined at the implementation level, with a core set of connections retained across all variants, and additional connections added or refined to support the architecture of each implementation variant. The core connections defined in the base wbs.generic implementation, inherited by all extending variants, include a bidirectional bus access connection between the accumulator pump pressure output and the selector accumulator input to deliver backup hydraulic pressure, bidirectional bus access connections between the power subsystem line1 and BSCU pwr1 interface and between the power subsystem line2 and BSCU pwr2 interface to deliver redundant electrical power to the BSCU, and unidirectional port connections from the pedals signal1 output to the BSCU pedal1 input and from the pedals signal2 output to the BSCU pedal2 input to deliver pilot brake input signals. The wbs.basic implementation shall add connections to support the simplified single-path hydraulic architecture, including bidirectional bus access connections between the blue pump pressure output and the simplified selector blue input, and between the green pump pressure output and the simplified selector green input to deliver primary pump pressure to the selector, unidirectional port connections from the BSCU Select_Alternate output to the simplified selector Select_Alternate input, from the BSCU cmd_nor output to the simplified selector cmd_nor input, and from the BSCU cmd_alt output to the simplified selector cmd_alt input to deliver BSCU control commands to the selector, and a bidirectional bus access connection between the simplified selector output and the single-input wheel input to deliver consolidated regulated brake pressure to the wheel brake assembly. The wbs.detailed implementation and its extending federated and IMA variants shall add connections to support the split dual-path hydraulic architecture with independent anti-skid modulation, including a bidirectional bus access connection between the blue pump pressure output and the detailed selector blue input to deliver direct blue circuit pressure to the selector, a bidirectional bus access connection between the green pump pressure output and the boolean shutoff valve input to route green circuit pressure through the shutoff valve, a bidirectional bus access connection between the shutoff valve output and the detailed selector green input to deliver gated green circuit pressure to the selector, unidirectional port connections from the BSCU Select_Alternate output to both the shutoff valve boolean input and the detailed selector select_alternate input to coordinate green circuit activation during alternate mode operation, unidirectional port connections from the BSCU cmd_nor output to the green_skid valve cmd_input and from the BSCU cmd_alt output to the blue_skid valve cmd_input to deliver independent anti-skid modulation commands to each circuit, bidirectional bus access connections between the detailed selector green output and the green_skid valve input and between the detailed selector blue output and the blue_skid valve input to deliver regulated circuit pressure to the anti-skid valves, and bidirectional bus access connections between the blue_skid valve output and the wheel blue_input and between the green_skid valve output and the wheel green_input to deliver modulated brake pressure from each independent circuit to the dual-input wheel brake assembly. The wbs.federated and wbs.ima implementations shall retain all connections defined in wbs.detailed, with no additional connection modifications required due to the interface-compatible BSCU refinement applied in these variants.

No explicit thread-level scheduling or end-to-end latency constraints shall be defined for the base wbs.generic, wbs.basic, or wbs.detailed implementations, as these variants use abstract or non-deployment-specific BSCU types that do not bind functions to specific computing resources. The wbs.federated implementation, which uses a federated BSCU variant, shall enforce dedicated resource scheduling for BSCU functions, where brake control and anti-skid logic execute on independent, dedicated computing modules with separate scheduling domains, eliminating resource contention between BSCU functions and other aircraft systems. The wbs.ima implementation, which uses an integrated modular avionics BSCU variant, shall enforce time-partitioned scheduling for BSCU functions executing on shared avionics computing resources, adhering to strict time partition allocation rules to prevent cross-function interference and guarantee deterministic execution of brake control logic. All hardwired signal and hydraulic bus connections shall propagate signals and pressure with negligible latency consistent with physical hardware behavior, with no scheduled transmission delays introduced by communication protocol stacks. System-level composite error behavior shall be evaluated continuously during system operation to detect fault conditions, with error state propagation occurring instantaneously across connected components to support timely fault detection and annunciation. The system shall support six defined top-level error states as specified in the error model: Operational, representing fully functional brake system performance, AnnunciatedTotalBrakingLoss representing total loss of brake function with active pilot fault annunciation, UnannunciatedTotalBrakingLoss representing total loss of brake function without active pilot fault annunciation, PartialBrakingLoss representing reduced brake function across one or more hydraulic circuits, AsymmetricLoss representing unequal brake force application across wheel brakes leading to directional control issues, and InadvertentBrake representing uncommanded brake application in the absence of pilot input. The composite error behavior logic shall define explicit transitions for total brake loss failure states as follows: an unannunciated total wheel brake loss failure state shall be entered when the BSCU is in a failed state, the accumulator pump is in a failed state, and the annunciation device is in a failed state, or when both the blue and green primary pumps are in failed states, the accumulator pump is in a failed state, and the annunciation device is in a failed state, with the duplicate trigger condition for combined BSCU and accumulator failure with annunciation failure retained as specified in the error model. An annunciated total wheel brake loss failure state shall be entered when the BSCU is in a failed state, the accumulator pump is in a failed state, and the annunciation device is in an operational state, or when both the blue and green primary pumps are in failed states, the accumulator pump is in a failed state, and the annunciation device is in an operational state, with the duplicate trigger condition for combined BSCU and accumulator failure with operational annunciation retained as specified in the error model. Transitions for partial braking loss, asymmetric loss, and inadvertent brake states shall be supported by the imported error library for subsequent implementation refinement.

All communication between system components shall use two distinct connection types, each with defined data and transmission rules. Hydraulic pressure transfer connections between pumps, valves, selectors, and wheel assemblies shall be implemented as bidirectional bus access connections, representing physical hydraulic fluid flow rather than digital data transfer, with continuous analog pressure values passed between connected components, no packetization, no addressing, and no protocol overhead. Electrical power transfer connections between the power subsystem and BSCU shall be implemented as bidirectional bus access connections, representing continuous electrical power delivery, with no data payload carried over the power connections, and redundant feeds maintained as independent, electrically isolated buses to prevent common-cause failure. Control signal connections between pedals, BSCU, and valve components shall be implemented as unidirectional port connections, carrying discrete or analog data values including pedal position measurements, boolean valve actuation commands, circuit selection signals, and brake modulation commands, with direct point-to-point transmission, no bus arbitration, and no protocol encapsulation consistent with hardwired avionics signal connections. Error state propagation between components shall use the EMV2 error modeling annex, with error types imported from the dedicated WBSImplementationErrorLib error library, and component-level error behavior defined using the TwostateWBS behavior specification from the same library, which defines two mutually exclusive component states for all fault-monitored components: Operational, representing fully functional component behavior, and Failed, representing total loss of component function. All component type substitutions across implementation variants shall follow the Type_Extension classifier substitution rule, ensuring that substituted components are valid subtypes of the original component type and fully implement the required interface of the original component to maintain connection compatibility across variants. No custom data types, bus types, device types, or system types shall be defined within the impl::wbs package beyond the root wbs system type and its implementations, as all port, bus, and subcomponent interfaces rely on types and components defined in the imported supporting packages.

A public AADL package named impl::wheel is defined, with an explicit dependency on the common package to access publicly declared modeling elements from that package. The package declares an abstract root system type named wheel, which acts as the base classifier for all wheel component variants and contains no concrete feature declarations or internal structure definitions. A system type named wheel_one_input is defined as a direct extension of the base wheel type, intended to represent the wheel configuration that abstracts dual pressure supply channels into a single logical access point. A corresponding system implementation named wheel_one_input.i is declared for the wheel_one_input type, with no internal subcomponents, connections, or behavior declarations. A system type named wheel_two_inputs is defined as a direct extension of the wheel_one_input type, intended to represent the wheel configuration that explicitly models independent dual pressure supply channels. A corresponding system implementation named wheel_two_inputs.i is declared for the wheel_two_inputs type, with no internal subcomponents, connections, or behavior declarations. All error modeling constructs within the package reference error types and behavior definitions from the WBSImplementationErrorLib error library as required by EMV2 annex specifications.

The abstract root wheel system type exposes no external interaction interfaces. The wheel_one_input system type declares a single required bus access feature named input, which supports access to an external pressure supply bus. The EMV2 annex subclause for wheel_one_input imports error types from WBSImplementationErrorLib and applies the Twostate error behavior model from the same library. Within this error specification, the input feature is defined as an inbound propagation point for the NoService error, and NoService errors arriving at the input feature are designated as an error sink. The component error behavior for wheel_one_input defines two operational states: Operational to indicate normal functional operation, and Failed to indicate a loss of component function. A single state transition rule is specified: when a NoService error propagates into the component via the input feature, the component immediately transitions from the Operational state to the Failed state. The wheel_two_inputs system type inherits the input required bus access feature from its parent wheel_one_input type, and declares two additional required bus access features named green_input and blue_input, each supporting access to an independent external pressure supply bus. The EMV2 annex subclause declared for wheel_two_inputs fully replaces the EMV2 subclause inherited from wheel_one_input, and similarly imports error types from WBSImplementationErrorLib and applies the Twostate error behavior model. Within this custom error specification, the green_input and blue_input features are defined as inbound propagation points for the NoService error, and NoService errors arriving at each of these two features are designated as separate error sinks. Two state transition rules are specified for wheel_two_inputs: when a NoService error propagates into the component via the green_input feature, the component transitions from the Operational state to the Failed state; when a NoService error propagates into the component via the blue_input feature, the component transitions from the Operational state to the Failed state. No error propagation rules, error flow definitions, or state transition logic are defined for the inherited input feature within the wheel_two_inputs error specification. Both wheel system implementations declare no internal subcomponents, no internal interaction points, and no internal connection logic.

For the wheel_one_input configuration, all pressure-related interaction data flows into the wheel component from the connected external pressure bus exclusively through the input required bus access interface. The component does not transmit any outbound data or error events to external systems. All NoService error events received through the input interface terminate at the component boundary as a designated error sink, directly triggering the component state transition to the Failed state, with no onward error propagation to external entities. For the wheel_two_inputs configuration, pressure-related interaction data may flow into the wheel component from connected external pressure buses through the inherited input interface, as well as through the green_input and blue_input interfaces. The component does not transmit any outbound data or error events to external systems. Per the defined error specification, only NoService error events received through the green_input and blue_input interfaces terminate at the component boundary as designated error sinks, with each event capable of independently triggering the component state transition to the Failed state. No error handling, termination, or propagation rules are defined for events received through the inherited input interface in this configuration.

No periodic scheduling policies, execution time budgets, end-to-end latency requirements, thread priority assignments, or mode-triggered scheduling rules are declared for any system type or implementation within the package. All defined component state transitions follow an event-triggered execution paradigm, where transitions to the Failed state are activated immediately upon reception of a qualifying NoService error event at the corresponding interface, with no mandated fixed scheduling time base or execution delay requirement.

No custom communication bus types, data types, or data representations are defined within the impl::wheel package. All required bus access features declared across all wheel component types reference the common::pressure.i bus instance defined in the dependent common package. All bus access features use the required access mode, meaning wheel components function exclusively as bus access requesters and do not act as bus service providers. For error modeling, the NoService error type used across all error propagation and transition logic is a predefined type from the WBSImplementationErrorLib, used to represent a total loss of pressure supply service from a connected bus. The Twostate behavior model applied to both wheel variants defines a minimal two-state operational lifecycle for components, with no intermediate degraded states defined.

The system shall define a public AADL package named WBSMappingErrorLib, which serves as a dedicated shared library for cross-layer error mapping definitions and base error behavior specifications within the wheel brake system error modeling framework. This package shall establish formal dependencies on two pre-existing public error library packages to support cross-package error type reference via fully qualified type names: the WBSImplementationErrorLib package that provides canonical implementation-layer error type definitions, and the WBSFunctionalErrorLib package that provides canonical functional-layer error type definitions. The package shall not contain standalone definitions of core AADL component categories including system, process, thread, device, processor, memory, or bus, and shall encapsulate all specialized error modeling logic within an EMV2 annex attached directly to the package root.

The package shall expose reusable EMV2 error modeling artifacts as its only publicly accessible interfaces for reference by other packages in the WBS architecture. The first exposed artifact is the Basic error behavior state machine, which defines a minimal, extensible error state set without embedded state transitions, error events, or propagation points, to support consistent error state definition across all WBS components. The remaining exposed artifacts are two typed error mapping sets, which define formal transformation logic for error propagations crossing the boundary between implementation and functional architecture layers. The package shall not define any data ports, event ports, bus access points, or subprogram call interfaces, as it operates as a static design-time library with no runtime interaction points. The Basic error behavior shall define two discrete states: the Operational state designated as the initial state representing normal fault-free operation, and the Failed state representing a faulted condition where the associated component cannot deliver intended functionality.

The error mapping logic defined in the package shall govern bidirectional cross-layer error propagation flows between the WBS implementation layer and functional layer. The FunctionToImplementation mapping set shall handle error flows that originate from implementation-layer components and propagate upward to functional-layer components, applying predefined transformation rules to convert implementation-layer error tokens to semantically aligned functional-layer error tokens. This mapping set shall implement a general catch-all flow path that routes any unspecified implementation error, represented by the AnyImplementationError type from WBSImplementationErrorLib, to the generic functional error type AnyFunctionalError from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, alongside four dedicated point-to-point flow paths for specific error conditions: HydraulicLossBlue errors from the implementation layer map directly to HydraulicLossBlue errors at the functional layer, HydraulicLossGreen implementation errors map directly to HydraulicLossGreen functional errors, HydraulicLossComponents implementation errors map directly to HydraulicLossComponents functional errors, and NoService implementation errors map directly to NoService functional errors. The ImplementationToFunction mapping set shall handle error flows that originate from functional-layer components and propagate downward to implementation-layer components, applying parallel transformation rules to convert functional-layer error tokens to semantically aligned implementation-layer error tokens. This mapping set shall implement a general catch-all flow path that routes any unspecified functional error, represented by the AnyFunctionalError type from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, to the generic implementation error type AnyImplementationError from WBSImplementationErrorLib, alongside four dedicated point-to-point flow paths for matching specific error conditions: HydraulicLossBlue functional errors map directly to HydraulicLossBlue implementation errors, HydraulicLossGreen functional errors map directly to HydraulicLossGreen implementation errors, HydraulicLossComponents functional errors map directly to HydraulicLossComponents implementation errors, and NoService functional errors map directly to NoService implementation errors.

The WBSMappingErrorLib package contains no runtime-executable components, schedulable threads, periodic processing tasks, or time-triggered logic, so no scheduling priority assignments, period specifications, execution time budgets, or deadline constraints shall be defined within the package structure. All error mapping rules contained in the package shall be treated as static, zero-latency transformation logic for error propagation analysis, introducing no additional time delay to calculated error propagation paths when referenced by component error models. The Basic error behavior state set defined in the package shall not specify any time-dependent state transition conditions, allowing referencing components to define custom transition timelines aligned with their specific fault response requirements without constraint from the base library.

The package shall not define any native AADL data types, communication bus types, data type representations, or bus protocol specifications within its scope. All error types referenced in the package’s mapping logic shall be imported directly from the two dependent error library packages, with no local redefinition, type modification, or semantic override of imported error types permitted. The two error mapping type definitions shall enforce strict type checking for propagated error tokens, only permitting transformation of error types explicitly listed in the mapping rule sets, with no support for implicit type conversion of unlisted error types. When applied to error propagation connections across architecture layers, the mapping rules shall operate independently of underlying communication bus types or transported payload data types, requiring no bus-specific or data-specific adaptation to function across all valid WBS inter-component connections.

The top-level modeling package shall be defined as integration::main, with all contained model elements declared within the public section of the package. The package shall declare explicit import dependencies on two external packages, functional::main and impl::wbs, to resolve all references to component types, component implementations, and associated properties defined in those packages. The package shall define a top-level system type named main, which acts as the root component of the integrated aircraft system deployment. A corresponding system implementation named main.impl shall be defined for the main system type to represent the complete integrated deployment configuration. The main.impl implementation shall instantiate two first-level subcomponents. The first subcomponent shall be named functional, instantiated from the basic implementation of the Aircraft system defined in the functional::main package. The second subcomponent shall be named wbs_impl, instantiated from the ima implementation of the wbs system defined in the impl::wbs package. The integration::main package shall not define additional component types, data types, bus types, or property sets beyond the main system type and its main.impl implementation, with all subcomponent references resolved exclusively from imported dependent packages. The EMV2 error behavior annex attached to main.impl shall declare dependencies on the WBSMappingErrorLib library, importing the FunctionToImplementation error type equivalence definition and the Basic error behavior definition to support composite error state propagation modeling.

The top-level main system type shall not define any externally exposed interaction ports, including data ports, event ports, and event data ports, establishing a closed integration layer boundary with no direct external interfaces defined at this level. The main.impl implementation shall define explicit Actual_Processor_Binding properties to map functional elements to their supporting physical runtime components, following binding propagation rules that require physical components to explicitly declare binding propagation attributes, while functional elements reference their associated runtime components via the processor binding property. The alert functional element contained within the functional subcomponent shall be bound to the bscu processor component contained within the wbs_impl subcomponent. The DecelerateWheels functional element contained within the decelerate functional module of the functional subcomponent shall be bound to the wbs_impl subsystem as a whole. The hydraulic functional element contained within the functional subcomponent shall be simultaneously bound to three physical components under the wbs_impl subcomponent: the blue_pump component, the green_pump component, and the accumulator component. The electrical functional element contained within the functional subcomponent shall be simultaneously bound to three power-related elements under the wbs_impl subcomponent: the power subsystem, the battery1 component nested under the power subsystem, and the battery2 component nested under the power subsystem. No functional element under the functional subcomponent shall remain unbound to a physical runtime element from the wbs_impl subcomponent. The composite error behavior logic defined for main.impl shall implement a direct failure propagation rule, where the top-level main system transitions to the Failed state immediately when the functional subcomponent enters the Failed state, with no intermediate error states or additional transition conditions specified for this failure path.

The main.impl integration implementation shall not define explicit port connections, including data connections, event connections, and event data connections, between the functional subcomponent and the wbs_impl subcomponent. All data exchange, service invocation, and state transmission interactions between functional elements and physical implementation elements shall be carried through the established processor binding relationships, with each functional element routing all runtime interaction traffic exclusively to its bound set of physical runtime elements. No data flow path shall be established between a functional element and a physical element that is not included in its declared processor binding set. All internal data flows and port connections within the functional subcomponent and within the wbs_impl subcomponent shall retain their original definitions from their respective source packages, with no connection rerouting, addition, or modification introduced at the integration layer.

The integration layer shall not define, override, or extend any timing, scheduling, or latency properties for contained subcomponents, including but not limited to task dispatch periods, worst-case execution time budgets, scheduling priorities, end-to-end flow latency budgets, and communication transmission delay values. All timing and scheduling rules for functional and physical components shall be inherited directly from the native definitions in the functional::main and impl::wbs dependent packages. The established processor binding relationships shall not alter the native scheduling parameters, priority assignments, or latency guarantees of the bound functional and physical elements. No additional timing constraints shall be imposed at the integration layer that would conflict with constraints defined in the original source packages of the subcomponents.

The integration::main package shall not define any custom data types within its scope. All data types used for functional interaction, state transmission, parameter passing, and fault signaling across the integrated system shall be reused exclusively from pre-defined data types in the functional::main and impl::wbs dependent packages, with no new data type definitions introduced at the integration layer. The integration::main package shall not define any custom bus types or bus instances within its scope. All communication buses used for inter-component and intra-component data transmission shall be reused exclusively from pre-defined bus implementations in the two imported dependent packages. The integration layer shall not modify native bus attributes including communication protocol specifications, available bandwidth, transmission latency, and fault handling mechanisms for any reused bus instance.

The top-level model module is defined as a package named functional_initial, which declares mandatory import dependencies on two external property set packages, WBSPS and ARP4761, to support function classification and safety assessment property assignments. The package defines a hierarchical set of system components representing aircraft deceleration functions, with the top-level system component named DecelerateAircraft, which is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true to mark it as a core system function. The DecelerateAircraft system defines one implementation variant named basic, which decomposes the top-level deceleration function into two direct subcomponent systems: an instance of DecelerateWheels using its basic implementation variant, and an instance of DecelerateThrottle. The DecelerateWheels system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one implementation variant named basic that decomposes the wheel deceleration function into eight direct subcomponent systems: two separate instances of ApplyWheelBrake each using the basic implementation variant, designated ApplyWheelBrake1 and ApplyWheelBrake2 to represent redundant wheel brake channels, plus single instances of NoseWheelSteering, AircraftStatus, CrewAlert, ElectricPower, HydraulicPower, and Annunciation. The CrewAlert system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The ElectricPower system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The HydraulicPower system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The Annunciation system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The AircraftStatus system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The ApplyWheelBrake system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one implementation variant named basic that decomposes the individual wheel brake function into four direct subcomponent systems: an instance of BrakeByWheel using its basic implementation variant, an instance of WBControl, an instance of BrakeCommand using its basic implementation variant, and an instance of WBStatus. The BrakeByWheel system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and defines one basic implementation variant that also carries the WBSPS::IsFunction property set to true, with no further internal subcomponent decomposition. The NoseWheelSteering, WBControl, and WBStatus systems do not carry the WBSPS::IsFunction property assignment, and have no implementation variants defined within the current package scope. The BrakeCommand system does not carry the WBSPS::IsFunction property assignment, and defines one implementation variant named basic that decomposes the brake command function into two direct subcomponent systems: an instance of ElectricPower, and an instance of Command. The Command system is assigned the WBSPS::IsFunction property with a value of true, and has no implementation variant defined within the current package scope. The DecelerateThrottle system does not carry the WBSPS::IsFunction property assignment, and has no implementation variant defined within the current package scope. All components containing error behavior specifications declare a dependency on the external error library WBSFunctionalErrorLib, to access shared error types and pre-defined error behavior state machines.

All system components shall expose a binary operational state interface to their parent composite components, indicating whether the component is in a fully operational state or a failed state, to support hierarchical error state propagation and composite failure logic. The DecelerateAircraft.basic implementation shall define composite error behavior using the TwostateWBS state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, where the component enters a top-level Failed state if either its DecelerateWheels subcomponent or DecelerateThrottle subcomponent reports a Failed state. The DecelerateWheels.basic implementation shall define composite error behavior using the TwostateWBS state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, where the component enters a Failed state only when the Annunciation subcomponent reports a Failed state concurrently with both ApplyWheelBrake1 and ApplyWheelBrake2 subcomponents reporting Failed states, corresponding to the unanunciated total wheel brake loss condition. The DecelerateWheels component shall attach four distinct ARP4761 hazard assessment records to its Failed state, each mapped to a specific failure mode. The first hazard record applies to the TotalWBLossAnunciated failure mode, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, describing anunciated total wheel braking loss occurring during the Landing flight phase, classified as a Hazardous failure condition with a Remote qualitative probability objective, associated with crew procedures to select a more suitable airport, notify emergency ground support, prepare occupants for runway overrun, and use spoilers and thrust reversers to the maximum extent possible, with an empty comment field. The second hazard record applies to the TotalWBLossUnanunciated failure mode, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, describing unanunciated total wheel braking loss occurring during the Landing and Rejected Takeoff flight phases, classified as a Hazardous failure condition with a Remote qualitative probability objective, associated with crew detection of failure when the brakes are operated, use of spoilers and thrust reversers to the maximum extent possible, and potential runway overrun, with an empty comment field. The third hazard record applies to the PartialSymmetricalWBLossUnAnunciated failure mode, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, describing unanunciated partial symmetrical wheel braking loss occurring during the Landing and Rejected Takeoff flight phases, classified as a Hazardous failure condition with a Remote qualitative probability objective, with a comment noting the condition is potentially catastrophic pending confirmation by analysis, associated with crew detection of failure when the brakes are used, use of available wheel braking, spoilers and thrust reversers to the maximum extent to decelerate the aircraft, elevated loaded brake wheel temperatures that may reach the point of wheel or fire failure, and runway overrun risk dependent on the number of lost brakes. The fourth hazard record applies to the PartialSymmetricalWBLossanunciated failure mode, cross-referenced to AIR6110 page 36, describing anunciated partial symmetrical wheel braking loss occurring during the Landing flight phase, classified as a Major failure condition with a Remote qualitative probability objective, associated with pre-landing crew awareness of partial braking loss, use of available wheel braking, spoilers and thrust reversers to the maximum extent to decelerate the aircraft, elevated loaded brake wheel temperatures that may reach the point of wheel or fire failure, and runway overrun risk dependent on the number of lost brakes, with an empty comment field. The CrewAlert system and its basic implementation shall use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, supporting binary Operational and Failed states with no component-specific error events defined in the current scope. The ElectricPower system shall use the Twostate error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, defining a single Failure error event typed to the WBErrorSet error group, which triggers an immediate state transition from Operational to Failed via transition t1; its basic implementation adds no additional error events, transitions, or subcomponents. The Command system shall use the Twostate error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, defining a single Failure error event typed to the WBErrorSet error group, which triggers an immediate state transition from Operational to Failed via transition t1. The HydraulicPower system and its basic implementation shall use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, supporting binary Operational and Failed states with no component-specific error events defined in the current scope. The Annunciation system shall use the Twostate error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, defining a single Failure error event typed to the WBErrorSet error group, which triggers an immediate state transition from Operational to Failed via transition t1; its basic implementation adds no additional error events, transitions, or subcomponents. The AircraftStatus system and its basic implementation shall use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, supporting binary Operational and Failed states with no component-specific error events defined in the current scope. The ApplyWheelBrake system and its basic implementation shall use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, where the basic implementation defines composite error logic that triggers a component Failed state if either the BrakeWheel subcomponent (of type BrakeByWheel) or BrakeCommand subcomponent reports a Failed state. The BrakeByWheel system shall use the Twostate error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, defining two separate error events typed to the WBErrorSet error group: LossHydraulicSupply and LossHydraulicComponents, each of which independently triggers an immediate state transition from Operational to Failed via transitions t1 and t2 respectively; its basic implementation retains the base Twostate error behavior with no additional error events, transitions, or subcomponents. The NoseWheelSteering, WBControl, and WBStatus systems shall each use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, supporting binary Operational and Failed states with no component-specific error events defined in the current scope. The BrakeCommand system shall use the TwostateWBS error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, where its basic implementation defines composite error logic that triggers a component Failed state if either its electricPower subcomponent (of type ElectricPower) or command subcomponent (of type Command) reports a Failed state. The DecelerateThrottle system shall use the Twostate error behavior state machine from WBSFunctionalErrorLib, defining a single Failure error event typed to the WBErrorSet error group, which triggers an immediate state transition from Operational to Failed via transition t1.

No explicit functional data or control signal flows between peer subcomponents are defined in the current package scope, as no port declarations, data connections, or access connections are specified for any system component. The only defined cross-component flow is hierarchical upward propagation of component Failed states, which travels from leaf components up through each layer of composite parent components to trigger parent failure states per the defined composite error logic. For the BrakeCommand.basic implementation, failed state inputs are received from the electric power supply subcomponent and the command input subcomponent to determine overall brake command function availability. For the ApplyWheelBrake.basic implementation, failed state inputs are received from the wheel brake actuation subcomponent (instance of BrakeByWheel) and the brake command subcomponent to determine overall individual brake channel availability. For the DecelerateWheels.basic implementation, failed state inputs are received from both redundant brake channel subcomponents and the annunciation subcomponent to distinguish between anunciated and unanunciated wheel brake loss conditions, and to trigger the wheel deceleration function failed state for the defined unanunciated total loss condition. For the top-level DecelerateAircraft.basic implementation, failed state inputs are received from the wheel deceleration subcomponent and the throttle deceleration subcomponent to determine overall aircraft deceleration function availability.

No explicit component execution scheduling rules, periodic execution rates, execution deadlines, or end-to-end functional latency constraints are defined within the current package scope. All wheel braking related deceleration functions shall be fully operational during the Landing and Rejected Takeoff flight phases, as these are the operational phases specified for the identified brake failure hazards. The qualitative probability objectives assigned to each hazard define long-term functional reliability requirements rather than real-time performance constraints, requiring each identified Hazardous and Major failure condition to occur at a Remote probability rate across all applicable operational flight phases. No time-based error detection or recovery timing requirements are specified in the current scope.

No custom application data type components or communication bus components are defined within the functional_initial package scope. All error event types used in component error behavior specifications are referenced from the external WBSFunctionalErrorLib library, with all explicitly defined error events belonging to the WBErrorSet shared error group. The WBSPS property set imported by the package provides the IsFunction boolean property used to classify core wheel braking system functions, while the imported ARP4761 property set provides the structured hazards property used to attach safety certification metadata, including cross-reference to applicable guidance documentation, failure condition descriptions, applicable flight phases, failure condition classification, qualitative probability objectives, and associated comment text, to component failure states. No data port type specifications, communication bus protocol definitions, bus access requirements, or data representation rules are defined for components in the current scope, as the model is limited to functional hierarchy decomposition and safety-related error behavior specification.

The top-level model module is defined as a public AADL package named bscu, which shall declare explicit import dependencies on six external packages to access shared model elements: the common package for shared command data types and power bus definitions, the platform package for federated and integrated modular avionics platform component models, the Base_Types package for primitive data type definitions, the error_library package for reusable error type and error behavior definitions, the EMV2 package for error modeling annex constructs and properties, and the ARP4761 package for safety assessment property sets aligned with aerospace safety standard requirements. No circular dependencies shall be permitted between components contained within the bscu package, and all cross-package element references shall resolve exclusively to elements declared in the explicitly imported external packages. The bscu package shall contain five core component type definitions: a command process component, a monitor process component, a bscu_subsystem system component, a select_alternate system component, and a top-level bscu system component. Each component type shall be paired with dedicated implementation definitions as required to support functional behavior and multiple deployment configurations. The top-level bscu system shall support three implementation variants: a minimal basic implementation without redundant subcomponents, a core generic implementation containing full redundant channel logic, a federated deployment implementation that extends the generic implementation for federated avionics architectures, and an integrated modular avionics (IMA) deployment implementation that extends the generic implementation for partitioned IMA architectures. The federated and IMA implementations shall inherit all features, subcomponents, connections, and error behavior from the generic bscu implementation, adding only platform-specific subcomponents and deployment binding properties.

All component interfaces shall be explicitly declared at the component type level, with no hidden external interfaces added at the implementation level. The command process component type shall expose three unidirectional data port interfaces: an output data port for generated brake command values, an output data port for generated skid command values, and an input data port for received pedal position values. The command.i implementation of the command process shall define an implicit processor error input point to receive software and hardware failure signals from the bound execution platform, with no additional external functional ports. The monitor process component type shall expose three unidirectional data port interfaces: an input data port for received brake command values, an input data port for received skid command values, and an output data port for generated channel validity status. The monitor.i implementation of the monitor process shall define an implicit processor error input point to receive software and hardware failure signals from the bound execution platform, plus an internal error event to capture spurious invalid status outputs generated without corresponding input or platform faults. The bscu_subsystem system component type shall expose five external interfaces: a required bus access interface to connect to a generic power supply, an input data port for received pedal position values, an output data port for generated brake command values, an output data port for generated skid command values, and an output data port for generated channel validity status. The bscu_subsystem.generic implementation of the bscu_subsystem shall contain two internal process subcomponents: one instance of the monitor.i process named mon, and one instance of the command.i process named cmd, with no additional external interfaces beyond those declared on the parent component type. The select_alternate system component type shall expose three unidirectional data port interfaces: two input data ports to receive validity status values from the primary and alternate BSCU channels respectively, and one output data port for the generated channel selection result. The select_alternate component shall define an internal error event to capture erroneous channel selection outputs generated without corresponding input validity faults. The top-level bscu system component type shall expose seven external interfaces: two required bus access interfaces to connect to independent generic power supplies for the primary and alternate channels, two input data ports to receive pedal position values for the primary and alternate channels respectively, an output data port for the generated alternate channel selection flag, an output data port for skid command values from the normal (primary) channel, and an output data port for skid command values from the alternate channel. The bscu.basic implementation of the top-level bscu shall contain no internal subcomponents, implementing only core error response behavior for power supply faults. The bscu.generic implementation of the top-level bscu shall contain three internal system subcomponents: two instances of the bscu_subsystem.generic component representing the primary and alternate BSCU channels, and one instance of the select_alternate component to implement channel selection logic. The bscu.federated implementation shall inherit all subcomponents and interfaces from bscu.generic, adding one internal subcomponent representing a federated avionics platform. The bscu.ima implementation shall inherit all subcomponents and interfaces from bscu.generic, adding one internal subcomponent representing a partitioned IMA platform.

All functional and error data flows between components shall be explicitly defined via port and bus access connections, with no implicit data routing permitted. All component error behavior shall reuse predefined error behavior state machines from the error_library package: the command, monitor, bscu_subsystem, and select_alternate components shall use the generic simple error behavior set, while the top-level bscu implementations shall use the dedicated bscu error behavior set from the error library to define standard operational and failed state transitions. Within each bscu_subsystem.generic instance, incoming pedal position data from the external pedal input port shall be routed directly to the pedal value input port of the internal command process subcomponent. The command process shall process received pedal position values to compute corresponding brake command and skid command output values. Generated brake command values from the command process shall be routed along two parallel paths: one path to the brake command input port of the internal monitor process subcomponent for validity checking, and a second path directly to the external brake command output port of the bscu_subsystem for delivery to downstream braking components. Generated skid command values from the command process shall be routed along two parallel paths: one path to the skid command input port of the internal monitor process subcomponent for validity checking, and a second path directly to the external skid command output port of the bscu_subsystem for delivery to downstream braking components. The monitor process shall perform validity assessments on received brake and skid command values, generating a boolean validity status that is routed directly to the external validity output port of the bscu_subsystem. At the top-level bscu.generic, bscu.federated, and bscu.ima implementations, power supplied via the first external power bus access port shall be routed exclusively to the power input of the primary bscu_subsystem instance, and power supplied via the second external power bus access port shall be routed exclusively to the power input of the alternate bscu_subsystem instance. Incoming pedal position data from the first external pedal input port shall be routed exclusively to the pedal input of the primary bscu_subsystem instance, and incoming pedal position data from the second external pedal input port shall be routed exclusively to the pedal input of the alternate bscu_subsystem instance. Validity status output from the primary bscu_subsystem instance shall be routed to the first input port of the select_alternate subcomponent, and validity status output from the alternate bscu_subsystem instance shall be routed to the second input port of the select_alternate subcomponent. The select_alternate component shall implement fixed selection logic that outputs a false value when the primary channel validity input indicates a valid primary channel, signaling use of the primary channel, and outputs a true value when the primary channel validity input indicates a primary channel fault, signaling switchover to the alternate channel. The generated selection result from the select_alternate component shall be routed directly to the external alternate selection output port of the top-level bscu. Skid command output from the primary bscu_subsystem instance shall be routed directly to the external normal channel skid command output port of the top-level bscu, and skid command output from the alternate bscu_subsystem instance shall be routed directly to the external alternate channel skid command output port of the top-level bscu. Error propagation paths shall be defined per EMV2 rules to model fault transmission across the system, supporting end-to-end fault tracing for FMEA and fault impact analysis. For the command process, a no-service error received on the pedal value input port, or software or hardware failure errors received from the bound execution platform, shall trigger a transition to a failed state, which propagates no-value errors out of both the brake and skid command output ports. For the monitor process, a no-value error received on either the brake or skid command input ports, software or hardware failure errors received from the bound execution platform, or an internal invalid report error event, shall trigger a transition to a failed state, which propagates a no-value error out of the validity status output port.
