For each bscu_subsystem instance, a no-power error received on the power bus access interface shall trigger a transition to a failed state, which propagates a no-value error out of the validity status output port, forming a continuous error path from power supply loss to invalid validity status output. The composite error state of each bscu_subsystem shall be marked as failed if either the internal command or monitor process is in a failed state, and shall be marked as operational only if both internal processes are in an operational state. For the select_alternate component, concurrent no-value errors received on both channel validity input ports, or an internal selection error event, shall trigger a transition to a failed state, which propagates a no-value error out of the selection result output port. For the minimal bscu.basic implementation, a no-power error received on either external power input shall trigger a transition to a failed state, with error sinks defined to capture power loss faults on both power interfaces. For the bscu.generic, federated, and ima implementations, the composite system error state shall be marked as failed only if both primary and alternate bscu_subsystem instances are in a failed state; the system shall enter an alternate operational state if the primary subsystem is failed while the alternate subsystem remains operational, or if both subsystems are operational but the select_alternate component is in a failed state; the system shall remain in a fully operational state only if both bscu_subsystem instances and the select_alternate component are in operational states. Concurrent loss of power to both external power inputs shall trigger a transition to the failed state for the generic, federated, and ima bscu implementations.

Deployment binding and scheduling rules shall be enforced per implementation variant to meet safety and temporal isolation requirements. For the bscu.federated implementation, the command and monitor processes of the primary bscu_subsystem instance shall be bound exclusively to the first central processing unit of the federated platform subcomponent, and the command and monitor processes of the alternate bscu_subsystem instance shall be bound exclusively to the second independent central processing unit of the federated platform subcomponent. Scheduling on federated platform processors shall enforce strict temporal separation between primary and alternate channel execution to prevent cross-channel fault propagation. For the bscu.ima implementation, the command process of the primary subsystem shall be bound exclusively to the first partition of the shared IMA platform central processing unit, the monitor process of the primary subsystem shall be bound exclusively to the second partition of the shared IMA central processing unit, the command process of the alternate subsystem shall be bound exclusively to the third partition of the shared IMA central processing unit, and the monitor process of the alternate subsystem shall be bound exclusively to the fourth partition of the shared IMA central processing unit. IMA partition scheduling shall enforce strict temporal and spatial isolation between all bound processes per ARINC 653 requirements to prevent fault propagation between processes sharing the same physical processor. Safety-related property constraints shall be applied per ARP4761 and EMV2 rules to meet certification requirements. The invalid report error event of the monitor process shall be classified as a minor hazard with a probable qualitative probability objective, describing a spurious monitor output that causes an invalid temporary switch to the alternate channel. The failed state of a single bscu_subsystem instance shall be classified as a major hazard with a probable qualitative probability objective, describing total failure of one BSCU channel, with a fixed occurrence probability of 3.3e-5 per operational period; this fault condition is noted to become catastrophic if both primary and alternate channels fail concurrently. The internal selection error event of the select_alternate component shall be classified as a hazardous hazard with an extremely improbable qualitative probability objective, describing an incorrect validity assessment that causes an uncommanded switch to the alternate channel without an actual primary channel fault, with a Poisson-distributed occurrence probability of 3.6e-6 per operational period, assigned a severity level of hazardous and likelihood level of extremely improbable per EMV2 property rules. Loss of a single external power supply to the bscu shall be classified as a hazardous hazard with an extremely improbable qualitative probability objective, while concurrent loss of both external power supplies shall be classified as a catastrophic hazard with an extremely improbable qualitative probability objective, describing permanent total loss of BSCU function. End-to-end latency for pedal input to command output delivery, and for validity fault detection to channel selection output delivery, shall be bounded to meet braking system response requirements, with no additional latency introduced by cross-partition or cross-processor communication paths beyond platform-enforced communication delays.

All data exchanged via component ports shall use strongly typed data definitions sourced exclusively from imported packages, with no implicit type conversions permitted at connection points. Pedal position values shall use the common::command.pedal data type, brake command values shall use the common::command.brake data type, skid command values shall use the common::command.skid data type, and all boolean validity status and channel selection flag values shall use the Base_Types::Boolean data type representing a binary true or false state. All power distribution connections shall use the common::power.generic bus type, which supports propagation of no-power error states to all connected components when the power supply is lost. All data port communications shall follow sampled port semantics, where only the most recently produced data value is delivered to the receiving component on each execution cycle, with no queuing of historical data values. Error propagation across all port and bus connections shall follow EMV2 rules, where only explicitly declared error types are transmitted across connection points, with error transformation logic defined per component error behavior specifications to map incoming error types to appropriate outgoing error types as required for fault impact analysis and FMEA reporting. All data type and bus definitions shall be reusable across other aircraft system models, with no model-specific modifications made to imported type or bus definitions within the bscu package.

The system shall define an independent public shared package named common, with all internal elements declared as publicly accessible. This package holds no dependencies on external AADL packages, and hosts globally reusable bus types, bus implementations, data types, and data implementations. No functional components including processors, processes, threads, or devices shall be defined within this package. All elements contained in the package have no cross-package reference requirements, and complete the binding between type declarations and corresponding implementations entirely within the public scope of the common package.

The system shall define three distinct bus components within the common package, with no externally exposed functional interaction ports or internal subcomponent structure specified at the bus type level. The first bus component is the power bus type, designed to support system-wide power transmission, paired with a generic bus implementation identified as power.generic. This implementation includes no additional attribute configurations or internal connection logic, and is applicable to universal power delivery scenarios. The second bus component is the pwm bus type, designed to support system-wide pulse width modulation signal transmission, paired with a generic bus implementation identified as pwm.generic. This implementation includes no additional attribute configurations or internal connection logic, and is applicable to universal PWM control signal delivery scenarios. The third bus component is the pressure bus type, designed to carry pressure signals sent and received between connected devices, pump units and other system nodes, paired with a standard bus implementation identified as pressure.i. This implementation includes no additional attribute configurations or internal connection logic, and is applicable to cross-component pressure signal interaction scenarios. The system shall define one base data component named command within the common package, which acts as the parent type for all concrete control instruction data, with no fixed internal data field constraints specified at the data type level. The command data type is paired with four scenario-specific concrete data implementations, all of which contain no additional internal data field extensions or nested substructures. The first data implementation is command.brake, which carries brake control instruction payloads. The second data implementation is command.skid, which carries skid control instruction payloads. The third data implementation is command.pedal, which carries pedal operation instruction payloads. The fourth data implementation is command.announce, which carries system announcement and prompt instruction payloads.

As a foundational resource definition package, the common package does not define independent end-to-end data flow paths natively. All bus types and implementations defined in the package provide logical and physical bearer channels for cross-component energy, signal, and data transmission in upper-level system architecture. All data types and implementations defined in the package provide standardized format specifications for information payloads exchanged between distributed system components. When upper-level systems construct concrete data flow links, they may directly bind the corresponding bus implementation as the transmission carrier, and instantiate the corresponding data implementation as the transmitted interaction payload.

All bus and data elements defined in the common package are not bound to dedicated timing scheduling rules, and are not configured with fixed end-to-end or per-hop latency constraint parameters. All timing-related attributes, scheduling execution policies, and latency performance indicators shall be configured by upper-level functional components that reference these foundational resources, in accordance with specific application scenario requirements. The foundational resources in the common package maintain a generic, unbound state, and impose no mandatory restrictions on the scheduling strategies or latency metrics adopted by upper-level applications.

For public data type definition, a hierarchical structure consisting of a base type and scenario-specific implementations shall be applied. The base command type defines the classification category for general instruction-class data, while each scenario-specific data implementation corresponds to a concrete business-domain instruction type. Data implementations do not predefine fixed field lengths, encoding rules, or data resolution parameters, to reserve sufficient extension space for upper-level application adaptation across different deployment contexts. For public communication bus definition, a hierarchical structure consisting of a bus type and corresponding general or standard implementation shall be applied. Each bus type explicitly defines its applicable scenario: the power bus supports power energy transmission scenarios, the pwm bus supports pulse width modulation control signal transmission scenarios, and the pressure bus supports pressure measurement and control signal transmission scenarios. Each bus implementation does not predefine hardware-specific parameters such as bandwidth, transmission rate, or electrical interface characteristics, to reserve sufficient extension space for upper-level adaptation across different hardware platforms. All bus implementations are generic foundational units with no embedded internal logic, and may be directly bound and referenced by bus access ports of upper-level components.

A public AADL package named communication shall be defined to encapsulate modeling elements associated with system annunciation functionality. The communication package shall declare explicit import dependencies on three external packages: the common package for shared public data type definitions, the EMV2 package for standardized error modeling annex support, and the ARP4761 package for aviation system safety and hazard analysis property support. The communication package shall not contain nested subpackages, and shall define a single device type named annunciation as its core functional element. The annunciation device is specified to abstract the system’s annunciation capability at an abstraction level sufficient to represent communication error scenarios that cause total loss of annunciation function, with modeling logic aligned to the fault tree error injection approach described in ARP4761 document page 199, figure L3. Overly sophisticated internal logic of physical annunciation hardware shall not be modeled at this abstraction level, as the core modeling purpose of the device is to represent an error source that propagates fault effects to the top-level system. A single device implementation identified as i shall be provided for the annunciation device type, and this implementation shall contain no internal subcomponents, internal connections, or standalone annex definitions, representing the minimal structural implementation of the annunciation device.

The annunciation device type shall define exactly one external interaction feature, which is an output data port named information. No input data ports, event ports, event data ports, bus access points, subprogram access points, or parameter connection points shall be defined for the annunciation device type. The annunciation.i implementation shall not define any additional external features beyond those inherited from the annunciation device type, and shall not expose internal subcomponent interfaces to the external environment. For error propagation interfaces, the annunciation device shall define an outbound error propagation path bound to the information output port, where the only permitted propagated error type is the NoService loss-of-service error.

Under normal operational conditions, the annunciation device acts as the originating source of annunciation information, generating and transmitting annunciation data conforming to the bound port data type outwards through the information output port. The device shall not accept incoming data from external components as input to generate its output annunciation content. A designated error flow labeled f1 shall be defined for the device, which treats the information port as an error source point that propagates NoService errors outwards to connected external components. When the device enters a failed state, normal annunciation data transmission on the information port shall cease, and the NoService error shall be transmitted along the same port connection path to connected upstream system elements, forming a complete fault propagation path for loss of annunciation capability across the device’s system boundary.

The annunciation device shall implement a two-state error behavior model for operational state tracking. The two defined states are the Operational state representing normal functional operation, and the Failed state representing total loss of annunciation function, with the device initializing in the Operational state on system startup. A single internal error event named LossAnnunciation shall be defined as the sole trigger for functional state transition. A single state transition labeled t1 shall be specified, which moves the device from the Operational state to the Failed state immediately upon occurrence of the LossAnnunciation event, with no intermediate states or guard conditions applied to the transition. A single error propagation rule labeled p1 shall be defined, which triggers unconditionally when the device is in the Failed state to propagate the NoService error to the information output port, with no additional trigger events or conditional checks applied to this propagation. The LossAnnunciation error event shall be assigned an occurrence distribution property per EMV2 specification, set to a fixed probability distribution with a probability value of 1.00. The LossAnnunciation event shall be associated with ARP4761 hazard properties as follows: the hazard cross-reference shall point to content from AIR6110 and ARP4761 corresponding to ARP4761 page 199, figure 3, the associated failure mode shall be Loss of Annunciation, the hazard shall apply to all operational phases of the system, the hazard description shall state that the system cannot annunciate errors, the failure condition classification shall be set to Catastrophic, the qualitative probability objective for the hazard shall be set to ExtremelyImprobable, and no additional comment text shall be attached to the hazard entry. No explicit periodic task scheduling rules, execution offset constraints, or end-to-end communication latency limits shall be defined for the annunciation device or its implementation, as the device operates as an event-driven source of data and fault effects without scheduled periodic execution requirements.

The communication package shall not define any custom bus types, bus implementations, or native data types within its scope. All data transmitted across the information port shall use the pre-defined announce data type located under the command namespace of the imported common package, with no local modification or extension to this data type permitted within the communication package. All error modeling types and behavior constructs used in the device error model shall be imported from the pre-defined error_library, specifically utilizing the simple error behavior set from the error library, with no custom error types or error behavior states defined locally in the communication package. All port-based communication for the annunciation device shall use the standard AADL data port communication mechanism, with no dedicated custom communication bus specified for annunciation data transmission at this modeling abstraction level.

A public AADL package named error_library shall be constructed as an independent reusable error modeling repository. The package shall have no external dependencies on other AADL packages, and shall embed an EMV2 annex to host standardized error modeling artifacts. All elements defined within the package shall be publicly accessible to all external AADL models that import the library via with statements. The package shall not contain instantiable runtime components such as hardware, software, or concrete system implementation units, and shall only provide reusable error type definitions and error behavior state machine templates to support consistent error modeling for upper-level system components.

As a static modeling definition repository, the error_library package shall not define instantiable runtime components including processes, threads, devices, processors, or bus components. No runtime functional interaction ports, internal component connection interfaces, or feature access points shall be specified within the package. All artifacts contained in the package shall serve as type-level modeling templates, and shall not define runtime instance-level interaction interfaces or contract specifications.

The error_library package shall not define runtime functional components or end-to-end data interaction links, so no runtime service data flow transmission paths shall be specified within the library. Error propagation logic implied by the library’s state machine templates shall only act as a reference for upper-level component instances when configuring their proprietary error behavior, and no concrete cross-component error propagation paths or fault propagation routes shall be defined in the library.

The error_library package shall not contain schedulable runtime entities such as threads, thread groups, or processes, so no runtime scheduling rules, execution periods, latency limits, deadline constraints, dispatch protocols, or time-related execution attributes shall be specified within the library. Error events and recovery events defined in the library’s error behavior templates shall only act as type identifiers for state machine transition triggers, and shall not be bound to specific time trigger thresholds, timeout values, or occurrence probability parameters.

All error type definitions within the EMV2 annex of the package shall follow a hierarchical inheritance structure. A top-level error type NoPower shall be defined to represent power supply loss faults. A top-level error type NoService shall be defined to represent service unavailability faults. A top-level error type ValueError shall be defined to represent abnormal data value faults, and a second-level error type NoValue shall be derived from ValueError to represent complete value missing faults, with full inheritance of all attributes and propagation rules associated with the ValueError type. A top-level error type PlatformFailure shall be defined to represent generic platform-level faults, and two second-level error types shall be derived from PlatformFailure: HardwareFailure to represent physical hardware faults with full inheritance of PlatformFailure attributes, and SoftwareFailure to represent executable software faults with full inheritance of PlatformFailure attributes.

Six reusable error behavior state machine templates shall be defined within the EMV2 annex for reference by upper-level components during error model configuration. The first state machine, identified as ThreeState, shall include three mutually exclusive states: Operational as the initial state representing normal component operation, NonCriticalModeFailure representing faults that do not impact critical functional modes, and CriticalModeFailure representing faults that disrupt critical functional modes; no trigger events or state transition logic shall be defined for this state machine template. The second state machine, identified as ThreeErrorStates, shall define three error trigger events typed as error events: BadValueEvent for invalid or out-of-range value occurrences, NoValueEvent for complete missing value occurrences, and LateValueEvent for value delivery beyond allowed time windows; this state machine shall include four mutually exclusive states, with Operational as the initial normal operation state, and three dedicated fault states including BadValueState, NoValueState, and LateValueState corresponding to the three defined error events respectively; transition logic for this state machine shall specify that a component in the Operational state shall transition to BadValueState upon activation of BadValueEvent, transition to NoValueState upon activation of NoValueEvent, and transition to LateValueState upon activation of LateValueEvent; no recovery transitions or transitions between fault states shall be defined for this state machine template. The third state machine, identified as Simple, shall include two mutually exclusive states: Operational as the initial normal operation state, and Failed representing permanent, unrecovered fault conditions; no trigger events or state transition logic shall be defined for this state machine template. The fourth state machine, identified as bscu, shall include three mutually exclusive states: Operational as the initial normal operation state, Alternate representing degraded operation in backup functional mode, and Failed representing permanent fault conditions that halt all function provision; no trigger events or state transition logic shall be defined for this state machine template. The fifth state machine, identified as WBS, shall include six mutually exclusive states: Operational as the initial normal operation state, and five fault states including AnnunciatedBrakingLoss representing braking function loss with active crew alert, UnannunciatedBrakingLoss representing braking function loss without active crew alert, PartialBrakingLoss representing partial loss of braking capability, AsymmetricLoss representing unequal braking force across symmetric wheel sets, and InadvertentBrake representing uncommanded brake activation during non-braking operational phases; no trigger events or state transition logic shall be defined for this state machine template. The sixth state machine, identified as SimpleAndTransient, shall define three trigger events: Failure typed as an error event for permanent, non-recoverable fault occurrences, FailureTransient typed as an error event for temporary, recoverable fault occurrences, and ResetEvent typed as a recovery event for intentional component reset actions; this state machine shall include three mutually exclusive states, with Operational as the initial normal operation state, Failed representing permanent fault conditions, and TransientFailure representing temporary fault conditions; transition logic for this state machine shall specify that a component in the Operational state shall transition to the Failed state upon activation of the Failure event, transition to the TransientFailure state upon activation of the FailureTransient event, and a component in the TransientFailure state shall transition back to the Operational state upon activation of the ResetEvent; no recovery transition logic shall be defined for components entering the Failed state.

No communication bus types, bus implementations, bus instances, bus access interfaces, or bus-associated attributes including communication protocol specifications, bandwidth limits, transmission latency values, or fault containment rules for buses shall be defined within the error_library package. All bus-related definitions shall be supplemented by upper-level system models that import the error library, aligned with specific application scenario and architecture requirements.

The system shall establish a standalone public AADL package named pedals to encapsulate all pedal system component definitions. The pedals package shall declare formal import dependencies on three external supporting packages: the common package to access shared cross-system data type definitions, the EMV2 annex package to enable standardized error modeling constructs, and the ARP4761 annex package to support aviation safety assessment property assignments. Within the pedals package, a system component type named pedals shall be defined to represent the abstract pedal system interface and associated behavior, and a single concrete system implementation named pedals.generic shall be provided as a stub instantiation of the pedals system type, with no internal subcomponent decomposition specified in the current implementation.

The pedals system type shall define two identical outbound data port features as its complete external functional interface, designated signal1 and signal2. Both ports shall operate as unidirectional out ports carrying data to connected downstream components. The pedals.generic system implementation shall not define internal subcomponents, internal port connections, or internal feature mappings, consistent with its role as an initial stub component for early system architecture integration.

Nominal functional data flow for the pedals system shall consist of pedal command values generated within the component, transmitted outward across the system boundary via both signal1 and signal2 out ports, with no inbound data ports or incoming data flows required to support core pedal signal generation functionality. For error-related flow paths, the system shall define two explicit error source flows, labeled f1 and f2, which originate at the external interface of signal1 and signal2 respectively, to propagate defined error states from the pedals component to connected downstream elements without traversing internal subcomponent error paths. The defined error propagation for both ports shall carry the NoService error state when activated.

The pedals system shall implement a state-based error behavior model aligned with EMV2 specifications to govern fault response and state transitions. The system shall initialize in the fully functional Operational state at system start. A single discrete internal error event named InternalFault shall be defined as the sole trigger for fault-related state changes; upon occurrence of the InternalFault event, the system shall execute an immediate, unconditional transition from the Operational state to the Failed state. When operating in the Failed state, the system shall immediately and unconditionally propagate the NoService error condition out through both the signal1 and signal2 out ports, with no guard conditions or added delay applied to this error propagation. No explicit periodic or aperiodic task scheduling rules, port transmission latency budgets, or end-to-end flow timing constraints shall be specified for the current stub implementation of the pedals system, with such timing requirements reserved for subsequent detailed design refinement.

All functional data transmitted across the signal1 and signal2 out ports shall strictly conform to the pedal command data type defined at the common::command path within the imported common package, with no custom pedal-specific data types defined locally within the pedals package. No dedicated communication bus components or bus access features shall be defined within the pedals package, as direct port-to-port data communication is used for all external signal exchanges between the pedals component and connected downstream elements. The error model for the pedals component shall import the standardized error type set and simple error behavior definitions from the shared error_library to ensure consistent error state representation across the broader system model. Safety properties aligned with ARP4761 standards shall be applied to the NoService error propagation on both signal1 and signal2 ports, classifying the associated hazard as Hazardous with a qualitative probability objective of ExtremelyRemote. The documented hazard for this NoService condition describes a failure mode where no pedal signal is transmitted to downstream components, preventing the BSCU from generating valid brake control outputs, with an associated note that concurrent loss of both system power supplies would escalate the severity of this failure condition to critical. Hazard metadata fields including cross-reference identifiers and applicable operational flight phases shall be marked as TBD for population during later safety assessment activities. An EMV2 occurrence distribution property shall be assigned to the pedals system Failed state, specifying a fixed probability distribution with a probability value of 3.4e-5 for system entry into the Failed state due to internal fault occurrence.

The root modeling module is a public AADL package named platform, which declares mandatory dependencies on the EMV2 error modeling annex property set and the ARP4761 aviation safety assessment property set to support error behavior specification and safety property annotation. No additional external package dependencies are permitted for this package. All component type and implementation definitions within the package are exposed as public elements, with no private component definitions included. The package defines three core component types: a virtual processor type named partition that models partition runtime management functionality for integrated modular avionics configurations, a processor type named cpu that models generic physical central processing unit hardware, and a system type named platform that acts as the top-level container for complete computing platform assemblies. Four component implementations are defined to support two distinct platform architectures: a generic virtual processor implementation named partition.generic for the partition type, which provides base partition runtime functionality without specialized configuration; two processor implementations for the cpu type, named cpu.ima for integrated modular avionics processing hardware and cpu.single for standalone federated architecture processing hardware; and two system implementations for the platform type, named platform.ima for the fully integrated modular avionics platform configuration and platform.federated for the distributed federated platform configuration. Strict dependency hierarchy is enforced across implementations: the cpu.ima processor implementation depends exclusively on the partition.generic virtual processor implementation for its internal subcomponents, the platform.ima system implementation depends exclusively on the cpu.ima processor implementation for its internal subcomponent, the platform.federated system implementation depends exclusively on the cpu.single processor implementation for its internal subcomponents, and no cross-dependencies are permitted between the integrated modular avionics and federated architecture implementation branches.

All components in the package define no functional data, event, or event data ports, with all interaction points limited to EMV2 error propagation interfaces aligned with safety modeling requirements. The partition virtual processor type defines two external error propagation interfaces: an outgoing propagation point named bindings that transmits both SoftwareFailure and HardwareFailure error types to software components bound to the partition, and an incoming propagation point named processor that receives HardwareFailure error types from the underlying physical processor hosting the partition. The partition.generic virtual processor implementation inherits all interface definitions from the partition type, defines no internal subcomponents, and adds no additional external or internal interfaces. The base cpu processor type defines a single external outgoing error propagation interface named bindings that transmits HardwareFailure error types to all hosted partition and software components. The cpu.ima processor implementation inherits the external bindings error propagation interface from the base cpu type, and defines four identical internal subcomponents instantiated from the partition.generic virtual processor, named partition1, partition2, partition3, and partition4 respectively; no additional external interfaces are added in this implementation, and each internal partition subcomponent is logically bound to the host cpu hardware to receive hardware failure propagations from the processor. The cpu.single processor implementation inherits the external bindings error propagation interface from the base cpu type, adds one additional external outgoing error propagation interface named processor that transmits SoftwareFailure error types to hosted application components, and defines no internal subcomponents to reflect the lack of separate partition runtime layers in federated standalone processors. The top-level platform system type defines no external interfaces of any kind, as it functions as a closed assembly of internal platform computing resources. The platform.ima system implementation inherits the empty external interface set from the platform type, and defines a single internal subcomponent instantiated from the cpu.ima processor, named cpu. The platform.federated system implementation inherits the empty external interface set from the platform type, and defines two identical internal subcomponents instantiated from the cpu.single processor, named cpu1 and cpu2 respectively, with no logical connection between the two processor instances to maintain fault isolation between federated resources. Each component type and implementation defines internal error events per its error behavior specification: the partition type defines an internal SoftwareFailure error event, the base cpu type defines an internal InternalFailure error event, and the cpu.single implementation defines an additional internal SoftwareFailure error event separate from the inherited hardware InternalFailure event. All components use the two-state simple error behavior model, with an initial Operational state and a terminal Failed state, where internal error events trigger a one-way transition from Operational to Failed with no recovery transitions defined.

All flows within the platform package are EMV2 error propagation flows, as no functional application data paths are defined at the platform abstraction layer. The partition virtual processor defines two formal error flows: an error source flow named fsoft that originates from the internal SoftwareFailure event and propagates out of the component via the bindings outgoing point as a SoftwareFailure error, and an error path flow named fhard that receives incoming HardwareFailure errors from the processor incoming point and passes these errors unmodified out through the bindings outgoing point. When a partition component is in the Operational state, all propagations via the bindings point carry a NoError value to indicate normal runtime operation; when a partition transitions to the Failed state due to an internal SoftwareFailure event, all propagations via the bindings point carry a SoftwareFailure value. The base cpu processor type defines a single error source flow named f1 that originates from the internal InternalFailure event and propagates out of the component via the bindings outgoing point as a HardwareFailure error. When a cpu component is in the Operational state, all propagations via the bindings point carry a NoError value; when a cpu transitions to the Failed state due to an internal InternalFailure event, all propagations via the bindings point carry a HardwareFailure value. For the cpu.ima implementation, HardwareFailure errors exiting the cpu via the bindings point are implicitly routed to the incoming processor error point of each of the four internal partition subcomponents via the standard virtual processor to physical processor binding mechanism defined in EMV2, triggering the fhard error path in each partition to pass hardware failure errors out through each partition's bindings point to hosted application software. No additional software failure flows are defined at the cpu.ima level, as all software runtime failures for integrated modular avionics configurations are contained within individual partition subcomponents rather than originating at the processor hardware layer. For the cpu.single implementation, an additional error source flow named fsoft is defined that originates from the implementation's internal SoftwareFailure event and propagates out of the component via the processor outgoing point as a SoftwareFailure error. When a cpu.single component is in the Operational state, all propagations via the processor point carry a NoError value; when a cpu.single transitions to the Failed state due to an internal SoftwareFailure event, all propagations via the processor point carry a SoftwareFailure value. The inherited hardware failure flow f1 from the base cpu type remains fully active in the cpu.single implementation, propagating hardware failures out through the original bindings point. For the platform.ima system implementation, all error flows are fully contained within the single internal cpu.ima subcomponent, with no error propagation across the platform system boundary consistent with the lack of external interfaces. For the platform.federated system implementation, all error flows are fully contained within the two isolated internal cpu.single subcomponents, with no error propagation across the platform system boundary and no error propagation connections between the two separate cpu instances to preserve federated fault isolation.

No functional task scheduling parameters, execution time budgets, partition scheduling window definitions, core allocation rules, or end-to-end functional latency constraints are specified within this platform package, as the model scope is limited to static platform structure and error propagation behavior, with those runtime configuration properties deferred to later application integration stages. No shared resource access latency or communication latency constraints are defined, as no communication resources or shared resource access protocols are modeled in this package. Temporal properties are defined exclusively for error event and error flow occurrence rates, aligned with ARP4761 safety assessment requirements. The SoftwareFailure error event on the partition virtual processor is assigned a Major failure severity classification per ARP4761, with a Probable qualitative likelihood objective; this failure applies across all operational phases, describes platform software failures such as operating system exceptions that impact all software components bound to the affected partition, and follows a Poisson occurrence distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5 per operational exposure period, with an associated hazard entry marked with a TBD cross-reference, empty formal failure identifier, and note describing the full impact scope of the failure. The InternalFailure error event on the base cpu processor type is assigned a Major failure severity classification per ARP4761, with a Probable qualitative likelihood objective; this failure applies across all operational phases, describes hardware failures of processing components or attached devices that impact all software hosted on the affected hardware, and follows a Poisson occurrence distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5 per operational exposure period, with an associated hazard entry marked with a TBD cross-reference, empty formal failure identifier, and note describing the full impact scope of the failure. The hardware failure error flow f1 on the base cpu type is assigned a Fixed occurrence distribution with a probability value of 6.75e-5 per operational exposure period. The SoftwareFailure error event on the cpu.single processor implementation is assigned a Major failure severity classification per ARP4761, with a Probable qualitative likelihood objective; this failure applies across all operational phases, describes platform software failures such as operating system exceptions that impact all software components hosted on the affected federated processor, and follows a Poisson occurrence distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5 per operational exposure period, with an associated hazard entry marked with a TBD cross-reference, empty formal failure identifier, and note describing the full impact scope of the failure. No redundant error detection, fault recovery, or reconfiguration timing constraints are defined for any component, as no recovery state transitions are included in the error behavior models.

No custom application data types, error types, or data implementations are defined within the platform package. All error types used in propagation interfaces, error flows, and error behavior definitions, including NoError, SoftwareFailure, and HardwareFailure, are imported from the external public error_library package, and all error behavior logic conforms to the simple two-state error behavior state machine defined in that library. No local modification, extension, or redefinition of imported error types or behavior models is permitted within the platform package to ensure consistency across dependent system models. No physical bus components, virtual bus components, bus access interfaces, or bus-related property definitions are included in the platform package, as the current model scope is limited to computing hardware and partition runtime components without modeling inter-component communication infrastructure.

The entire modeled domain is encapsulated within a public package named power. The power package shall declare explicit dependencies on three external packages to support cross-package element referencing: the common package for shared generic resource definitions, the ARP4761 package for aviation safety assessment standard property definitions, and the EMV2 package for error modeling annex semantic definitions. Two top-level component types shall be defined within the power package: a device component typed as battery, and a system component typed as power. Each component type shall be paired with one generic implementation variant, specifically battery.generic for the battery device type, and power.generic for the power system type. The battery component shall act as a leaf-level hardware device module with no nested subcomponents in its implementation. The power component shall act as an aggregate system-level module that depends on the battery component type to construct its internal subcomponent structure.

The battery device component shall define a single external feature: a provided bus access port named socket, which conforms to the generic power bus type defined as common::power.generic. The battery component shall implement EMV2 error model constructs, which import type definitions from the standard error_library, and import the simple error behavior definitions from error_library to support state machine specification. The battery component shall define error propagation interfaces aligned with EMV2 semantics, where the socket port supports outward propagation of the NoPower error, with a defined error source path f1 that sources the NoPower error directly at the socket port. The battery component shall define internal error behavior constructs including two distinct error events: the Depleted event representing total battery charge exhaustion, and the Explode event representing catastrophic battery structural failure. The battery component shall have two discrete operational states for error behavior: the Operational state representing nominal functional status, and the Failed state representing loss of intended function. State transition rules for the battery component shall specify that a transition from the Operational state to the Failed state is triggered by either the Depleted error event or the Explode error event. Error propagation rules tied to component state shall specify that when the component resides in the Operational state, the socket port propagates a NoError status via propagation path normal, and when the component resides in the Failed state, the socket port propagates the NoPower error via propagation path p1. The battery.generic device implementation shall not define additional subcomponents, internal connections, or extended features, and shall fully inherit all interface and behavior definitions from the battery component type. The power system component shall define two external provided bus access ports, named line1 and line2 respectively, both of which conform to the common::power.generic power bus type. The power.generic system implementation shall define two internal subcomponents, both instantiated from the battery.generic device type, named battery1 and battery2 respectively. The power.generic implementation shall define two bidirectional bus access connections: the connection named pwr1 shall link the socket port of the battery1 subcomponent to the external line1 port of the power system, and the connection named pwr2 shall link the socket port of the battery2 subcomponent to the external line2 port of the power system. No additional internal connections or cross-links between subcomponents shall be defined in the power.generic implementation.

Power supply as the core transmitted entity shall flow along the bidirectional bus access paths within the power system. External power-consuming loads connected to the power system shall receive power supply from the battery1 subcomponent via the line1 external port, through the direct connection between battery1.socket and line1, and shall receive power supply from the battery2 subcomponent via the line2 external port, through the direct connection between battery2.socket and line2. The two power supply paths shall be fully independent with no cross-over power flow, no intermediate power conversion, and no internal signal processing between subcomponent output ports and system external ports. Error states shall propagate along the same physical paths as nominal power flow. When either battery subcomponent transitions to the Failed state due to an internal error event, the associated NoPower error shall propagate sequentially from the subcomponent socket port, across the internal bus connection, to the corresponding external system line port, and onward to connected downstream loads. When a battery subcomponent remains in the Operational state, no error condition shall propagate along its connected supply path.

All components defined within the power package are hardware device and system constructs, with no defined thread, process, or other software executable units. As such, no periodic scheduling, event-triggered task scheduling, priority assignment, or execution deadline constraints shall apply to elements in the package. The power supply paths are persistent hardware conduction paths with no protocol-induced scheduling overhead. Error state propagation shall be strictly synchronous with component state transitions: immediately following a component state change triggered by an internal error event, the corresponding port error status shall be updated and propagated to all connected bus endpoints, with no intentional propagation delay configured.

All bus access ports defined within the power package shall reuse the pre-defined common::power.generic generic power bus type from the common package; no new bus types shall be defined locally within the power package. All bus access connections shall represent bidirectional hardware power delivery paths capable of supporting the electrical interface requirements of the generic power bus. Error types used in the EMV2 annex for the battery component shall be imported from the referenced external error library, including the NoError and NoPower error types, with no custom error data types defined locally within the power package. Safety and reliability property values shall be configured per defined rules: for the NoPower error propagated from the battery socket port, ARP4761 hazard properties shall be set to reference ARP4761 page 277 figure 9, describe the failure as loss of one power source with critical risk if both primary and redundant sources are lost, apply to the Landing and RTO flight phases, describe the effect as loss of electrical power to the BSCU, assign a FailureConditionClassification of Major, set a QualitativeProbabilityObjective of Probable, and note that dual power loss constitutes a major hazard. The EMV2 OccurrenceDistribution property for the socket.NoPower error shall be configured to use a Poisson distribution with a probability value of 1.35e-5. For the internal Explode error event of the battery component, ARP4761 hazard properties shall be set with a to-be-determined cross reference, describe the failure as battery explosion, apply to all flight phases, describe the effect as a major physical hazard, assign a FailureConditionClassification of Catastrophic, set a QualitativeProbabilityObjective of ExtremelyImprobable, and note that the failure causes physical impact to adjacent components. For the internal Depleted error event of the battery component, ARP4761 hazard properties shall be set with a to-be-determined cross reference, describe the failure as battery charge depletion, apply to all flight phases, describe the effect as total loss of stored battery power, assign a FailureConditionClassification of Major, set a QualitativeProbabilityObjective of Probable, and note that the failure becomes a system-level concern if the redundant battery also fails.

The system shall define a publicly accessible AADL package named WBS_Proofs to serve as the dedicated namespace for all wheel brake system geometry conformance proof constructs. The package shall not declare import dependencies on any external AADL packages, as all logic contained within the package is fully self-contained. The public section of the package shall include a single package-level Resolute annex subclause to host all executable assurance claim definitions, helper functions, and external analysis invocation logic. No additional top-level AADL declarations including component types, component implementations, data types, or bus definitions shall be placed directly in the public package section outside the Resolute annex subclause.

Within the package-level Resolute annex, three parameterless top-level assurance claims shall be defined as the externally accessible validation entry points for geometry conformance checks. The first entry point, identified as contain_two_bscu, shall encapsulate the check for required BSCU components in the referenced system geometry model. The second entry point, identified as contain_two_selector_valve, shall encapsulate the check for required selector valve components in the referenced system geometry model. The third entry point, identified as contain_two_power_supply, shall encapsulate the check for required electrical power supply components in the referenced system geometry model. A single internal reusable helper function named contains_geometry shall be defined within the same Resolute annex scope to support execution of the three top-level claims, with a formal input interface accepting three positional parameters: a string value specifying the full file system path of the target geometry model file, a string value specifying the exact component name to search for within the geometry model, and an integer value specifying the minimum required count of components matching the target name. The contains_geometry helper function shall have scope restricted to invocation by constructs within the same Resolute annex, and shall not be exposed as an external validation entry point for referencing models. Each top-level claim shall invoke the contains_geometry helper with fixed hardcoded parameter values: the contain_two_bscu claim shall pass the file path value "C:\\jjc.stp", component name value "BSCU", and required count value of 1; the contain_two_selector_valve claim shall pass the file path value "C:\\jjc.stp", component name value "SELECTOR VALVE", and required count value of 2; the contain_two_power_supply claim shall pass the file path value "C:\\jjc.stp", component name value "ELECTRICAL POWER SUPPLY", and required count value of 2.

During execution of architecture validation activities, data shall flow along a fixed linear path for each top-level assurance claim. When a top-level claim is triggered by the Resolute assurance framework, the fixed parameter values hardcoded in the claim definition shall be passed directly as input arguments to the internal contains_geometry helper function, with no intermediate data transformation or persistent storage applied to the parameter values. Upon receiving the input parameters, the contains_geometry helper function shall pass the three received values as sequential positional arguments to the external ngrep geometry analysis utility. The ngrep utility shall access the geometry file at the specified file path, scan the file content to count elements matching the provided component name, compare the counted value against the required minimum count, and generate a boolean pass or fail result. This result shall be passed directly back from the ngrep utility to the contains_geometry helper function, which propagates the result unchanged to the calling top-level claim. The top-level claim shall then return the final boolean result to the Resolute framework to indicate whether the geometry conformance requirement is satisfied. No branching data paths, feedback loops, or parallel data processing steps shall be included in the validation logic flow.

No runtime task scheduling configurations, execution priority assignments, periodic trigger rules, event-triggered activation logic, or hard end-to-end latency constraints shall be defined within the WBS_Proofs package. All logic contained in the package supports offline architecture verification activities that execute outside the operational runtime context of the deployed wheel brake system, and thus is not subject to the real-time scheduling rules applied to runtime system components. Invocation of the top-level assurance claims and supporting helper functions shall occur synchronously when triggered by a user-initiated or automated architecture validation workflow. No mandatory upper bound shall be imposed on the execution duration of the ngrep analysis utility or the associated Resolute function calls, as execution time may vary based on host system performance and geometry file size.

All parameter values exchanged between Resolute functions within the package, and between the contains_geometry helper function and the external ngrep analysis utility, shall use built-in primitive data types natively supported by the Resolute annex language. String data type shall be used for all values representing file system paths and component name identifiers, and integer data type shall be used for all values representing minimum required component counts. No custom user-defined AADL data types shall be declared within the WBS_Proofs package, as all data exchange uses the supported primitive types. No AADL bus, virtual bus, bus access interface, or formal communication protocol definition shall be included in the WBS_Proofs package, as the contained validation logic does not model runtime inter-component communication paths for the deployed wheel brake system. Data exchange between Resolute functions and the external ngrep utility shall use direct in-memory parameter passing with positional argument ordering, and shall not require dedicated communication bus infrastructure, message encoding rules, or transport layer protocols.

The system shall define a standalone AADL package named pump, with all model elements declared in the package’s public scope accessible to external dependent models. The pump package shall declare three mandatory external package dependencies at the public level, consisting of the common package for shared interface and data type specifications, the ARP4761 package for civil aviation safety assessment property definitions, and the EMV2 package for error modeling annex capability support. The pump package shall not contain nested sub-packages, and all component type and implementation declarations shall reside within the public section of the package.

The pump package shall define a top-level system type named pump. The pump system shall expose a single provided bus access feature identified as pressure_output, which is bound to the pressure interface instance i defined in the common package. The pump system shall support outbound error propagation through the pressure_output feature, with NoService as the only propagable error state on this interface. A named error source flow named nopressure shall be defined for this error propagation path, marking the pressure_output interface as the origination point of NoService error for end-to-end error propagation analysis. A corresponding system implementation identified as pump.i shall be declared for the pump system type. The pump.i implementation shall not define internal subcomponents, internal features, port groups, or internal connection structures, forming a minimal leaf-level system implementation with no nested composition.

The pump system shall operate as a root source of pressure transmission service, delivering valid, error-free pressure service to externally connected components via the pressure_output provided bus access interface during normal functional operation. No internal data forwarding paths between subcomponents exist within the pump.i implementation, as all output service states are generated directly by the pump system’s own operational status rather than forwarded from internal sub-elements. When the pump enters a failed operational state, it shall immediately cease delivery of normal pressure service and transmit corresponding service failure status through the same pressure_output interface to connected downstream components.

The pump system shall implement a two-state component error behavior model, with the initial state set to Operational to represent normal, fully functional operation, and a terminal Failed state to represent complete loss of pump pressure delivery capability. The system shall define an internal error event named HydraulicError as the only trigger for state transition. When the pump is in the Operational state, occurrence of the HydraulicError event shall trigger an unconditional, zero-added-delay transition directly to the Failed state, with no intermediate processing states or transition guard conditions. The system shall enforce state-aligned output propagation rules at all times: when operating in the Operational state, the pressure_output interface shall continuously propagate the NoError status without service interruption or data corruption; when operating in the Failed state, the pressure_output interface shall continuously propagate the NoService status to indicate total loss of pressure delivery capability. Safety property constraints shall be applied to the HydraulicError event in compliance with ARP4761 requirements, with the hazard cross-reference mapped to ARP4761 page 275 figure L9, the failure scenario defined as hydraulic error occurring on a pump, applicable flight and operational phases marked as to be determined, failure effect described as loss of one pump unit, failure condition classification set to the Major hazard level, qualitative probability objective set to Probable, and supplementary annotation specifying that concurrent loss of both pump units constitutes a Major hazard. The error occurrence distribution for the HydraulicError event and the propagated NoService error on the pressure_output interface shall follow a Poisson distribution with a fixed probability value of 2.5e-5, per EMV2 occurrence property specifications.

The pump package shall not redefine, modify, or extend the pressure bus type and associated protocol used for the pressure_output interface, and shall fully reuse the pre-defined bus specification for the pressure.i instance imported from the common package. The pump system shall hold provider-level access permission to the connected pressure bus, granting it authority to drive bus state and transmit both normal service data and error status to all components connected as bus subscribers. No custom data type definitions shall be declared within the pump package, as all interface data formats and bus protocol specifications are sourced from imported external shared packages. The error behavior model for the pump system shall import all required error state types and the base simple error behavior rule set from the referenced error_library, with no local custom error type definitions or core behavior rule redefinitions beyond the specified HydraulicError event, associated state transitions, and propagation mappings.

The top-level modeling namespace is defined as the valves public package, which declares explicit import dependencies on two external supporting packages: the base_types package containing core primitive data type definitions, and the common package containing shared communication bus interface and structured command data type definitions. All component definitions within the valves package are contained in the public package section to support unqualified external reference. The package defines a hierarchy of system component types structured through type extension to maximize reuse of common valve and selector functionality, paired with corresponding implementation definitions for instantiable component types. The root generic system type forms the base abstraction for all inline pressure path valve components, with three directly extended subtypes: the generic_pwm_input system type that adds PWM control input capability, the boolean_shutoff system type that adds binary boolean shutoff control input, and the cmd_shutoff system type that adds structured skid command input for command-driven shutoff operation. A separate root selector system type forms the base abstraction for multi-source pressure selection components, with two directly extended subtypes: the selector_basic system type that provides a single combined selected pressure output, and the selector_detailed system type that provides independent split pressure outputs for dual channel distribution. Instantiable system types are paired with empty implementation definitions suffixed with .i, including generic.i, generic_pwm_input.i, and selector.i, with no internal subcomponents, connections, or private behavior defined for these implementations at the current abstraction level.

The base generic valve system type defines two bus access interfaces aligned with pressure signal transfer: a required bus access port named input for connection to upstream pressure supply via the common::pressure.i bus interface, and a provided bus access port named output for connection to downstream pressure consumers via the common::pressure.i bus interface. Error propagation semantics for the generic valve, defined using the error type set from the shared error_library and the standard simple error behavior model from that library, define that the input port accepts incoming NoService error propagations, the output port transmits outgoing NoService error propagations, and a direct error flow path maps NoService errors received at the input port to immediate propagation out of the output port. The generic_pwm_input system type inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the generic base type, and adds one additional required bus access port named input_pwm for connection to PWM control sources via the common::pwm.generic bus interface, with no additional error propagation rules defined for this added interface at the type level. The boolean_shutoff system type inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the generic base type, and adds one additional incoming data port named boolean_input that carries Base_Types::Boolean values for binary shutoff control, with no additional error propagation rules defined for this added interface at the type level. The cmd_shutoff system type inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the generic base type, and adds one additional incoming data port named cmd_input that carries common::command.skid values for skid command-driven shutoff control. Error propagation rules for cmd_shutoff, defined using the error type set from the shared error_library and the standard simple error behavior model from that library, define that the cmd_input port accepts incoming NoValue error propagations, with two dedicated error flow paths: one path maps NoValue errors received at cmd_input to NoService error propagation out of the output port, and a second path defines an internal error source capable of generating NoService errors directly on the output port. The error behavior state machine for cmd_shutoff defines two failure transitions from the initial Operational state: a transition to the Failed state triggered by reception of a NoValue error on the cmd_input port, and a transition to the Failed state triggered by reception of a NoService error on the inherited input pressure port. When operating in the Failed state, the cmd_shutoff component unconditionally propagates a NoService error out of the inherited output pressure port. The base selector system type defines three required bus access ports for incoming pressure supply connections, all interfacing to the common::pressure.i bus: accumulator_input for connection to the accumulator pressure source, green_input for connection to the green system pressure source, blue_input for connection to the blue system pressure source. The base selector also defines three incoming data ports for control input: select_alternate carrying Base_Types::Boolean values to trigger alternate source selection, cmd_nor carrying common::command.skid values for normal operating mode commands, and cmd_alt carrying common::command.skid values for alternate operating mode commands. Error propagation rules for the base selector, defined using the error type set from the shared error_library, define that all three pressure input ports accept incoming NoService error propagations, and all three control data ports accept incoming NoValue error propagations. Three error sink flows are defined for the base selector, which terminate NoValue errors received on the cmd_nor, cmd_alt, and select_alternate ports within the component without direct propagation to other interfaces at the base type level. The selector_basic system type inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base selector type, and adds one provided bus access port named output for connection to downstream consumers via the common::pressure.i bus interface. Additional error propagation rules for selector_basic, defined using the error type set from the shared error_library, define that the output port transmits outgoing NoService error propagations, with three direct error flow paths mapping NoService errors received on the green_input, blue_input, and accumulator_input ports respectively to NoService error propagation out of the output port. The selector_detailed system type inherits all interfaces and error propagation rules from the base selector type, and adds two provided bus access ports for dual channel pressure delivery, both interfacing to the common::pressure.i bus: green_output for the green distribution channel, and blue_output for the blue distribution channel. Additional error propagation rules for selector_detailed, defined using the error type set from the shared error_library and the standard simple error behavior model from that library, define that both green_output and blue_output ports transmit outgoing NoService error propagations, supported by eight dedicated error flow paths: NoService errors received on green_input propagate to green_output, NoService errors received on blue_input propagate to blue_output, NoService errors received on accumulator_input propagate to both green_output and blue_output, NoValue errors received on cmd_alt propagate as NoService errors out of blue_output, NoValue errors received on cmd_nor propagate as NoService errors out of green_output, and NoValue errors received on select_alternate propagate as NoService errors out of both green_output and blue_output. The error behavior state machine for selector_detailed defines three failure transitions from the initial Operational state: a transition to the Failed state triggered by reception of a NoValue error on the select_alternate port, a transition to the Failed state triggered by reception of a NoValue error on the cmd_alt port, and a transition to the Failed state triggered by reception of a NoValue error on the cmd_nor port. When operating in the Failed state, the selector_detailed component unconditionally propagates NoService errors out of both the green_output and blue_output ports.

Functional data flow across all valve components derived from the generic base type follows a core path that transfers pressure signaling from the upstream required input pressure bus access to the downstream provided output pressure bus access, with flow modulation applied via component-specific control inputs. For the generic_pwm_input valve variant, PWM control signals received via the input_pwm bus access are used to modulate the magnitude of pressure passed from the input to output pressure path. For the boolean_shutoff valve variant, binary state values received via the boolean_input data port are used to toggle between fully open pressure passage and fully closed pressure shutoff between the input and output pressure ports. For the cmd_shutoff valve variant, structured skid command values received via the cmd_input data port are used to control pressure passage or shutoff between the input and output pressure ports, with a defined fail-safe state that fully blocks pressure delivery to the output port when valid command input is lost or valid incoming pressure supply is lost. Functional data flow across all selector components follows a core path that routes pressure from one or more of the three incoming pressure supply inputs to component outputs, with source selection determined by the state of received control inputs. For the selector_basic variant, pressure from the selected source, chosen based on the boolean state of the select_alternate input and the content of received cmd_nor and cmd_alt skid commands, is routed to the single output pressure port as a unified supply with no split between separate distribution channels. For the selector_detailed variant, pressure from selected sources is routed independently to the two output channels: the green_output path is supplied by the green_input and accumulator pressure sources, with gating control applied via the cmd_nor input, and the blue_output path is supplied by the blue_input and accumulator pressure sources, with gating control applied via the cmd_alt input, while cross-channel source switching is triggered by the state of the select_alternate control signal. Error flows across all components with defined error behavior follow predefined propagation paths separate from functional flow, where lost service on pressure inputs or lost value on control inputs triggers predefined error propagation to downstream interfaces or component failure state transitions as specified per component type.

At the current abstraction level, no explicit scheduling rules, execution time budgets, deadline constraints, or end-to-end latency limits are defined for any component within the valves package. All components are modeled as system-level abstractions without decomposition into executable thread or process subcomponents, so no periodic or aperiodic dispatch rules, priority assignments, or processor binding requirements are specified. Error propagation and state transition behavior is defined as logically immediate, with no specified time delay between error reception, state transition execution, and error propagation to downstream interfaces. No clock synchronization or time-triggered communication requirements are defined for bus or data port interactions.

All communication bus interfaces referenced by components in the valves package are imported from the external common package, with strict type matching enforced for all bus access connections. The common::pressure.i bus type is designated for all pressure signal transfer paths, used exclusively for connections between upstream pressure sources, valve components, selector components, and downstream pressure consumers. The common::pwm.generic bus type is designated for PWM control signal transfer, used exclusively for connections between PWM control sources and the input_pwm port of the generic_pwm_input valve variant. Bus access direction follows a consistent rule: required bus access ports are used for all incoming bus connections, where the component acts as a bus access requester connecting to an upstream bus provider, and provided bus access ports are used for all outgoing bus connections, where the component acts as a bus provider for downstream connected components. All data port values use types imported from external packages, with strict type matching enforced for all data port connections. The Base_Types::Boolean primitive data type is designated for binary state control signals, used for both the boolean shutoff input on boolean_shutoff valves and the alternate selection input on selector components. The common::command.skid structured data type is designated for skid control command signals, used for both the command input on cmd_shutoff valves and the normal and alternate command inputs on selector components. All data ports are defined as unidirectional incoming ports, with no outgoing data ports specified on any valve or selector component at the current abstraction level. Error type definitions for components with specified error behavior are imported from the external error_library, with components that include state-based failure logic utilizing the predefined simple error behavior model that defines Operational and Failed component states. Two standard error tokens are used across applicable components: the NoService error token, which indicates loss of valid pressure signal transfer and is only propagated across pressure bus interfaces with explicitly defined error propagation rules, and the NoValue error token, which indicates loss of valid data content and is only propagated across control data ports with explicitly defined error propagation rules. Defined error mapping rules specify that incoming NoValue errors on control ports with defined error propagation may trigger component failure and subsequent outgoing NoService errors on pressure output ports, with no reverse mapping of NoService errors on pressure ports to NoValue errors on control ports defined for any component.

The top-level system model is contained within a package named wbs, which shall declare explicit import dependencies on supporting packages including bscu, communication, valves, wheel, pump, power, pedals, ARP4761, and EMV2 to access pre-defined component types, safety property sets, and error modeling constructs. The wbs package defines a root system type named wbs with no externally exposed ports or bus access points at the system boundary, and four hierarchical system implementations tied to the wbs type through an inheritance structure. The base implementation wbs.generic defines the common set of subcomponents and core connections shared across all wbs configuration variants. Three specialized implementations extend wbs.generic to support different levels of model fidelity and architecture patterns: wbs.basic provides a high-level abstracted view of hydraulic valving logic, wbs.detailed provides a fine-grained representation of the full hydraulic circuit, wbs.federated extends wbs.detailed to implement a federated avionics architecture for the brake control function, and wbs.ima extends wbs.detailed to implement an integrated modular avionics architecture for the brake control function with attached formal verification claims. The common subcomponents defined in wbs.generic include a pedal input subsystem of type pedals::pedals.generic, an electrical power distribution subsystem of type power::power.generic, three hydraulic pump components of type pump::pump.i designated blue_pump, green_pump, and accumulator respectively, a hydraulic selector valve assembly, a brake system control unit, a wheel brake assembly, and a crew annunciation device of type communication::annunciation.i.
